body.translated_text: (1) When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvaśūra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Here, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) is the most difficult practice.' (2) 'For what reason? Rare, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the conduct of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; just so, rare is the holy life. (3) When one practices the holy life, then one will see the <s>Tathāgata</s> face to face, and day and night the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s> will occur. (4) When one sees the <s>Tathāgata</s>, one sees the <s>Buddha</s>-field. (5) When one sees the <s>Buddha</s>-field, one sees all the treasuries of <s>dharmas</s>. (6) When one sees all the treasuries of <s>dharmas</s>, then <s>Māra</s>...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 80
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 80

body.text: 1. evam ukte bhagavān sarvaśūraṃ bodhisatvaṃ mahāsatvam etad avocat: durlabhaḥ sarvaśūra tathāgatānām utpādaḥ? 2. āha: durlabho bhagavan durlabhaḥ sugata! 3. bhagavān āha: evam eva sarvaśūra durlabho 'yaṃ saṃghāto dharmaparyāyaḥ. 4. yeṣāṃ khalu punaḥ sarvaśūrāyaṃ saṃghāṭo dharmaparyāyaḥ śrotrāvabhāsam āgamiṣyati, so 'śīti kalpāṃ jātyā jātismaro bhaviṣyati; 5. ṣaṣṭi kalpasahasrāṇi cakravartirājyaṃ pratilapsyate; 6. aṣṭau kalpasahasrāṇi śakratvaṃ pratilapsyate; 7. paṃcaviṃśatiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi śuddhāvāsakāyikānān devānāṃ sahabhāvyatāyām upapatsyate; 8. aṣṭātṛṃśat kalpasahasrāṇi mahābrahmā bhaviṣyati;
body.translated_text: (1) When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvaśūra</s>: 'Is the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s> rare, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>?' (2) He said: 'Rare, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, rare, O <s>Sugata</s>!' (3) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharmaparyāya</s> is rare. (4) Those, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, whose ears this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharmaparyāya</s> shall illumine — they shall remember their past lives for eighty <s>kalpas</s>, birth after birth. (5) For sixty thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall obtain <s>Cakravartin</s> kingship. (6) For eight thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall obtain the sovereignty of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>). (7) For twenty-five <s>kalpas</s>...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 81
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 81

body.text: 1. navānavatiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati; 2. kalpaśatasahasraṃ preteṣu nopapatsyate; 3. aṣṭāviṃśati kalpasahasrāṇi tiryakṣur nopapatsyate; 4. trayodaśa kalpasahasrāṇy asurakāyikeṣu nopapatsyate; 5. na śastreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyati, na viṣeṇa, nāgninā; 6. na cāsya paropakramabhayaṃ bhaviṣyati;
body.translated_text: (1) 'For ninety-nine thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not fall into the lower realms. (2) For a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn among the hungry ghosts (<s>pretas</s>). (3) For twenty-eight thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn as animals. (4) For thirteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn among the <s>Asura</s> hosts. (5) They shall not die by weapons, nor by poison, nor by fire. (6) And they shall have no fear of harm from others.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 82
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 82

body.text: 1. paṃcaviṃśatiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi na duṣprajño bhaviṣyati; 2. sapta kalpasahasrāṇi prajñācarito bhaviṣyati; 3. nava kalpasahasrāṇi prāsādiko bhaviṣyati, darśanīyaḥ; yathā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyarūpakāyapariniṣpattis tathā tasya bhaviṣyati; 4. paṃcadaśa kalpasahasrāṇi na strībhāveṣūpapatsyate; 5. ṣoḍaśa kalpasahasrāṇi vyādhiḥ kāye nākramiṣyati; 6. paṃcatṛṃśat kalpasahasrāṇi divyacakṣur bhaviṣyati;
body.translated_text: (1) 'For twenty-five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be of poor wisdom. (2) For seven thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall be of wisdom-conduct. (3) For nine thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall be attractive and beautiful to behold; just as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Fully Awakened One has the perfection of the form-body, so shall theirs be. (4) For fifteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn in female form. (5) For sixteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> no disease shall afflict their bodies. (6) For thirty-five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall possess the divine eye.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 83
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 83

body.text: 1. ekonaviṃśat kalpasahasrāṇi nāgayoniṣu nopapatsyate; 2. ṣaṭ kalpasahasrāṇi na krodhābhibhūto bhaviṣyati; 3. sapta kalpasahasrāṇi daridrakuleṣu nopapatsyate; 4. aśītiḥ kalpasahasrāṇi dvau dvīpau paribhuṃkte; 5. yadā daridro bhavati tadā īdṛśaṃ sukhaṃ pratilapsyate: 6. dvādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi andhayoniṣu nopapatsyate; 7. trayodaśa kalpasahasrāṇi apāyeṣu nopapatsyate; 8. ekādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi kṣāntivādī bhaviṣyati; 9. maraṇakālasamaye carimavijñānanirodhe vartamāne, na viparītasaṃjñī bhaviṣyati; 10. na ca krodhābhibhūto bhaviṣyati;
body.translated_text: (1) 'For nineteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn in <s>Nāga</s> (serpent) wombs. (2) For six thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be overcome by anger. (3) For seven thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn in destitute families. (4) For eighty thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall enjoy two continents. (5) When they become poor, they shall obtain such happiness [as this]: (6) For twelve thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn in blind wombs. (7) For thirteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall not be reborn in the lower realms (<s>apāyas</s>). (8) For eleven thousand <s>kalpas</s> they shall be speakers of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>). (9) At the time of death, when the final consciousness is ceasing, they shall not have distorted perceptions...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 84
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 84

body.text: 1. sa pūrvasyān diśi dvādaśagaṃgānadībālikāsamān buddhān bhagavataḥ saṃmukhan drakṣyati; 2. dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi viṃśati buddhakoṭī saṃmukhan drakṣyati; 3. paścimasyān diśi paṃcaviṃśatigaṃgānadībālikāsamān buddhān bhagavataḥ saṃmukhaṃ drakṣyati; 4. uttarasyān diśi viṃśatigaṃgānadībālikāsamān buddhāṃ bhagavataḥ saṃmukhaṃ drakṣyati; 5. ūrdhvāyāṃ diśi navati koṭīsahasrāṇi buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ saṃmukhaṃ drakṣyati; 6. adhastāddiśi koṭīśataṃ gaṃgānadībālikāsamān buddhān bhagavataḥ saṃmukhan drakṣyati;
body.translated_text: (1) 'In the eastern direction they shall see face to face <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> equal in number to twelve times the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River. (2) In the southern direction they shall see face to face twenty <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Buddhas</s>. (3) In the western direction they shall see face to face <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> equal in number to twenty-five times the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. (4) In the northern direction they shall see face to face <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> equal in number to twenty times the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. (5) In the upward direction they shall see face to face ninety thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>. (6) In the downward direction they shall see face to face <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> equal in number to a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 85
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 85

body.text: 1. te ca sarve tathāgatās taṃ kulaputram āśvāsayanti: mā bhaiḥ kulaputra, tava, saṃghāṭaṃ sūtran dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā, iyantaḥ sāṃparāyikāni guṇāni sukhāni ca bhaviṣyanti! 2. paśyasi tvaṃ bhoḥ kulaputremāny anekāni gaṃgānadībālikāsamāni tathāgatakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi? 3. āha: paśyāmi bhagavan paśyāmi sugata. 4. bhagavān āha: ete bhoḥ kulaputra tathāgatās tava sakāśam upasaṃkrāntā darśanāya.
body.translated_text: (1) And all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> comforted that son of good family: 'Do not fear, O son of good family! Having heard the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>, this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), you will have this many future virtues and happinesses! (2) Do you see, O good sir, these many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River?' (3) He said: 'I see them, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I see them, O <s>Sugata</s>.' (4) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'These <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O good sir, have come into your presence for the purpose of seeing you.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 86
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 86

body.text: 1. āha: śṛṇu kulaputra, tvayā mānuṣyakam ātmabhāvaṃ pratilabhya saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrotrāvabhāsam āgataṃ; tena tvayā etāvat puṇyaskandhaṃ prasūtaṃ. 2. āha: yadi mama bhagavann etāvān puṇyaskandhaḥ, kaḥ punar vādo yaḥ sakalasamāptaṃ śroṣyati!
body.translated_text: (1) He said: 'Listen, O son of good family. Having obtained a human form, the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> has come within the range of your hearing; by that, you have produced this great heap of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>).' (2) He said: 'If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, such a great heap of merit is mine, what then need be said of one who will hear it in its entirety!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 87
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 87

body.text: 1. āhā: alam bhoḥ kulaputra! catuṣpadikāyā gāthāyāḥ śrutāyāḥ puṇyaṃ varṇayāmi. 2. tadyathā kulaputra, trayodaśagaṃgānadībālikāsamānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ yaḥ puṇyaskandhas, tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati yaś catuṣpadikām api gāthām ito dharmaparyāyāc chroṣyati; 3. yaś ca trayodaśagaṃgānadībālikāsamāṃs tathāgatān arhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān pūjayati, yaś cetaḥ saṃghāṭād dharmaparyāyād antaśaś catuṣpādikām api gāthāṃ śroṣyati, ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati. 4. kaḥ punar vādo yaḥ sakalasamāptaṃ śroṣyati!
body.translated_text: (1) He said: 'Enough, O good sir! I shall describe the merit of having heard [even] a four-line verse (<s>catuṣpadikā gāthā</s>). (2) Suppose, O son of good family, there were thirteen <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones, equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River — whatever their heap of merit, one who will hear even a four-line verse from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> produces a greater heap of merit than that. (3) And whoever worships thirteen <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and whoever will hear even a four-line verse from this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> — this one will produce a greater heap of merit than that. (4) What then need be said of one who will hear it in its entirety!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 88
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 88

body.text: 1. śṛṇu kulaputra, yaś cemaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ sūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sakalasamāptaṃ śroṣyati tasya kiyantaṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati. 2. tadyathāpināma kaścid eva puruṣaḥ eva puruṣaḥ sarvasyāṃ tṛsāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau tilaṃ vāpayed; yāvantas te tilaphalakās tāvanto rājānaś cakravartino bhaveyur; atha kaścid eva puruṣo bhaved āḍhayo mahābhogaḥ; 3. atha khalu sa puruṣas teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ rājñāṃ cakravartināṃ dānan dadyāt; yaś caikasya srotaāpannasya dānam dadyād, ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Listen, O son of good family: whoever will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> in its entirety — how great a heap of merit will he produce? (2) Suppose some man were to sow sesame seeds throughout the entire <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> (billion-fold) world-system; as many sesame plants as there would be, that many <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) kings there would be; and suppose some man were wealthy, of great possessions. (3) Then suppose that man were to give gifts to all those <s>cakravartin</s> kings; and [suppose another] were to give a gift to a single <s>Srotaāpanna</s> (Stream-enterer) — this one produces a greater heap of merit than that.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 89
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 89

body.text: 1. ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau satvās te sarve srotaāpanā bhaveyus, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yat puṇyaskandhaṃ, ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati ya ekasya sakṛdāgāmino dānan dadyād. 2. ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau satvās te sarve sakṛdāgāmino bhaveyuḥ, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ, ayan tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati ya ekasyānāgāmino dānān dadyād. 3. ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau satvās te sarve 'nāgāmino bhaveyuḥ, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yaḥ puṇyaskandhaṃ, ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati ya ekasyārhato dānan dadyād. 4. ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau satvās te sarve 'rhanto bhaveyuḥ, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ, ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati ya ekasya pratyekabuddhasya dānan dadyād. 5. ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau satvās te sarve pratyekabuddhā bhaveyus, teṣān sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati ya ekasya bodhisatvasya dānan dadyād. 6. ye trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau satvās te sarve bodhisatvā bhaveyus, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ dānan dadato yaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ, ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati ya ekasya tathāgatasya cittaṃ prasādayed.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Were all the beings in the <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> world-system to become <s>Srotaāpannas</s>, the heap of merit from giving gifts to all of them — this one produces a greater heap of merit who would give a gift to a single <s>Sakṛdāgāmin</s> (Once-returner). (2) Were all the beings in the <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> world-system to become <s>Sakṛdāgāmins</s>, the heap of merit from giving gifts to all of them — this one produces a greater heap of merit who would give a gift to a single <s>Anāgāmin</s> (Non-returner). (3) Were all the beings in the <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> world-system to become <s>Anāgāmins</s>, the heap of merit from giving gifts to all of them — this one produces a greater heap of merit who would give a gift to a single <s>Arhat</s>. (4) Were all the beings in the <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> world-system to become <s>Arhats</s>, the heap of merit from giving gifts to all of them — this one produces a greater heap of merit who would give a gift to a single <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. (5) Were all the beings in the <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> world-system to become <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, the heap of merit from giving gifts to all of them — this one produces a greater heap of merit who would give a gift to a single <s>Bodhisattva</s>. (6) Were all the beings in the <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> world-system to become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the heap of merit from giving gifts to all of them — this one produces a greater heap of merit who would generate faith (<s>cittaprasāda</s>) in the mind of a single <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 90
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 90

body.text: 1. yaś ca trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau tathāgataparipūrṇāyāṃ cittaṃ prasādayed, ayam eva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati ya imaṃ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyati. 2. kaḥ punar vādaḥ sarvaśūra ya iman dharmaparyāyaṃ likhiṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati. 3. kaḥ punar vādaḥ sarvaśūra ya imaṃ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ cittaprasādena namaskariṣyati.
body.translated_text: (1) 'And whoever would generate faith in [<s>Tathāgatas</s>] filling the <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> world-system — this very one will produce a greater heap of merit who will hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. (2) What then need be said, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, of one who will copy, preserve, recite, or master this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>? (3) What then need be said, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, of one who will pay homage to this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> with a faithful mind (<s>cittaprasāda</s>)?'

body.text: SaSū(C) 91
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 91

body.text: 1. tat kiṃ manyase sarvaśūra? śakyam idaṃ sūtraṃ bālapṛthagjanaiḥ śrotuṃ? 2. ye ca śroṣyanti na ca prasādam utpādayiṣyanti. 3. śṛṇu sarvaśūra, santi kecit sarvaśūra bālapṛthagjanāḥ satvāḥ ye śaknuyur mahāsamudre gādhaṃ labdhum? 4. āha: no hīdaṃ bhagavan!
body.translated_text: (1) 'What do you think, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>? Is it possible for this sūtra to be heard by foolish ordinary beings (<s>bāla-pṛthagjana</s>)? (2) Those who will hear it but will not generate faith — (3) listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, are there any foolish ordinary beings who could find a foothold in the great ocean?' (4) He said: 'No indeed, O <s>Bhagavān</s>!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 92
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 92

body.text: 1. bhagavān āha: asti punaḥ sarvaśūra kaścit satvo ya ekapāṇitalena samudraṃ kṣapayed? 2. āha: no hīdaṃ bhagavan, no hīdaṃ sugata! 3. bhagavān āha: yathā sarvaśūra nāsti sa kaścit satvo yaḥ śaknuyād ekapāṇitalena mahāsamudraṃ śoṣayituṃ, evam eva sarvaśūra ye hīnādhimuktikāḥ satvāḥ na śakyaṃ tair ayan dharmaparyāyaḥ śrotuṃ. 4. yaiḥ sarvaśūrāśītir gaṃgānadībālikāsamāni tathāgatakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi na dṛṣṭāni, na taiḥ śakyam ayaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ likhituṃ. 5. yair navatigaṃgānadībālikāsamāni tathāgatāni na dṛṣṭāni, na taiḥ śakyam ayan dharmaparyāyaḥ śrotum.
body.translated_text: (1) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is there furthermore, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, any being who could drain the ocean with a single palm-stroke?' (2) He said: 'No indeed, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! No indeed, O <s>Sugata</s>!' (3) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Just as, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, there is no being who could dry up the great ocean with a single palm-stroke, just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, beings of inferior aspiration (<s>hīnādhimuktika</s>) cannot hear this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. (4) Those, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who have not seen eighty <s>koṭī-nayuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — they cannot copy this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. (5) Those who have not seen ninety <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — they cannot hear this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 93
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 93

body.text: yena tathāgatakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi na dṛṣṭāni, ta iman dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā pratikṣipanti. 2. yaiḥ sarvaśūragaṃgānadībālikāsamānitathāgatakoṭīśatāni dṛṣṭāni, ta iman dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā prasādacittam utpādayanti, harṣayanti, yathābhūtaṃ prajānanti. 3. ya imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ yathābhūtaṃ śraddadhanti na pratikṣipanti.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Those who have not seen hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s> — having heard this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, they reject it. (2) Those, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who have seen hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — having heard this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, they generate a faithful mind, they rejoice, they understand it as it truly is. (3) Those who truly believe this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> and do not reject it.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 94
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 94

body.text: 1. śṛṇu sarvaśūra, ye kecid asmāt saṃghāṭād dharmaparyāyād ekām api catuṣpadikāṃ gāthāṃ likhiṣyanti teṣāṃ sarvaśūra satvānāṃ, tataḥ paścāt paṃcanavati koṭīsahasrāni lokadhātūnām atikramya yathā sukhāvatīlokadhātus, tathā teṣāṃ buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati; 2. teṣāṃ ca sarvaśūra satvānāṃ caturaśītiḥ kalpasahasrāṇy āyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: all those beings who will copy even a single four-line verse from this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> — for those beings, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, having passed beyond ninety-five thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of world-systems, just as the world-system <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Land of Bliss) is, so will their <s>Buddha</s>-field be. (2) And the lifespan of those beings, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, will be eighty-four thousand <s>kalpas</s> (aeons).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 95
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 95

body.text: 1. śṛṇu sarvaśūra, ye bodhisatvā mahāsatvā asmāt saṃghāṭād dharmaparyāyād antaśaś catuṣpadikām api gāthāṃ śroṣyanti. 2. tadyathā sarvaśūra kaścit satvo bhaved yaḥ paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kuryāt, kārayed vā, kriyamāṇāni vānumodet, sa itaḥ saṃghāṭād dharmaparyāyāc catuṣpadikām api gāthāṃ śṛṇuyāt, tasya tāni paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuḥ.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who will hear even a four-line verse from this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> — (2) suppose, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, there were a being who would commit the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) <s>karmas</s> (deeds), or cause them to be committed, or rejoice in their being committed — if he were to hear even a four-line verse from this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, those five <s>ānantarya karmas</s> of his would be completely exhausted.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 96
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 96

body.text:
1. śṛṇu sarvaśūra, punar aparaṃ guṇam āmantrayāmi: 2. tadyathāpināma kaścit satvo bhaved yaḥ stūpabhedaṃ kārayet, saṃghabhedaṃ ca, 3. bodhisatvaṃ samādher uccālayet, 4. buddhajñānasyāntarāyaṃ kuryāt, 5. mātāpitaraṃ jīvitād vyavaropayed
6. atha sa satvaḥ paścāt paridevati, śocati: naṣṭo 'ham anena kāyena, naṣṭaṃ me paralokam iti, kalpam evāhaṃ naṣṭaḥ. 7. tato 'sya mahācintāyāsaṃ bhaveta, duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayeta, kaṭukāṃ vedanāṃ vedayeta; 8. tasya sarvaśūra satvasya sarvasatvāḥ parivarjayanti, jugupsanti ca: 9. dagdho naṣṭa eṣa satva, laukikalokottarād dharmā naṣṭo 'nekāni kalpāni, yathā dagdhasthūṇā.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, I will further declare another virtue: (2) suppose there were a being who caused the breaking of a <s>stūpa</s>, and a schism in the <s>Saṅgha</s>, (3) and who dislodged a <s>Bodhisattva</s> from <s>samādhi</s> (meditation), (4) and who obstructed the knowledge of a <s>Buddha</s>, (5) and who killed his mother and father. (6) Then that being later laments and grieves: "I am lost with this body; my next world is lost; I am lost for an entire <s>kalpa</s>." (7) Then great anxiety and distress would arise in him; he would feel painful sensations, bitter sensations. (8) All beings, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, shun and abhor that being: (9) "This being is burnt, is lost — lost from both worldly and supramundane <s>dharmas</s> for many <s>kalpas</s>, like a burnt pillar."'

body.text: SaSū(C) 97

1. evam evāyaṃ puruṣaḥ: yathā sucitraṃ gṛhaṃ dagdhasthūṇaṃ na śobhate, evam evāyaṃ sa puruṣa iha loke na śobhate; 2. yatra yatra ca gacchati tatra tatra satvaiḥ paribhāṣyate, praharanti ca; 3. kṣutpipāsārdito 'pi na kiṃcil labhate; 4. tato duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayati.
body.translated_text: 1. In just this way, this man — just as a well-adorned house with burnt pillars is not beautiful, so too this man is not beautiful in this world. 2. Wherever he goes, he is reviled and struck by beings. 3. Though tormented by hunger and thirst, he obtains nothing. 4. Therefore he experiences painful sensation.

body.text: SaSū(C) 98
1. sa kṣutpipāsāhetunāparibhāṣāhetunāprahārahetunā, stūpabhedaṃ ca, paṃcānantaryāṇi ca karmāṇi samanusmarati; 2. sa tato duḥkhān nirvedacittam utpādayati: kutrāhaṃ yāsyāmi, ko me trāta bhavisyati?
body.translated_text: 1. Because of hunger and thirst, because of being reviled, because of being struck, he recalls the destruction of the <s>stūpa</s> and the five heinous deeds (<s>pañcānantarya</s>). 2. From that, in suffering, he generates a mind of disenchantment: 'Where shall I go? Who will be my protector?'

body.text: SaSū(C) 99
1. sa evaṃ cintayati: gamiṣyāmy ahaṃ parvatagirikandareṣu, praviśāmi, tatra me kālakriyā bhaviṣyati, na ca me iha kaścit trātāsti. āha ca:
body.translated_text: 1. He thinks thus: 'I shall go to the mountain caves and gorges and enter there; there my death will come, and there is no protector for me here.' And he spoke:

children.text: (1) kṛtaṃ me pāpakaṃ karma dagdhasthūṇaṃ nirantaram /
children.translated_text: (1) I have done evil <s>karma</s> — [my pillar is] burnt, ceaselessly;

children.text: nemaṃ loke śobhayiṣye na śobhayiṣyāmi paratra ca /
children.translated_text: I will not be beautiful in this world, nor will I be beautiful in the next;

children.text: antargṛhe na śobhāmi na śobhāmi ca bāhire //
children.translated_text: I am not beautiful inside the house, nor am I beautiful outside.

children.text: (2) doṣahetoḥ kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tena yāsyāmi durgatim /
children.translated_text: (2) Because of faults, I have done evil — by that I shall go to a bad rebirth;

children.text: paratra duḥkhitaḥ kutra vasiṣyāmi ha durgatau //
children.translated_text: suffering in the next world, where shall I dwell in that bad destiny?

children.text: (3) śṛṇvanti devatā vācam aśrukaṇṭhaṃ prarodati /
children.translated_text: (3) The deities hear [his] words as he cries out with tears in his throat:

children.text: nirāśaḥ paraloke prayāsyāmīha durgatiṃ //
children.translated_text: 'Without hope, I shall depart from this world to a bad rebirth.'

body.text: 2. taṃ devatā āhuḥ:
body.translated_text: 2. The deities said to him:

children.text: (4) mūḍho 'si gaccha puruṣa maivaṃ cintaya duḥkhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: (4) 'You are deluded — go, O man! Do not think thus in your suffering!

children.text: śaraṇo na ca me trāṇaṃ duḥkhāṃ vindāmi vedanām //
children.translated_text: [He replies:] 'I have no refuge, no protection — I experience painful sensation!

children.text: (5) mātṛghāṭaṃ pitṛghāṭaṃ paṃcānantaryāñ ca me kṛtam /
children.translated_text: (5) I have committed matricide, patricide, and the five heinous deeds;

children.text: parvate mūrdhni gacchāmi tata ātmāṃ tyajāmy aham //
children.translated_text: I shall go to the mountain summit and from there I shall cast myself down.'

children.text: (6) mā gaccha mūḍhapuruṣa karma mā kuru pāpakaṃ /
children.translated_text: (6) [The deities reply:] 'Do not go, O deluded man! Do not perform evil <s>karma</s>!

children.text: bahu tvayā kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ vyāpannena hi cetasā //
children.translated_text: Much evil has been done by you, with a corrupted mind.

children.text: (7) kurvanti ye ātmaghātaṃ narakaṃ yānti duḥkhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: (7) Those who commit self-destruction go to hell, suffering;

children.text: tataḥ patanti bhūmīṣu krandanti śokavedanāḥ //
children.translated_text: from there they fall into [further] realms, crying out in sorrow and pain.

body.text: (8) na tena vīryeṇa bhavanti buddhā bhavanti naivāpi ca bodhisatvā //
body.translated_text: (8) By such effort (<s>vīrya</s>) neither Buddhas nor <s>bodhisattvas</s> come to be;

body.text: na śrāvakaṃ labhyati mokṣayānam anyasya vīryasya kuruṣva yatnam //
body.translated_text: nor is the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle of liberation attained — strive for a different kind of effort!

children.text: (9) gacchasva taṃ parvatu yena so ṛṣi gatvā ca taṃ dṛṣṭva ṛṣiṃ mahātmā /
children.translated_text: (9) Go to that mountain where that sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>) is; having gone and seen that great-souled sage,

children.text: vanditva pādau śirasā ca tasya trāṇaṃ bhavāhī mama agrasatva //
children.translated_text: bow with your head at his feet [and say]: "Be my protector, O foremost being!

children.text: (10) deśehi dharmaṃ kuśalaṃ muhūrttam bhīto 'smi trasto atiduḥkhapīḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: (10) Teach the virtuous <s>Dharma</s> for a moment! I am frightened, terrified, afflicted by great suffering."'

children.text: ṛṣir vadantaṃ śṛṇu satvasāra niṣadya cittasya kṣaṇaṃ kuruṣva //
children.translated_text: [The sage speaks:] 'O essence of beings, listen to what the sage says; sit down and compose your mind for a moment.'

children.text: (11) bhītaḥ sa trasto atiduḥkhapīḍitas tato niṣaṇṇaḥ kṣaṇiko muhūrtam /
children.translated_text: (11) Frightened, terrified, afflicted by great suffering, he sat down there, momentarily, for a moment:

children.text: deśemi pāpaṃ kṛta yan mayā bahū ṛṣir hi vācam idam abravīti //
children.translated_text: 'I confess the evil that I have done in abundance.' Thus the sage spoke this word:

body.text: 4. ṛṣir āha:
body.translated_text: 4. The sage said:

children.text: (12) bhuṃjāhi taṃ bhojanu yad dadāmi duḥkhena ca krandasi śokapīḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: (12) 'Eat this food that I give you — you cry out in suffering, afflicted by sorrow;

children.text: kṣudhā pipāsāya ca pīḍitas tvaṃ nirāśakaś ca tribhavād bhaviṣyasi //
children.translated_text: you are tormented by hunger and thirst, and you will become free from hope in the three worlds of existence.'

children.text: (13) bhojanāny upanāmitvā ṛṣiḥ satvaṃ prasādayan /
children.translated_text: (13) Having offered food, the sage, gladdening the being [said]:

children.text: mṛṣṭaṃ bhuṃja manāpaṃ ca śarīre tarpaṇārthikaṃ //
children.translated_text: 'Eat this fine and pleasant [food], nourishing for the body.'

children.text: (14) paścāt te dharma bhāṣāmi sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram /
children.translated_text: (14) 'Afterward I shall teach you the <s>Dharma</s> that destroys all evil.'

children.text: tasya tad bhojanaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ muhūrtaṃ bhuktavān asau //
children.translated_text: That one ate the fine food for a moment.

children.text: (15) bhuktvā hastau ca prakṣālya kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ ṛṣiṃ /
children.translated_text: (15) Having eaten and washed his hands, having circumambulated the sage,

children.text: paryaṃkena niṣīditvā vada yat pāpakaṃ kṛtam //
children.translated_text: he sat cross-legged: 'Speak of the evil that was done.'

children.text: (16) mātṛghātaṃ pitṛghātaṃ stūpabhedaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ /
children.translated_text: (16) 'Matricide, patricide, and the destruction of a <s>stūpa</s> were done by me;

children.text: bodhisatvasya buddhatve antarāyaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā //
children.translated_text: I created an obstacle to the Buddhahood of a <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

children.text: (17) tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā ṛṣir vākyam athābravīt /
children.translated_text: (17) Having heard that speech, the sage then spoke these words:

children.text: asādhus tava bho puruṣa yat kṛtaṃ pāpakaṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: 'Not good, O sir, is what evil you have done!

children.text: deśehi pāpakaṃ karma kṛtaṃ kārāpitaṃ ca yat //
children.translated_text: Confess the evil <s>karma</s>, both what was done and what was caused to be done.'

body.text: 5. atha khalu tasmin kāle sa puruṣaḥ śokaśalyasamarpito, bhītas, trasta, udvignaḥ: ko me trātā bhaviṣyati?
body.translated_text: 5. Then at that time, that man, pierced by the arrow of sorrow, frightened, terrified, agitated [thought]: 'Who will be my protector?'

children.text: (18) kṛtaṃ me pāpakaṃ karma duḥkhāṃ vetsyāmi vedanāṃ /
children.translated_text: (18) 'I have done evil <s>karma</s> — I shall experience painful sensation;

children.text: ko me syāt trāyako nātho yo me duḥkhāt pramocayet //
children.translated_text: who will be my savior, my lord, who will free me from suffering?'

body.text: 6. atha khalu sa puruṣas tasya ṛṣer jānudvayaṃ bhūmau nipātyāha ca:
body.translated_text: 6. Then that man, placing both knees on the ground before the sage, spoke:

children.text: (19) deśeyaṃ pāpakaṃ karma yat kṛtaṃ kāritaṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: (19) 'I would confess the evil <s>karma</s> that was done and caused to be done by me;

children.text: mā phalaṃ pāpakaṃ bhotu mā me syād duḥkhavedanā //
children.translated_text: may the evil fruit not ripen! May I not experience painful sensation!

children.text: (20) ṛṣis trāṇaṃ bhaven mahyam āsanno 'haṃ bhaven tava /
children.translated_text: (20) May the sage be my protector! I would be near you;

children.text: niṣkaukṛtyasya śāntasya śamyantāṃ pāpakān mama //
children.translated_text: of one freed from remorse, at peace — may my evil deeds be calmed!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 100

1. atha khalu sa riṣis tena kālena tena samayena taṃ puruṣam etad avocat, evaṃ cāśvāsayati: 2. mā bhaiḥ puruṣa, ahaṃ te trāṇaṃ bhaviṣyāmy, ahan te gatir, ahaṃ parāyaṇaṃ bhaviṣyāmi; 3. saṃmukhaṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇu. śrutaṃ tvayā kiṃcit saṃghāṭaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ? 4. sa āha: na me kadācic chrutaṃ. 5. ṛṣir āha: ko 'gnidagdhasya satvasya dharman deśayaty anyatra yaḥ karuṇāvihāritayā satvānāṃ dharman deśayati? 6. āha: śṛṇu kulaputra,
body.translated_text: 1. Then at that time, the sage spoke to that man, and consoled him thus: 2. 'Do not fear, O man! I shall be your protector; I shall be your refuge, I shall be your final resort. 3. Listen to the <s>Dharma</s> face-to-face. Have you ever heard of a <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s>?' 4. He said: 'I have never heard it.' 5. The sage said: 'Who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to a being burnt by fire, other than one who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings out of compassionate conduct?' 6. He said: 'Listen, son of good family:'

body.text: SaSū(C) 101

1. bhūtapūrvaṃ, asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpair asaṃkhyeyatarair yadāsīt tena kālena tena samayena, vimalacandro nāma rājābhūd, dhārmiko, dharmarājā. 2. tasya khalu punaḥ kulaputra rājño vimalacandrasya gṛhe putro jātaḥ.
body.translated_text: 1. 'In the past, incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) ago, even more incalculable than that, at that time there was a king named <s>Vimalacandra</s> (Pure Moon), righteous, a <s>Dharma</s>-king. 2. And in the house of that King <s>Vimalacandra</s>, a son was born.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 102

1. atha sa rājā vimalacandro lakṣaṇanaimittikāṃ chāstrapāṭhakān brāhmaṇān sannipātyaivam āha: 2. kiṃ brāhmaṇāḥ kumārasya nimittaṃ paśyatha, śobhanam aśobhanaṃ veti? 3. atha naimittikā brāhmaṇāḥ kathayaty: asādhur ayaṃ mahārāja kumāro jātaḥ, asādhur iti. 4. rājā śrutvā sasaṃbhramaṃ papraccha: kimidaṃ brāhmaṇā? 5. naimittikāḥ kathayanty: ayaṃ deva rājakumāro yadi sapta varṣāṇi jīvati sa eṣa mātāpitaraṃ jīvitād vyāvaropayiṣyati. 6. tato sa rājā evam āha: varaṃ me jīvitāntarāyo bhavatu mā cāhaṃ putraṃ vadheyaṃ. 7. tat kasmāt? kadācit karhacil loke manuṣyotpādaṃ labhyate. 8. nāhaṃ tathā kariṣyāmi yad imaṃ mānuṣyakaṃ kāyaṃ virāgayiṣyāmi.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Then King <s>Vimalacandra</s> summoned the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who were readers of the marks and signs and of the scriptures, and said to them: 2. "What sign do you see for the prince, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — auspicious or inauspicious?" 3. The sign-reading <s>brāhmaṇas</s> said: "This prince is born inauspicious, O great king — inauspicious!" 4. The king, having heard, asked with alarm: "What is this, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s>?" 5. The sign-readers said: "O lord, if this prince lives for seven years, he will deprive his mother and father of life." 6. Then the king said: "Let there be danger to my own life, but I shall not kill my son! 7. Why? Because a human birth is obtained in the world only rarely. 8. I shall not do anything that would cause me to be repulsed by this human body."'

body.text: SaSū(C) 103

1. atha sa kumāro vardhate: yad anye varṣadvayena vardhante tadāsāv ekena māsena vardhate; 2. jānāti ca sa rājā vimalacandro: 'yaṃ kumāro mama karmopacayena vardhate. 3. tato rājā tasya kumārasya paṭṭam ābandhyaivam āha: tava rājyaṃ bhavatu, vipulā ca kīrti, rājyabhogaiśvaryaṃ ca kāraya dharmeṇa, mā adharmeṇa. 4. tataḥ paṭṭaṃ badhvā, rājeti nāmadheyam akarot. 5. sa ca rājā vimalacandro na bhūyaḥ svaviṣaye rājyaṃ kārayaty.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Then the prince grew: what others grow in two years, he grew in a single month. 2. And King <s>Vimalacandra</s> knew: "The prince is growing through the ripening of my <s>karma</s>." 3. Then the king tied the royal turban (<s>paṭṭa</s>) on the prince and said: "May the kingdom be yours, and widespread fame! Exercise sovereignty and royal enjoyment righteously, not unrighteously!" 4. Having tied the turban, he gave him the title of king. 5. And King <s>Vimalacandra</s> no longer exercised kingship in his own realm.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 104

1. atha te triṃśad amātyakoṭyo, yena sa rājā vimalacandras tenopasaṃkrāntā, upetya, taṃ rājānaṃ vimalacandram evam āhuḥ: kasmāt tvaṃ bhoḥ mahārāja svaviṣaye na bhūyo rājyaṃ kārayasi? 2. rājāha: bahūny asaṃkhyeyāni kalpāni, yan mayā rājyabhogaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritaṃ, na ca me kadācid viṣayeṣu tṛptir āsīt. 3. tena ca kālena tena samayena na cireṇa kālāntareṇa sa putras taṃ mātāpitaraṃ jīvitād vyavaropayati, 4. tena ca tatra paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāny upacitāni. 5. ahaṃ ca bhoḥ puruṣa tāvac ciraṃ kālasamayam anusmarāmi yathādya śvo vā.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Then thirty <s>koṭis</s> of ministers approached King <s>Vimalacandra</s> and said to him: "Why, O great king, do you no longer exercise kingship in your own realm?" 2. The king said: "For many incalculable <s>kalpas</s> I have exercised sovereignty, royal enjoyment, and dominion, yet I was never satiated with sense-pleasures. 3. And at that time, before long, the son deprived his mother and father of life. 4. And thereby the five heinous deeds (<s>pañcānantarya</s>) were accumulated. 5. And I, O sir, remember that long past time as if it were yesterday or today.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 105

1. yadā tasya rājño duḥkhā vedanā utpannā tadā sa rājā vipratisārībhūto 'śrukaṇṭhaḥ paridevati: pāpaṃ me karma kṛtam iti! avīcau mahānarake duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ pratyanubhaviṣyāmīti! 2. tato 'haṃ kāruṇyacittam utpādya tatra gatvā tasya rājño dharman deśayitavān; 3. atha sa rājā taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā tasya tāni paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṣipraṃ niravaśeṣaṃ parikṣayaṃ gatāni. āha:
body.translated_text: 1. 'When painful sensation arose for that king, the king, filled with remorse, wept with tears: "Evil <s>karma</s> has been done by me! I shall experience painful sensation in the <s>Avīci</s> great hell!" 2. Then I, having generated a mind of compassion, went there and taught the <s>Dharma</s> to that king. 3. Then that king, having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, his five heinous deeds were quickly and completely exhausted without remainder.' He spoke:

children.text: (1) saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrarājaṃ mahātapāḥ /
children.translated_text: (1) 'The <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>Dharma</s> discourse, the king of <s>sūtras</s>, O great ascetic —

children.text: ye śroṣyanti iman dharman padaṃ prāpsyanty anuttaram //
children.translated_text: those who will hear this <s>Dharma</s> will attain the unsurpassed stage (<s>pada</s>).

children.text: (2) sarvapāpakṣayaṃ bhavati sarvakleśāṃc chamiṣyati /
children.translated_text: (2) All evil will be destroyed, and all afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) will be pacified.'

children.text: śṛṇu dharmaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena kṣipraṃ vimokṣase //
children.translated_text: Listen! I shall proclaim the <s>Dharma</s> by which you will be swiftly liberated.

children.text: (3) catuṣpadāyāṃ gāthāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇaṃ nirantaraṃ /
children.translated_text: (3) When a four-line verse (<s>gāthā</s>) is being spoken continuously,

children.text: sarvapāpakṣayaṃ kṛtvā srotāpanno bhaviṣyasi //
children.translated_text: having destroyed all evil, you will become a stream-enterer (<s>srotāpanna</s>).

children.text: (4) tatodānaṃ udānemi sarvapāpapramocanaṃ /
children.translated_text: (4) Then I utter an inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>), the release from all evil:

children.text: mocitā duḥkhitā satvā nārakād bhayabhairavāt //
children.translated_text: 'Freed are the suffering beings from the fearful and terrible hell!'

children.text: (5) tataḥ sa puruṣotthāya āsanād añjalīkṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: (5) Then that man, rising from his seat, with palms joined,

children.text: praṇamya śirasā tasya sādhukāraṃ prayacchati //
children.translated_text: bowing his head before him, gives forth a cry of approval:

children.text: (6) sādhu kalyāṇamitrāṇi sādhu pāpavināśaka /
children.translated_text: (6) 'Excellent are the spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>)! Excellent, the destroyer of evil!

children.text: sādhu saṃghāṭanirdeśaṃ ye śroṣyanti mahānayaṃ //
children.translated_text: Excellent, the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> teaching! Those who will hear this great doctrine —'

body.text: SaSū(C) 106
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 106

body.text: 1. atha khalu tena kālena tena samayenopary antarikṣe sthitāni dvādaśa devaputrasahasrāṇi kṛtāṃjalipuṭāni, tam ṛṣim upagamya, pādau śirasā praṇamya, evam āhuḥ: bhagavan, kevac ciraṃ smarasi mahātapa? 2. evaṃ catvāraḥ koṭīr nāgarājñām āgatya, aṣṭādaśa koṭīsahasrāṇi yakṣarājñām āgatya, yena sa ṛṣis tenāṃjaliṃ praṇāmya, evam āhuḥ: kevac ciraṃ smarasi?
body.translated_text: 1. Now at that time and on that occasion, twelve thousand <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods), standing in the sky above with palms joined, approached that <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer), bowed their heads at his feet, and said: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, how far back do you remember, O Great Ascetic?' 2. Likewise, four <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Nāga</s>-kings came, and eighteen thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Yakṣa</s>-kings came, and joining palms toward the <s>ṛṣi</s>, they said: 'How far back do you remember?'

body.text: SaSū(C) 107
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 107

body.text: 1. mahātmā ṛṣir āha: śatam asaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīnayutasahasrāṇi samanusmarāmi. 2. āhu: kena kuśalakarmaṇā muhūrtamātreṇaivaṃ pāpaṃ karma praśāntam? 3. āha: saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā, anena kuśalakarmaṇā sarvapāpakarma praśāntam;
body.translated_text: 1. The great-souled <s>ṛṣi</s> said: 'I remember back a hundred <s>asaṃkhyeya</s> (incalculable) thousands of myriads of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons).' 2. They asked: 'By what meritorious action was such evil <s>karma</s> pacified in a mere moment?' 3. He said: 'By hearing the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> — by this meritorious action, all evil <s>karma</s> was pacified.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 108
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 108

body.text: 1. ye ca tatra satvāḥ sannipatitāḥ, yair imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā śraddadhānatā vā kṛtā, te sarve vyākriyante 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau; 2. yena ca puruṣeṇa tāni paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṛtāni, tenemaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā muhūrtamātreṇa tāni paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi niravaśeṣaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ kṛtāṇi; 3. tasyānekāni kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi sarvadurgatidvārāṇi pithitāni bhavanti; 4. dvātriṃśad devalokadvārāṇy apāvṛtāni bhavanti; 5. ya itaḥ saṃghāṭād dharmaparyāyād antaśaś catuṣpadikām api gāthāṃ śroṣyati, tasyetādṛśāni kuśalamūlāni bhaviṣyanti; 6. kaḥ punar vādo yaḥ saṃghāṭasūtraṃ satkariṣyati gurukariṣyati mānayiṣyati pūjayiṣyati puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākābhirvādyāṃjalikarmapraṇāmaṃ vā kariṣyati, ekāṃ vārāṃ anumodiṣyaty, evaṃ ca vakṣyati: sādhu subhāṣitam iti!
body.translated_text: 1. 'Those beings who gathered there and who, having heard this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, produced even [a moment of] faith — they are all predicted for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). 2. That man who committed the five actions of immediate retribution (<s>pañcānantarya</s>), having heard this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, in a mere moment those five actions of immediate retribution were completely exhausted and consumed. 3. For countless hundreds of thousands of myriads of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, the doors to all unfortunate rebirths (<s>durgati</s>) become closed for him; 4. and the doors to the thirty-two <s>deva</s>-worlds become opened. 5. Whoever hears from this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> even a single four-line verse — such will be his roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). 6. What need is there to speak of one who will honor the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>, esteem it, respect it, worship it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and pennants, or will perform music, gestures of reverence, and prostrations, or will rejoice even once, saying: "Well spoken!"'

body.text: SaSū(C) 109
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 109

body.text: 1. atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: kiyantaṃ bhagavann añjalipraṇāmāt puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavati ye te saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣyamāṇaṃ śrutvāñjaliṃ kṛtvā praṇamanti? 2. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu kulaputra, yena paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṛtāṇi, kāritāni, kriyamāṇāni vānumoditāni, yadi sa itaḥ saṃghāṭād dharmaparyāyād antaśaś catuṣpadikām api gāthāṃ śrutvāñjaliṃ praṇāmayiṣyati, tasya tāni sarvāṇi paṃcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṣayaṃ gatāni bhaviṣyanti; 3. kaḥ punar vādaḥ sarvaśūra yaḥ sakalasamāptam evāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyaty: ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'How great a mass of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>), O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does one generate from joining palms and prostrating, who, having heard the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> being spoken, joins palms and prostrates?' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, O son of good family. One who has committed, caused to be committed, or approved of the five actions of immediate retribution (<s>pañcānantarya</s>) being committed — if that person, having heard from this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> even a single four-line verse, joins palms and prostrates, all those five actions of immediate retribution will become exhausted. 3. What need is there to speak, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, of one who will hear this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> complete and entire — that person will generate a far greater mass of merit.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 110
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 110

body.text: 1. upamāṃ te kulaputra kariṣyāmi asya saṃghāṭasūtrārthasya vijñaptaye: 2. tadyathāpināma sarvaśūrānavataptasya nāgarājasya bhavane na kadācit sūryo 'vabhāsayati, tataś ca paṃca mahānadyaḥ pravahanti. atha kaścid eva puruṣo bhaved yas tāsāṃ paṃcānāṃ mahānadīnām udakasya bindūni gaṇayet. 4. tat kiṃ manyase sarvaśūra, śakyaṃ teṣām udakavindunāṃ gaṇanāyogena paryantam adhigantum? 5. āha: no hīdaṃ bhagavan, no hīdaṃ sugata! 6. bhagavān āha: evam eva sarvaśūra na śakyaṃ saṃghāṭasūtrasya dharmaparyāyasya kuśalamūlaṃ, kalpena vā, kalpaśatena vā, kalpasahasreṇa vā, kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṇa vā, gaṇanayā paryantam adhigantuṃ.
body.translated_text: 1. 'I shall give you a simile, O son of good family, for the understanding of the meaning of this <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s>: 2. Suppose, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, in the abode of the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Anavatapata</s>, the sun never shines, and from there five great rivers flow. Now suppose some man were to count the drops of water of those five great rivers. 4. What do you think, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s> — would it be possible to reach the end of the count of those water-drops?' 5. He said: 'No indeed, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! No indeed, O <s>Sugata</s>!' 6. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Just so, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, it is not possible to reach the end, by counting — whether in one <s>kalpa</s>, a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, or hundreds of thousands of myriads of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — of the roots of merit of the <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s> discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 111
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 111

body.text: 1. tat kiṃ manyase sarvaśūra, duṣkaraṃ tasya ya imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ muhūrtaṃ prakāśayeta? 2. āha: duṣkaraṃ bhagavaṃ! 3. bhagavān āha: ataḥ suduṣkarataraṃ sarvaśūra tasya ya imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śakṣyati śrotum.
body.translated_text: 1. 'What do you think, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s> — is it difficult for one who illuminates this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> even for a moment?' 2. He said: 'It is difficult, O <s>Bhagavān</s>!' 3. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Even more difficult than that, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, is it for one who is able to hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 112
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 112

body.text: 1. tadyathā anavataptāt paṃca mahānadyaḥ pravahanti, tāsāṃ paṃcānāṃ mahānadīnāṃ pravahantīnām udakavindūn na śakyaṃ gaṇanayā paryantam adhigantum, evam evāsya dharmaparyāyasya puṇyaskandhasya na śakyaṃ paryantam adhigantum. sarvaśūra āha: katamās tā bhagavan paṃca mahānadyaḥ? 3. bhagavān āha: tadyathā: gaṃgā, sītā, vakṣur, yamunā, candrabhāgā ca. 4. imā sarvaśūra paṃca mahānadyo mahāsamudre praviśanti; 5. ekaikā ca mahānadī paṃcanadīśataparivārā.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Just as five great rivers flow from <s>Anavatapata</s>, and it is not possible to reach the end of the water-drops of those five great rivers as they flow — just so, it is not possible to reach the end of the mass of merit of this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>.' <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'What are those five great rivers, O <s>Bhagavān</s>?' 3. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'They are: the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the <s>Sītā</s>, the <s>Vakṣu</s>, the <s>Yamunā</s>, and the <s>Candrabhāgā</s>. 4. These five great rivers, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, enter the great ocean; 5. and each great river is accompanied by five hundred rivers.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 113
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 113

body.text: 1. punar aparaṃ sarvaśūra, paṃcemā mahānadyaḥ ākāśe pravahanti yā prajāṃ prahlādayanti; 2. tāś ca paṃca mahānadyaḥ ekaikā sahasraparivārāḥ. 3. āha: katamās tā bhagavan paṃca mahānadyaḥ sahasrāparivārāḥ? 4. bhagavān āha: sundarī nāma nadī sahasraparivārā, śaṃkhā nāma nadī sahasraparivārā, vahantī nāma nadī sahasraparivārā, citrasenā nāma nadī sahasraparivārā, dharmavṛttā nāma nadī sahasraparivārā. 5. imās tā sarvaśūra paṃca mahānadyaḥ sahasraparivārā yā jaṃbudvīpe autsukyam āpadyante, yāḥ kālena kālaṃ jaṃbudvīpe bindubhir varṣadhārāḥ pramuṃcanti; 6. tena puṣpaphalasasyāny abhiruhyanti. 7. yadā jaṃbudvīpe varṣadhārāḥ prapatanti, tadā udakaṃ jāyate, jātaṃ codakaṃ, sarvakṣetrārāmeṣu tṛpteṣu, satvāḥ sukhino bhavanti.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Furthermore, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, these five great rivers flow in the sky and refresh the people; 2. and each of those five great rivers has a thousand companions.' 3. He said: 'What are those five great rivers with a thousand companions, O <s>Bhagavān</s>?' 4. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The river called <s>Sundarī</s> with a thousand companions, the river called <s>Śaṅkhā</s> with a thousand companions, the river called <s>Vahantī</s> with a thousand companions, the river called <s>Citrasenā</s> with a thousand companions, the river called <s>Dharmavṛttā</s> with a thousand companions. 5. These, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, are the five great rivers with a thousand companions that bring beneficent rainfall to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, releasing showers of rain-drops upon <s>Jambudvīpa</s> from time to time; 6. by that, flowers, fruits, and crops grow. 7. When rain-showers fall upon <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, water is produced, and once the water is produced and all fields and gardens are satisfied, beings become happy.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 114
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 114

body.text: 1. tadyathāpināma sarvaśūra prajāpati sarvajaṃbudvīpe sukhaṃ kārayati, evam eva sarvaśūrāyaṃ saṃghāṭo dharmaparyāya bahujanahitāya jaṃbudvīpe prakāśitaḥ. 2. yathā devānāṃ trāyastriṃśatāṃ āyuṣpramāṇaṃ na tathā manuṣyāṇāṃ. 3. katame sarvaśūra trāyastriṃśā devā yatra śakro devānām indraḥ prativasati. 4. te trāyastriṃśā nāma devāḥ santi tadyathā sarvaśūra satvā ye vāksucaritaṃ bhāṣante. 5. teṣāṃ na śakyaṃ puṇyaskandhasyopamāṃ kartuṃ.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Just as <s>Prajāpati</s> (the Rain-lord) causes happiness in all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, even so, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> has been proclaimed in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> for the benefit of many people. 2. The lifespan of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods is not like that of humans. 3. Which, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, are the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, among whom <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the <s>devas</s>, dwells? 4. Those called the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, are beings who speak well-conducted speech. 5. It is not possible to make a comparison for their mass of merit.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 115
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 115

body.text: 1. santi sarvaśūra satvā ye vāgduścaritaṃ bhāṣante; 2. na śakyaṃ teṣām apuṇyaskandhasyopamāṃ kartum yat te satvāḥ narakatiryakpretaduḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti; 3. na ca kaścit teṣāṃ trātā bhavati; tatra te nirāśāḥ paridevante narakeṣu prapatamānāḥ; 4. tad akalyāṇamitravaśena draṣṭavyaṃ. 5. ye satvā vāksucaritaṃ bhāṣante teṣāṃ na śakyaṃ puṇyaskandhasyopamāṃ kartuṃ; 6. tat kalyāṇamitravaśena draṣṭavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 1. 'There are, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, beings who speak ill-conducted speech. 2. It is not possible to make a comparison for their mass of demerit — the suffering they experience in the hells, animal realms, and <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) realms. 3. No one becomes their rescuer; there they lament without hope, falling into the hells. 4. That should be understood as the effect of bad spiritual friends (<s>akalyāṇamitra</s>). 5. For beings who speak well-conducted speech, it is not possible to make a comparison for their mass of merit. 6. That should be understood as the effect of good spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 116
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 116

body.text: 1. yadā kalyāṇamitraṃ paśyati, tadā tathāgato dṛṣṭo bhavati; 2. yadā tathāgataṃ paśyati, tadā tasya sarvapāpakṣayo bhavati; 3. yadā sarvapāpakṣayo bhavati, tadā prajāpatir jaṃbudvīpe autsukyaṃ karoti; 4. yadā prajāpatir jaṃbudvīpe autsukyaṃ karoti, tadā jaṃbudvīpakānāṃ satvānāṃ sukhasya na śakyam upamāṃ kartum. 5. evam evāyaṃ sarvaśūra saṃghāṭo dharmaparyāyo jaṃbudvīpe buddhakṛtyaṃ karoti; 6. tadā na śakyaṃ teṣāṃ satvānāṃ puṇyaskandhasyopamāṃ kartum.
body.translated_text: 1. 'When one sees a good spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> is seen. 2. When one sees the <s>Tathāgata</s>, all one's evil is destroyed. 3. When all one's evil is destroyed, <s>Prajāpati</s> brings beneficial rain to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. 4. When <s>Prajāpati</s> brings beneficial rain to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, it is not possible to make a comparison for the happiness of the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. 5. Just so, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> performs the work of a <s>Buddha</s> in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. 6. Then it is not possible to make a comparison for the mass of merit of those beings.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 117
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 117

body.text: tadyathāpināma sarvaśūra, yatremāḥ paṃca mahānadyaḥ saṃbhedaṃ samavasaraṇaṃ gacchanti, tatra na śakyam udakasya pramāṇam udgrahītuṃ, etāvad udakakuṃbhā vā, udakakuṃbhaśatāni vā, udakakuṃbhasahasrāṇi vā, udakakuṃbhaśatasahasrāṇi vā. api tu bahutvād udakasya mahān udakaskandha: iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati.
body.translated_text: Just as, for example, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, where these five great rivers come together at a confluence, there it is not possible to measure the quantity of water — so many water-pots, or hundreds of water-pots, or thousands of water-pots, or hundreds of thousands of water-pots. Rather, due to the abundance of water, it is reckoned as a great mass of water.

body.text: SaSū(C) 118
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 118

body.text: evam eva sarvaśūra yadā jaṃbudvīpakā satvā imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti, śrutvā codgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti, vācayiṣyanti, paryavāpsyanti, pareṣāṃ ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, pratipattyā ca saṃpādayiṣyanti, tadā na śakyaṃ teṣāṃ satvānāṃ puṇyaskandhasya pramāṇaṃ udgrahītum. api tu bahutvāt puṇyasya mahān puṇyaskandha: iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati.
body.translated_text: Just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, when the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma), and having heard it, will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, explain it in detail to others, and accomplish it through practice, then it is not possible to measure the mass of merit of those beings. Rather, due to the abundance of merit, it is reckoned as a great mass of merit.

body.text: SaSū(C) 119
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 119

body.text: 1. ye sarvaśūra satvāḥ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ na śroṣyanti, na taiḥ śakyam anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃboddhum; 2. na śakyaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayitum; 3. na śakyaṃ dharmagaṇḍī parāhanitum; 4. na śakyaṃ tair dharmasiṃhāsanam abhiroḍhuṃ; 5. na śakyaṃ nirvāṇadhātum anupraveṣṭuṃ; 6. na śakyam aprameyai raśmibhir avabhāsayitum; 7. ya imaṃ sarvaśūra saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ na śroṣyanti, na śakyaṃ tair bodhimaṇḍe niṣattuṃ.
body.translated_text: 1. Those beings, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who will not hear the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, for them it is not possible to fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening); 2. it is not possible to turn the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Dharma); 3. it is not possible to strike the <s>dharmagaṇḍī</s> (Dharma gong); 4. it is not possible for them to ascend the <s>dharmasiṃhāsana</s> (Dharma lion-throne); 5. it is not possible to enter the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> (realm of nirvāṇa); 6. it is not possible to illuminate with immeasurable rays of light; 7. Those who will not hear this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, for them it is not possible to sit at the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening).

body.text: SaSū(C) 120
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 120

body.text: 1. sarvaśūra āha: pṛcchāmi bhagavaṃ, pṛcchāmi sugata kaṃcid eva kautuhalam. 2. bhagavān āha: pṛccha tvaṃ sarvaśūra, yad yad evākāṃkṣasy ahaṃ te niṣkāṃkṣaṃ kariṣyāmi. 3. sarvaśūra āha: katamaḥ sa bhagavan ṛṣir abhūd yena te satvāḥ paṃcabhir ānantaryaiḥ karmabhiḥ parimokṣitāḥ, avaivartikabhūmau ca pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ? 4. bhagavān āha:
body.translated_text: 1. <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'I ask the <s>Bhagavān</s>, I ask the <s>Sugata</s> a certain question out of curiosity.' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Ask, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, whatever you wish; I shall remove your doubt.' 3. <s>Sarvaśūra</s> said: 'Who was that <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage), O <s>Bhagavān</s>, by whom those beings were liberated from the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) <s>karmas</s> (actions) and established on the stage of non-retrogression?' 4. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: (1) sūkṣmaṃ vacana buddhānāṃ sarvaśūra śṛṇohi me /
children.translated_text: (1) 'The words of the <s>Buddhas</s> are subtle, <s>Sarvaśūra</s> — hear me!

children.text: saṃghāṭadarśanaṃ sūtraṃ ṛṣirūpeṇa darśitam //
children.translated_text: The <s>Saṃghāṭa Sūtra</s> was revealed in the form of a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage).

children.text: (2) saṃghāṭo buddharūpaṃ ca darśayaty anukampayā /
children.translated_text: (2) The <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> displays the form of a <s>Buddha</s> out of compassion,

children.text: yathā bālika gaṃgāyā rūpaṃ darśayate tathā //
children.translated_text: just as, O child, it displays the form of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> (Ganges).

children.text: (3) buddho darśayate rūpaṃ dharman deśayate svayam /
children.translated_text: (3) The <s>Buddha</s> displays his form and teaches the <s>Dharma</s> himself;

children.text: buddhaṃ ya icchate draṣṭuṃ lokanāthaṃ jinottamaṃ //
children.translated_text: whoever wishes to see the <s>Buddha</s>, the protector of the world, the supreme victor —

children.text: (4) saṃghāṭas tena śrotavyaḥ saṃghāṭaṃ buddhasādṛśaṃ /
children.translated_text: (4) by that person the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> should be heard; the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> is the likeness of the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: buddhas tatra bhaven nityaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddha</s> is always present wherever the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> abides.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 121
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 121

body.text: 1. tatra khalu bhagavān punar api sarvaśūraṃ bodhisatvam āmantrayate sma: 2. bhūtapūrvaṃ sarvaśūrātīte 'dhvani navānavaty asaṃkhyeyān kalpān anusmarāmi; 3. tatra dvādaśa buddhakoṭyo babhūvan, ratnottamanāmānas, tathāgatā, arhantaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ. 4. ahaṃ tena kālena tena samayena pradānaśūro 'bhūvaṃ candro nāma. 5. te ca me dvādaśa buddhakoṭya paryupāsitāḥ; khādanīyabhojanīyamālyagandhavilepanena, yathāsukhaṃ, praṇītenāhāreṇa, sarvasukhopadhānenopasthitāḥ; upasthāpya ca, 6. tatraiva mayā sarvaśūra vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdham.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> again addressed the <s>bodhisattva Sarvaśūra</s>: 2. 'In a former time, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, in the past, I recall ninety-nine incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) ago; 3. there arose twelve <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of <s>Buddhas</s> named <s>Ratnottama</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. 4. At that time and occasion I was a generous hero named <s>Candra</s>. 5. Those twelve <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> were attended by me with food and drink, garlands, perfumes, and ointments, with proper nourishment as they wished, and served with every comfort; and having served them, 6. right there, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, I received a prophecy of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 122
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 122

body.text: 1. anusmarāmy ahaṃ sarvaśūra: aṣṭādaśa buddhakoṭya, sarve ratnāvabhāsanāmānas tathāgatā loka utpannā abhūvan. 2. tatrāham api pradānaśūro 'bhūvaṃ garbhaseno nāma. 3. te cāṣṭādaśa buddhakoṭyo mayā paryupāsitāḥ, pūjitāś ca, yathā tathāgatānāṃ pratyarhaṃ gandhamālyavilepanālaṃkāravibhūṣaṇaiḥ. 4. tatra ca me vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ.
body.translated_text: 1. 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, all named <s>Ratnāvabhāsa</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arose in the world. 2. There too I was a generous hero named <s>Garbhasena</s>. 3. Those eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> were attended and worshipped by me, with perfumes, garlands, ointments, and ornaments befitting <s>Tathāgatas</s>. 4. And there I received a prophecy of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 123
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 123

body.text: 1. anusmarāmy ahaṃ sarvaśūra: viṃśati buddhakoṭyaḥ śikhisaṃbhavanāmānas, tathāgatā, arhantaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddhā loka udapadyanta. 2. pūjitā me te buddhā bhagavanto yathā pratyarheṇa pūjasatkāreṇa. 3. tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdham; 4. na cādyāpi kālasamayam abhūd vyākaraṇāya.
body.translated_text: 1. 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> named <s>Śikhisaṃbhava</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, arose in the world. 2. Those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> were worshipped by me with fitting honor and veneration. 3. And right there I received a prophecy of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening); 4. yet even now the time and occasion for that prophecy has not yet come.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 124
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 124

body.text: 1. anusmarāmy ahaṃ sarvaśūra: viṃśaty eva buddhakoṭyaḥ kāśyapanāmānas, tathāgatā, arhantaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddhā loka udapadyanta. 2. tatrāham api pradānaśūro 'bhūvaṃ. 3. kṛtaṃ me teṣāṃ tathāgatānām upasthānaṃ; gandhena, mālyena, vilepanena, tathāgatagurūpasthānenopasthitāḥ; yathā tathāgatānāṃ gurugauravaṃ kartavyaṃ tathā kṛtaṃ. 4. tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ.
body.translated_text: 1. 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, arose in the world. 2. There too I was a generous hero. 3. I performed service to those <s>Tathāgatas</s> — with perfume, garlands, and ointments, I attended them with the reverent service due to <s>Tathāgatas</s>; just as reverence and respect should be shown to <s>Tathāgatas</s>, so was it done. 4. And right there I received a prophecy of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 125
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 125

body.text: 1. anusmarāmy ahaṃ sarvaśūra: ṣoḍaśa buddhakoṭyo 'bhūvan, vimalaprabhāsanāmānas, tathāgatā, arhantaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ. 2. tena ca kālena tena samayenāhaṃ gṛhapatir abhūvam, āḍhyo mahādhano, mahābhogaḥ, sarvasvaparityāgī. 3. te ca mayā ṣoḍaśa buddhakoṭyaḥ pūjitā, āstaraṇaprāvaraṇena, gandhena, mālyena, vilepanena, vibhūṣaṇācchādanena ca; yathā tathāgatānāṃ gurūpasthānaṃ kartavyaṃ tathā ca mayā kṛtaṃ. 4. tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ; 5. na ca me kālaṃ na samayam abhūd vyākaraṇāya.
body.translated_text: 1. 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: there were sixteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> named <s>Vimalaprabha</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. 2. At that time and occasion I was a householder, wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, one who renounced everything. 3. Those sixteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> were worshipped by me with bedding and coverings, perfume, garlands, ointments, and ornaments and clothing; just as reverent service should be rendered to <s>Tathāgatas</s>, so was it done by me. 4. And right there I received a prophecy of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening); 5. yet the time and occasion for that prophecy has not yet come.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 126
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 126

body.text: 1. śṛṇu sarvaśūra, anusmarāmy ahaṃ: paṃcanavatir buddhakoṭyo loka utpannāny abhūvan, sarve śākyamunināmānas, tathāgatā, arhantaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ. 2. ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena ca rājābhūvaṃ, dhārmiko, dharmarājā. 3. paryupāsitā me te paṃcanavatir buddhakoṭyaḥ śākyamunināmadheyās tathāgatāḥ, gandhena, mālyena, vilepanena, āstaraṇapravaraṇena, cchatradhvajapatākābhiś ca. 4. tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdham.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, I recall: ninety-five <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> arose in the world, all named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. 2. At that time and occasion I was a king, a righteous one, a <s>Dharmarāja</s> (king of Dharma). 3. Those ninety-five <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, were attended by me with perfume, garlands, ointments, bedding and coverings, and with parasols, banners, and flags. 4. And right there I received a prophecy of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 127
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 127

body.text: 1. anusmarāmy ahaṃ sarvaśūra: navati buddhakoṭyaḥ krakatsudanāmānas, tathāgatā, arhantaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddhā, loka udapadyanta. 2. ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena brāhmaṇakumāro 'bhūvam, āḍhyo, mahādhano, mahābhogaḥ, pradānadātā, sarvasvaparityāgī. 3. te ca mayā tathāgatā sarve upasthitāḥ, gandhena, mālyena, vilepanena, āstarāṇaprāvaraṇena, vibhūṣaṇācchādanena; yādṛśaṃ ca tathāgatānām upasthānaṃ tathā teṣāṃ mayā pratyarham upasthānaṃ kṛtaṃ. 4. tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ; 5. na ca me kālaṃ na samayaṃ vyākaraṇāya.
body.translated_text: 1. 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: ninety <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> named <s>Krakatsuda</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, arose in the world. 2. At that time and occasion I was a young <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, a giver of gifts, one who renounced everything. 3. All those <s>Tathāgatas</s> were served by me with perfume, garlands, ointments, bedding and coverings, and ornaments and clothing; just as service should be rendered to <s>Tathāgatas</s>, so was fitting service rendered to them by me. 4. And right there I received a prophecy of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening); 5. yet the time and occasion for that prophecy has not yet come.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 128
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 128

body.text: 1. anusmarāmy ahaṃ sarvaśūra: aṣṭādaśa buddhakoṭyo loka udapadyanta, sarve kanakamunināmānas, tathāgatā, arhantaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ. 2. ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena pradānaśūro 'bhūvam. 3. paryupāsitā me te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ, pūjitāś ca gandhena, mālyena, vilepanena, āstaraṇaprāvaraṇena, vibhūṣaṇena; yathā tathāgatānāṃ gurūpasthānāṃ tathā me upasthitāḥ. 4. tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ; 5. na ca me kālaṃ na samayaṃ vyākaraṇāya.
body.translated_text: 1. 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> arose in the world, all named <s>Kanakamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. 2. At that time and occasion I was a generous hero. 3. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones were attended and worshipped by me with perfume, garlands, ointments, bedding and coverings, and ornaments; just as reverent service should be rendered to <s>Tathāgatas</s>, so were they served by me. 4. And right there I received a prophecy of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening); 5. yet the time and occasion for that prophecy has not yet come.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 129
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 129

body.text: 1. anusmarāmy ahaṃ sarvaśūra: trayodaśa buddhakoṭyo loka udapadyanta, sarve 'vabhāsaśrīnāmānas, tathāgatā, arhantaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ. 2. te ca me tathāgatāḥ pūjitā, āstaraṇaprāvaraṇena, gandhena, mālyena, vilepanācchādanavibhūṣaṇena; yathā tathāgatānāṃ gurūpasthānaṃ kṛtaṃ tādṛśam upasthānam upasthitāḥ. 3. taiś ca tathāgatair nānādharmamukhāni bhāṣitāni arthavinayaviniścayāt. 4. tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ; 5. na cādyāpi samayaṃ vyākaraṇāya.
body.translated_text: (1) 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: thirteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> arose in the world, all named <s>Avabhāsaśrī</s> (Radiance-Glory), <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones. (2) Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> were honored by me with bedding and coverings, with fragrance, garlands, ointments, coverings, and ornaments; such attendance as is rendered to <s>Tathāgatas</s> as preceptors, such attendance I rendered. (3) Those <s>Tathāgatas</s> taught various gateways of the <s>Dharma</s>, by way of definitive meaning and discipline. (4) There...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 130
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 130

body.text: 1. anusmarāmy ahaṃ sarvaśūra: paṃcaviṃśati buddhakoṭyaḥ puṣyanāmānas, tathāgatā, arhantaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddhā loka udapādyanta. 2. ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena pravrajito 'bhūvam. 3. paryupāsitā me te tathāgatā; yathānanda etarhi mamopasthānam upatiṣṭhati, tādṛśaṃ ca me te tathāgatā upasthitāḥ. 4. tatraiva ca me vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhaṃ; 5. na cādyāpi samayam abhūd vyākaraṇāya.
body.translated_text: (1) 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: twenty-five <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> named <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones, arose in the world. (2) At that time and season I had gone forth [as a renunciant]. (3) I attended upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s>; just as <s>Ānanda</s> now renders attendance to me, so I attended upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. (4) And there I received the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) of supreme perfect awakening. (5) But even now it is not yet fully...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 131
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 131

body.text: 1. anusmarāmy ahaṃ sarvaśūra: aṣṭādaśa buddhakoṭyo vipaśyināmānas, tathāgatā, arhantaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddhā loka udapadyanta. 2. paryupāsitā me te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ, ābharaṇaprāvaraṇena, ācchādanagandhamālyavilepanena; yathā tathāgatopasthānaṃ tathā me upasthitā. 3. ahaṃ ca tena kālena tena samayena pravrajito 'bhūvam. 4. tatraiva cāhaṃ vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhavān; 5. na cādyāpi samayaṃ vyākaraṇāya, na cireṇa kālena.
body.translated_text: (1) 'I recall, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones, arose in the world. (2) I attended upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones, with ornaments and coverings, with coverings, fragrances, garlands, and ointments; just as attendance is rendered to a <s>Tathāgata</s>, so I attended upon them. (3) At that time and season I had gone forth [as a renunciant]. (4) And there I received the prediction of supreme perfect awakening...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 132
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 132

body.text: 1. yaḥ paścimako vipaśyī loka utpannaḥ sa imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣitavān. 2. tam ahaṃ jñātvā, tasmin samaye, jaṃbudvīpe saptaratnavarṣaṃ pravṛṣṭavān. tadā te jāṃbudvīpakāḥ satvā adaridrā saṃvṛttāḥ. 3. tatraiva cāhaṃ vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabdhavān; 4. tataś cireṇa kālasamayenādyāpi ca māṃ na vyākaroty anutpattikadharmakṣāntivyākaraṇena.
body.translated_text: (1) 'The last <s>Vipaśyin</s> who arose in the world — he taught this <s>Saṃghāṭa dharmaparyāya</s>. (2) Having known that, at that time I caused a rain of the seven treasures to fall upon <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Then those beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> became free from poverty. (3) And there I received the prediction of supreme perfect awakening. (4) But even after a long time and season, even now he does not give me the prediction of the patience of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 133
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 133

body.text: 1. āha: katamaḥ sa bhagavan kālaḥ, katamaḥ sa samayaḥ? 2. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu sarvaśūra, tato 'py asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpair dīpaṃkaro nāma tathāgato, 'rhan, samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi. 3. tato 'haṃ sarvaśura tena kālena tena samayena megho nāma māṇavako 'bhūvam. 4. yadā sa dīpaṃkaras tathāgato loka utpannaḥ, tadāham api tasmin kāle tasmin samaye brahmacaryam acārṣaṃ māṇavakarūpeṇa. 5. tato 'haṃ, bhagavantan dīpaṃkaran tathāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā, prasādapratilabdhaḥ saptabhir utpalair avakīrṇavām, tac ca tathāgatāvaropitaṃ kuśalamūlam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmitam. 6. sa ca mān dīpaṃkaras tathāgato vyākārṣīd: bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇavakānāgate 'dhvany asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpaiḥ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato, 'rhan, samyaksaṃbuddha iti.
body.translated_text: (1) He said: 'What was that time, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, what was that season?' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>. Incalculable <s>kalpas</s> beyond even that, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> (Lamp-Maker), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Fully Awakened One, arose in the world. (3) Then, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, at that time and season, I was a young man named <s>Megha</s> (Cloud). (4) When that <s>Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara</s> arose in the world, at that very time and season I practiced the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the form of a young man. (5) Then...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 134
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 134

body.text: 1. tato 'haṃ sarvaśūra, dvādaśatālamātraṃ vihāyasam antarīkṣe sthitvā, anutpattikadharmakṣāntiṃ pratilabdhavān. 2. yac ca me sarvaśūrāsaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpeṣu brahmacaryaṃ cīrṇaṃ, yac ca pāramitāpratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ, tat sarvam āmukhībhūtam ivānusmarāmi yathādya śvo vā. 3. tatra mayā sarvaśūrānekāni satvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāni. 4. kaḥ punar vādaḥ sarvaśūra, ya etarhy aham, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ, sarvasatvahitaiṣī, kāruṇikaḥ, satvānāṃ nirodhadharman deśayiṣyāmi.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Then, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, having stood in the air at a height of twelve palm-trees, I attained the patience of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>). (2) Whatever holy life I have led through incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, and whatever wholesome roots connected with the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) — all that I recall as vividly as if it were today or tomorrow. (3) There, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, I established many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of beings in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. (4) What then need be said...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 135
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 135

body.text: 1. naitat sthānaṃ vidyate. tat kasya hetoḥ? 2. bahuprakāraṃ cāhaṃ sarvaśūra satvānān dharman deśayāmi: yathārūpavaineyānāṃ satvānāṃ, tathārūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi. 3. devarūpeṇa devaloke dharman deśayāmi; 4. nāgabhavane nāgarūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi; 5. yakṣabhavane yakṣarūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi; 6. pretabhavane pretarūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi; 7. manuṣyaloke manuṣyarūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi; 8. buddhavaineyānāṃ satvānāṃ buddharūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi; 9. bodhisatvāvaineyānāṃ satvānāṃ bodhisatvarūpeṇa dharman deśayāmi; 10. yena yena rūpeṇa satvā vinayaṃ gacchanti, tena tena rūpeṇāhaṃ satvānān dharman deśayāmi; evaṃ bahuprakāram ahaṃ sarvaśūra satvānān dharman deśayāmi.
body.translated_text: (1) 'This is not possible [that beings would not be helped]. For what reason? (2) In many ways, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings: to beings who are to be trained in a particular form, in that form I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. (3) In the form of a <s>deva</s> I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in the <s>deva</s>-world. (4) In the <s>Nāga</s>-realm, in the form of a <s>Nāga</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. (5) In the <s>Yakṣa</s>-realm, in the form of a <s>Yakṣa</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. (6) In the <s>Preta</s> (hungry ghost)-realm, in the form of a <s>Preta</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. (7) In the human world, in human form, I teach the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 136
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 136

body.text: 1. tat kasya hetor? yathaiva sarvaśūra satvā bahuprakāraṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti, tathaiva te satvasārā bahuprakāraṃ kuśalamūlāni kariṣyanti, 2. dānāni ca dadanti, puṇyāni ca kurvanti, svārthe ca pratijāgaranti, maraṇānusmṛtiṃ ca bhāvayiṣyanti; 3. te caivaṃrūpaṃ kuśalaṃ karmābhisaṃskāraṃ kariṣyanti; 4. tena ca dharmaśravaṇahetunā tat pūrvakaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ saṃsmariṣyanti. 5. teṣāṃ tad bhaviṣyati dīrgharātram arthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca. 6. evaṃ hi sarvaśūra saṃghāṭasūtrasya dharmaparyāyasya sahaśravaṇamātreṇaivam aprameyā guṇānuśaṃsā bhaviṣyanti.
body.translated_text: (1) 'For what reason? Just as, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, beings hear the <s>Dharma</s> in many ways, so those beings of fine essence will perform wholesome roots in many ways. (2) They give gifts, create merit, are vigilant about their own welfare, and cultivate the recollection of death. (3) They will perform such wholesome <s>karmic</s> formations. (4) By the cause of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, they will recall their former wholesome roots. (5) That will become for them...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 137
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 137

body.text: 1. atha te satvāḥ parasparam evam āhuḥ: 2. asty anyaḥ kaścit kuśalamūlo yasya kṛtatvād upacitatvād anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyante, sarvasatvahitaiṣiṇaś ca bhavanti?
body.translated_text: (1) 'Then those beings said to each other: (2) "Is there some other wholesome root, by performing and accumulating which one attains supreme perfect awakening and becomes one who desires the welfare of all beings?"'

body.text: SaSū(C) 138
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 138

body.text: 1. atha bhagavāṃs, teṣāṃ satvānāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāya, tān etad avocat: asti kulaputrā! 2. ye dharmaṃ pattīyanti te evaṃ vakṣyanti: asti dharmo yathābhūtaḥ. 3. teṣāṃ mahāphalaṃ, sukhavipākam, anuttaraṃ dharmasukhaṃ bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known with his own mind the mental deliberation of those beings, said this to them: "There is, O sons of good family! (2) Those who have faith in the <s>Dharma</s> will say thus: 'The <s>Dharma</s> is as it truly is.' (3) For them there will be great fruit, a pleasant ripening, unsurpassed happiness of the <s>Dharma</s>."'

body.text: SaSū(C) 139
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 139

body.text: 1. ye punaḥ satvā mohamūḍhās ta evaṃ vakṣyanti: na santi dharmāḥ, nāsti kaścid dharmāṇāṃ pāragaḥ. 2. sa, teṣāṃ mahāphalaṃ kaṭukavipākam, apāyeṣūpapatsyate, punaḥ punaś ca te mohapuruṣā apāyabhūmiparāyaṇā bhaviṣyanti.
body.translated_text: (1) '"But those beings who are deluded by ignorance will say thus: 'There are no <s>dharmas</s>; there is no one who has gone to the far shore of the <s>dharmas</s>.' (2) For them there will be great fruit — a bitter ripening: they will be reborn in the lower realms (<s>apāyas</s>), and again and again those deluded people will be destined for the planes of suffering."'

body.text: SaSū(C) 140
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 140

body.text: aṣṭau kalpān nairāyikān duḥkhāṃ vedanām anubhaviṣyanti; dvādaśa kalpāni pretayoniṣu duḥkhāṃ vedanām vedayiṣyanti; 3. ṣoḍaśa kalpāny asureṣūpapatsyante; 4. nava kalpasahasrāni bhūtapiśācayoniṣūpapatsyante; 5. caturdaśa kalpasahasrāṇi ajihvakā bhaviṣyanti; 6. ṣoḍaśa kalpasahasrāṇi mātugarbhe kālaṃ kariṣyanti; 7. dvādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi māṃsapiṇḍā bhaviṣyanti; 8. ekādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi jātyandhabhūtāḥ prajāsyanti, duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānā.
body.translated_text: (1) 'They will experience painful feelings in the <s>Naraka</s> (hell) realms for eight <s>kalpas</s>.
