(2) For twelve <s>kalpas</s> they will experience painful feelings in the <s>Preta</s> (hungry ghost) wombs. (3) For sixteen <s>kalpas</s> they will be reborn among the <s>Asuras</s>. (4) For nine thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be reborn in the wombs of <s>Bhūta-Piśāca</s> (ghosts and goblins). (5) For fourteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be tongueless. (6) For sixteen thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will die in the mother's womb. (7) For twelve thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be lumps of flesh. (8) For eleven thousand <s>kalpas</s>...'

body.text: SaSū(C) 141
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 141

body.text: 1. jātyandhaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tadā mātāpitṛbhyām evaṃ bhaviṣyati: nirāsvādam asmābhir duḥkham anubhūtaṃ; nirāsvādam asmākāṃ putro jātaḥ; nirāsvādaṃ navāmāsāḥ kukṣau dhāritaḥ. 2. śītoṣṇāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānaiḥ kṣutpipāsāsuḥkhāni ca pratyanubhūtāni, bahūni ca dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyāny, anyāni ca duḥkhāni pratyanubhūtāni. 3. tatyathāpināmasarvaśūrajātyandhaṃ putraṃ dṛṣṭvā mātāpitror nautsukyaṃ bhavati, mahatī ca nirāśatā bhaviṣyati, evam eva sarvaśūra nirāśāḥ saddharmapratikṣepakāḥ satvāḥ; 4. narakatiryakpretaparāyaṇāḥ, te ca tasmin maraṇakālasamaye mahāśokāśalyasamarpitā bhaviṣyanti.
body.translated_text: (1) And upon seeing the child born blind, the mother and father will think: 'We have experienced suffering without reward; our son was born without reward; for nine months he was carried in the womb without reward.' (2) Experiencing sensations of cold and heat, they endured the sufferings of hunger and thirst, and many sufferings to be experienced in the present life, and other sufferings were endured. (3) Just as, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, upon seeing a blind-born son, the mother and father feel no joy and great despair will arise — just so, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, despairing are those beings who reject the true <s>Dharma</s>. (4) Destined for the hells, animal realms, and the realm of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), they will be pierced by the great thorn of grief at the time of death.

body.text: SaSū(C) 142
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 142

body.text: 1. ye tu sarvaśūra satvā evaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣante: asti dharmaḥ, asti dharmāṇāṃ pāragaḥ, te tena kuśalamūlena viṃśati kalpāny uttarakuruṣūpapatsyante; 2. paṃcaviṃśati kalpasahasrāṇi trāyastriṃśatāṃ devānāṃ sahabhāvyatāyām upapatsyante; 3. trāyastriṃśadbhyo devebhyaś cyavitvā uttarakuruṣūpapatsyante; 4. na ca mātuḥ kukṣāv upapatsyante; 5. lokadhātuśatasahasraṃ ca drakṣyanti; sarve ca tāṃ lokadhātavaḥ sukhāvatīnāmānaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrasandarśanan dṛṣṭvā, tatraiva pratiṣṭhānāṃ kṛtvā, tatraiva bodhim abhisambhotsyante.
body.translated_text: (1) 'But those beings, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, who speak these words: "The <s>Dharma</s> exists; there exists one who has gone beyond the <s>dharmas</s>" — by that root of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), they will be reborn in <s>Uttarakuru</s> for twenty <s>kalpas</s>. (2) For twenty-five thousand <s>kalpas</s> they will be reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods in companionship. (3) Falling from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, they will be reborn in <s>Uttarakuru</s>. (4) They will not be reborn in a mother's womb. (5) And they will see a hundred thousand world-systems; and all those world-systems will be named <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss). Having seen the display of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, having established themselves right there, they will attain awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) right there.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 143
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 143

body.text: 1. evaṃ hi sarvaśūra mahāprabhāvo 'yaṃ saṃghāṭo dharmaparyāyaḥ: 2. ye 'smiṃś cittaprasādaṃ kariṣyanti na te jātu viṣamaparihāreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyanti; pariśuddhaśīlasamavāgatās te satvā bhaviṣyanti.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Such indeed, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, is the great power of this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>: (2) those who will generate faith (<s>cittaprasāda</s>) in it will never die by an adverse death; those beings will be endowed with perfectly pure morality (<s>śīla</s>).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 144
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 144

body.text: 1. santi sarvaśūra satvā ya evaṃ kathayanti: rātrindivam tathāgato bahūni satvāni saṃsārāt parimocayanti, adyāpi satvadhātuḥ kṣayaṃ na gacchanti. 2. bahavo bodhāya praṇidhānaṃ kurvanti, bahavaḥ svargaloka upapadyante, bahavo nirvṛtim anuprāpnuvanti; atha kena hetunā satvānāṃ kṣayo na bhavati?
body.translated_text: (1) 'There are, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, beings who say thus: "Day and night the <s>Tathāgata</s> liberates many beings from <s>saṃsāra</s>, yet even now the realm of beings does not become exhausted." (2) "Many make aspirations toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), many are reborn in the heavenly worlds, many attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> — yet for what reason does the depletion of beings not occur?"'

body.text: SaSū(C) 145
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 145

body.text: 1. athānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthānām etad abhavat: 2. gamiṣyāmo vayaṃ, śramaṇena gautamena sārdhaṃ vivādaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ. 3. atha khalu caturnavati brāhmaṇānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakāḥ, anekāni ca nigranthaśatāni, yena rājagṛhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmanti. 4. tena ca kālena tena samayena bhagavān smitāṃ prāduścakāra.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>tīrthika</s> (non-Buddhist) wanderers, ascetics, mendicants, and <s>Nirgranthas</s> (Jain monks) had this thought: (2) 'We shall go and engage in debate with the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>.' (3) Then ninety-four <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, ascetics, and mendicants, and many hundreds of <s>Nirgranthas</s>, approached <s>Rājagṛha</s>. (4) And at that time and season, the <s>Bhagavān</s> displayed a smile.

body.text: SaSū(C) 146
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 146

body.text: 1. atha khalu maitreyo bodhisatvo mahāsatva utthāyāsanād, ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā, dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya, bhagavantam etad avocat: 2. ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya prāduṣkaraṇāya? nāhetuṃ nāpratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā smitaṃ prāduṣkurvanti.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Maitreya</s>, having risen from his seat, having arranged his upper robe on one shoulder, having placed his right knee on the ground, and extending his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> and bowing, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: (2) 'What is the cause, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, what is the condition for the display of this smile? <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones do not display a smile without cause or condition.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 147
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 147

body.text: 1. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu kulaputra, adyeha rājagṛhe mahānagare rājagṛhe mahāsannipāto bhaviṣyati. 2. āha: ke bhagavann ihāyāsyanti, devā vā, nāgā vā, yakṣā vā, manuṣyā vā, amanuṣyā vā? 3. bhagavān āha: sarva ete maitreyādyehāgamiṣyanti: devanāgayakṣamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ, caturaśītiś ca sahasrāṇi brāhmaṇānām ihāyāsyanti;
body.translated_text: (1) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, O son of good family. Today here in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, there will be a great assembly.' (2) He said: 'Who, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, will come here — gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, humans, or non-humans?' (3) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'All of these, <s>Maitreya</s>, will come here today: gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, humans, and non-humans; and eighty-four thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> will come here.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 148
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 148

body.text: 1. navati koṭīsahasrāṇi tīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthānām ihāyāsyanti. te mayā sārdhaṃ vivādaṃ kariṣyanti. 2. teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ vivādaśamanāya dharman deśayiṣyāmi. 3. sarve ca te brāhmaṇā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittam utpādayiṣyanti. 4. navati koṭīśatasahasrāṇy anyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthāḥ sarve srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāpsyanti.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Ninety thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, ascetics, mendicants, and <s>Nirgranthas</s> will come here. They will engage in debate with me. (2) For the pacification of all their disputes, I shall teach the <s>Dharma</s>. (3) And all those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> will generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). (4) Ninety hundred thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, ascetics, mendicants, and <s>Nirgranthas</s> will all attain the fruit of <s>Srotaāpatti</s> (Stream-entry).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 149
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 149

body.text: aṣṭādaśa koṭīsahasrāṇi nāgarājñām āgamiṣyanti ye mamāntikād dharmaṃ śroṣyanti; śrutvā ca sarve 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpādayiṣyanti.
body.translated_text: 'Eighteen thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Nāga</s> kings will come, who will hear the <s>Dharma</s> from me; and having heard, all will generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 150
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 150

body.text: 1. ṣaṣṭi koṭīsahasrāṇi śuddhāvāsakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇām āgamiṣyanti; 2. tṛṃśat koṭīsahasrāṇi mārāṇāṃ pāpīmatāṃ saparivārāṇām āyāsyanti; 3. dvādaśa koṭīsahasrāṇi asurarājñām āgamiṣyanti; 4. paṃcamātrāṇi ca rājaśatāni saparivārāṇy āyāsyanti dharmaśravaṇāya. 5. te sarve mamāntikād dharmaṃ śrutvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpādayiṣyanti.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Sixty thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of divine sons from the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abode) realms will come; (2) thirty thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Māras</s>, evil ones, with their retinues, will come; (3) twelve thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Asura</s> kings will come; (4) and about five hundred kings with their retinues will come for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. (5) All of them, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from me, will generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 151
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 151

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā, bhagavantaṃ tṛṣ pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā, tatraivāntardhitataḥ.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Maitreya</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, disappeared right there.

body.text: SaSū(C) 152
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 152

body.text: 1. atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisatvo mahāsatva utthāyāsanād, ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā, dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya, bhagavantam etad avocat: 2. kin nāmāni bhagavan paṃcamātrāṇi rājaśatāni?
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvaśūra</s>, having risen from his seat, having arranged his upper robe on one shoulder, having placed his right knee on the ground, and extending his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> and bowing, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: (2) 'What are the names, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, of those approximately five hundred kings?'

body.text: SaSū(C) 153
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 153

body.text: 1. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu sarvaśūra, nando nāma rājā, 2. sunando nāma rājā, 3. upanando nāma rājā, 4. jinarṣabho nāma rājā, 5. brahmaseno nāma rājā, 6. brahmaghoṣo nāma rājā, 7. sudarśano nāma rājā, 8. jayaseno nāma rājā, 9. nandaseno nāma rājā, 10. biṃbisāro nāma rājā, 11. prasenajin nāma rājā, 12. virūḍhako nāma rājā; 13. evaṃpramukhāni paṃcamātrāṇi rājaśatāni, ekaiko rājā viṃśatikoṭīsahasraparivāraḥ. 14. te sarve 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitāḥ, sthāpayitvā rājā virūḍhakaḥ.
body.translated_text: (1) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>: a king named <s>Nanda</s>, (2) a king named <s>Sunanda</s>, (3) a king named <s>Upananda</s>, (4) a king named <s>Jinarṣabha</s>, (5) a king named <s>Brahmasena</s>, (6) a king named <s>Brahmaghoṣa</s>, (7) a king named <s>Sudarśana</s>, (8) a king named <s>Jayasena</s>, (9) a king named <s>Nandasena</s>, (10) a king named <s>Bimbisāra</s>, (11) a king named <s>Prasenajit</s>, (12) a king named <s>Virūḍhaka</s>; (13) thus, headed by these, approximately five hundred kings, each king with a retinue of twenty thousand <s>koṭīs</s>. (14) All of them have set out toward supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), except King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 154
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 154

body.text: 1. pūrvasyān diśi tṛṃśat koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisatvānām āgacchanti; 2. dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi paṃcāśat koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisatvānām āgacchanti; 3. paścimāyān diśi ṣaṣṭi koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisatvānām āgacchanti; 4. uttarasyān diśi aśīti koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisatvānām āgacchanti; 5. adhastāddiśi navati koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisatvānām āgacchanti; 6. ūrdhvāyān diśi śatakoṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisatvānām āgacchanti; 7. sarve ca daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitāḥ.
body.translated_text: (1) 'From the eastern direction, thirty thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> come; (2) from the southern direction, fifty thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> come; (3) from the western direction, sixty thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> come; (4) from the northern direction, eighty thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> come; (5) from the lower direction, ninety thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> come; (6) from the upper direction, a hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> come; (7) and all are established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 155
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 155

body.text: atha te sarve bodhisatvā, yena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ, yena ca gṛddhrakūṭaparvato, yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntā bhagavato darśanāya vandanāya, sarve ca te bodhisatvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitāḥ.
body.translated_text: Then all those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> approached the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, and <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) Mountain, and came into the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s> for the purpose of seeing and paying homage; and all those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> had set out toward supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: SaSū(C) 156
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 156

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhagavān sarvaśūraṃ bodhisatvaṃ mahāsatvam āmantrayati sma: 2. gaccha tvaṃ sarvaśūra daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu, bodhisatvānām evaṃ vada: 3. adya tathāgato rājagṛhe mahānagare dharman deśayati. tad yūyaṃ sarve daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu sthitā añjalīn praṇāmayatha. 4. anuśrāvya ca muhūrtamātreṇa ca punar eva nivartayasva dharmaśravaṇāya.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvaśūra</s>: (2) 'Go, <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in all world-systems in the ten directions and say thus: (3) "Today the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. You who are established in the world-systems of the ten directions, all bow with joined palms." (4) And having announced this, return again within a moment for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 157
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 157

body.text: atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisatvo mahāsatva utthāyāsanād, bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya, bhagavantaṃ tṛṣ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya, ṛddhibalenāntardhitaḥ.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvaśūra</s>, having risen from his seat, having bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, disappeared by the power of supernatural ability (<s>ṛddhi</s>).

body.text: SaSū(C) 158
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 158

body.text: 1. atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisatvo mahāsatvo, daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu gatvā, bodhisatvānām ārocayati: 2. adya mārṣā śākyamunis tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau rājagṛhe mahānagare satvānān dharman deśayati. 3. tad yūyaṃ sādhukāram anuprayacchatha, tad yuṣmākam adyaiva hitāya sukhāya mahālābho bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvaśūra</s>, having gone to the world-systems in the ten directions, announced to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: (2) 'Today, venerables, the <s>Tathāgata Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Fully Awakened One, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in the <s>Sahā</s> world-system, in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. (3) You should utter cries of approval, for today there will be great gain for your benefit and happiness.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 159
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 159

body.text: 1. atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisatvo mahāsatvo, daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu gatvā, sarvabuddhān paryupāsya, bodhisatvānām ārocayitvā, tadyathāpināma balavān puruṣo 'cchaṭāsaṃghāṭaṃ kuryād, atrāntare sarvaśūro bodhisatvo mahāsatvo, yena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ, yena ca bhagavāṃs, tenāgatya, bhagavataḥ purataḥ sthitaḥ. 2. tatra ca sarve brāhmaṇānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthāḥ sannipatitāḥ; 3. bahavaś ca devanāgamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ, paṃcamātrāṇi ca rājaśatāni saparivārāṇi sannipatitāni; 4. triṃśat koṭīsahasrāṇi mārāṇāṃ pāpīyasāṃ saparivārāḥ sannipatitā.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, having gone to the world-systems in the ten directions, having attended upon all the <s>Buddhas</s>, and having informed the <s>bodhisattvas</s> — just as a strong man might snap his fingers — in that instant the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s> came to the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, to where the <s>Bhagavān</s> was, and stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. 2. There, all the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, non-Buddhist wanderers (<s>anyatīrthika</s>), mendicants (<s>caraka</s>), peripatetics (<s>parivrājaka</s>), and <s>Nirgranthas</s> had assembled; 3. and many <s>devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, humans, and non-humans, and five hundred kings with their retinues had assembled; 4. thirty thousand <s>koṭis</s> of evil <s>Māras</s> with their retinues had assembled.

body.text: SaSū(C) 160
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 160

body.text: 1. tena khalu punaḥ samayena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ prakaṃpitam. 2. atha khalu daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu divyaṃ candanacūrṇaṃ pravarṣitaṃ; 3. divyaṃ ca puṣpavarṣaṃ pravarṣitaṃ. 4. tad bhagavato mūrdhasandhau kūṭāgāraḥ saṃsthitaḥ. 5. tena khalu punaḥ samayena tathāgatasya purataḥ śakro devānām indraḥ sthito 'bhūt. sa vajreṇa bhūmiṃ parāhanat.
body.translated_text: 1. At that time, the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> trembled. 2. Then, from the world-systems in the ten directions, divine sandalwood powder rained down; 3. and a divine shower of flowers rained down. 4. A pavilion (<s>kūṭāgāra</s>) stood upon the crown of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s head. 5. At that time, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, stood before the <s>Tathāgata</s>. He struck the earth with his <s>vajra</s>.

body.text: SaSū(C) 161
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 161

body.text: 1. atha khalu tasmin samaye caturdiśaṃ catvāro vātarājāna utthāya pravānti, 2. ye ca rājagṛhe mahānagare saṃkarā vā, pāṃsavo vā, bālikā vā, tat sarvaṃ nagarād bahiḥ prakṣipanti; 3. daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu gandhodakavarṣaṃ pravarṣanti; 4. daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣūtpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkāṇi pravarṣanti; 5. te ca puṣpās teṣāṃ satvānām upari murdhni puṣpacchatrāṇi tasthire, tathāgatasya copari murdhni. 6. upary antarīkṣe caturaśītiḥ kūṭāgārasahasrāṇi saṃsthitāni, 7. teṣu ca caturaśītiṣu puṣpakūṭāgārasahasreṣu caturaśīti sahasrāṇy āsanānāṃ prajñaptāni saptaratnamayāni prādurbhūtāni, 8. sarvatra cāsane tathāgato niṣaṇṇo dharman deśayati. 9. atha khalv ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitaḥ.
body.translated_text: 1. Then at that time, four wind-kings arose and blew from the four directions, 2. casting out from the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> all the refuse, dust, and sand beyond the city; 3. from the world-systems in the ten directions, a rain of fragrant water poured down; 4. from the world-systems in the ten directions, <s>utpalas</s> (blue lotuses), <s>padmas</s> (lotuses), <s>kumudas</s> (white water-lilies), and <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> (white lotuses) rained down; 5. and those flowers formed flower-canopies above the heads of those beings, and above the head of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. 6. In the sky above, eighty-four thousand pavilions (<s>kūṭāgāras</s>) appeared, 7. and in those eighty-four thousand flower-pavilions, eighty-four thousand seats made of the seven precious substances were set forth and manifested, 8. and on every seat a <s>Tathāgata</s> was seated, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. 9. Then this trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>) quaked in six ways.

body.text: SaSū(C) 162
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 162

body.text: 1. atha khalu sarvaśūro bodhisatvo mahāsatvo, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya, bhagavantam etad avocat: ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yad imāny evaṃrūpāṇi rājagṛhe mahānagare prātihāryāṇi sandṛśyante? 2. bhagavān āha: tadyathā kaścid eva puruṣaḥ syāc, cañcalaś, capalo, 'haṃkāramamakārasthitaḥ; sa ca daridro bhavet. 3. tasya rājā śīrṣaṃ parimārjayed; atha sa puruṣo 'dhimānād, yāvād rājadvāraṃ gatvā, balasā taṃ rājakulaṃ praveṣṭum icched. atha te rājāmātyapārṣadyās taṃ puruṣaṃ gṛhṇīyur, bahubhiś ca prakārais tāḍayeyur.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> and bowing, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause, what the condition, that such wondrous miracles (<s>prātihārya</s>) are seen in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>?' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Suppose there were a certain man — restless, fickle, established in ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and possessiveness (<s>mamakāra</s>) — and he were poor. 3. The king pats his head; then that man, out of arrogance (<s>adhimāna</s>), goes as far as the royal gate and tries to force his way into the royal palace. Then the king's ministers and courtiers seize that man and beat him in many ways.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 163
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 163

body.text: 1. atha tena kālena tena samayena sa rājā śṛṇuyād etāṃ prakṛtiṃ: sa daridrapuruṣo balasābhyantaraṃ praveṣṭukāma. iti śrutvā cāsyaivaṃ bhaved: avaśyam ayaṃ mama ghātayitukāmaḥ. 2. tataḥ sa rājā ruṣṭas tān pārṣadyān evaṃ vaded: gacchantu bhavanta, etaṃ puruṣaṃ parvatavivaraṃ nītvā jīvitād vyaparopayatha sarvaparivāraṃ; 3. mātāpitṛputraduhitṛdāsīdāsakarmakarāṇāṃ ca vyasanam āpādayatha. 4. atha te sarve jīvitād vyavaropitāḥ, 5. tasya ca sarve svajanabandhuvargāḥ paramaśokaśalyasamarpitā bhaveyuḥ.
body.translated_text: 1. Then at that time and on that occasion, the king hears this report: 'That poor man tried to enter the inner palace by force.' Having heard this, the thought arises in him: 'Surely this man intends to kill me.' 2. Then the king, enraged, speaks thus to those courtiers: 'Go, sirs — take this man to a mountain crevasse and put him to death along with his entire retinue; 3. and bring ruin upon his mother, father, sons, daughters, female servants, male servants, and workers.' 4. Then they are all put to death, 5. and all his kinsmen and relatives are pierced by the dart of extreme grief.

body.text: SaSū(C) 164
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 164

body.text: 1. evam eva sarvaśūra tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ satvānān dharman deśayati. 2. tatra, yathā sa puruṣo 'dhimānika, evaṃ bālapṛthagjanās: tathāgataṃ rūpavarṇaliṃgasaṃsthānato nimittam udgṛhya, tathāgatakāyam iti saṃjānanti.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Just so, O <s>Sarvaśūra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. 2. Just as that man was arrogant, so too are foolish ordinary people (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>): grasping the <s>Tathāgata</s> by form, color, marks, and shape as a sign, they conceive that to be the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 165
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 165

body.text: 1. tatra te bahūn dharmāṃ cchrutvādhimāne patanti, nānāpralāpān pralapanti. 2. ahaṃkāramamakāreṇābhibhūtāḥ svayam eva dharmaṃ na śṛṇvanti na prakāśayanti. 3. yaḥ kaścit sūtraṃ vā gāthāṃ vāntaśo dṛṣṭāntaṃ vā teṣāṃ ārocayati, tat te na gṛhṇanti, na śrotram avadadhanti: vayaṃ svayaṃ jānīmaha iti: 4. tat kasya hetor? yathāpinamādhimānatvāt tena bāhuśrutyena pramādam āpadyante.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Having heard many teachings, they fall into conceit (<s>adhimāna</s>), uttering various kinds of prattle. 2. Overcome by ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and possessiveness (<s>mamakāra</s>), they themselves neither listen to the <s>Dharma</s> nor proclaim it. 3. When someone teaches them a <s>sūtra</s>, a verse (<s>gāthā</s>), or even a simile (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), they do not accept it, they do not lend their ear, saying: "We know by ourselves!" 4. Why is that? Because, through that very arrogance (<s>adhimāna</s>), through their much-learning (<s>bāhuśrutya</s>), they become heedless.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 166
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 166

body.text: 1. ye bālapṛthagjanaiḥ sārdhaṃ samavadhānaṃ kurvanti na te tathārūpaṃ dharmopasaṃhitaṃ vacanaṃ śroṣyanti; 2. te tena bāhuśrutyena pramattā bhaviṣyanti; 3. te tathārūpāḥ puruṣāḥ svakāvyāni sthāpayanti, svakāni granthānidānāni sthāpayanti; 4. te sarvalokaṃ cātmānaṃ ca visaṃpādayanti; 5. vyarthaṃ ca rāṣṭrapiṇḍaṃ prabhūtaṃ paribhokṣyanti, bhuktvā ca na samyak pariṇamayiṣyanti. 6. maraṇakālasamaye teṣāṃ mahāsantrāso bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Those who associate with foolish ordinary people (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>) will not hear such <s>Dharma</s>-connected speech; 2. they will become heedless through that much-learning. 3. Such men set up their own compositions (<s>kāvya</s>), establish their own texts and narratives (<s>grantha-nidāna</s>); 4. they ruin the entire world and themselves; 5. they will consume the abundant alms-food of the kingdom in vain, and having consumed it, will not properly digest it. 6. At the time of death, great terror will arise in them.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 167
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 167

body.text: 1. te ca satvās taṃ vakṣyanti: bahavas tvayā vayaṃ śilpajñānaṃ śikṣāpitāḥ kathaṃ tvaṃ svam ātmānaṃ na śaknuṣe saṃsthāpayituṃ? 2. sa teṣāṃ evaṃ vaden: na śakyaṃ mārṣā idānīm ātmānaṃ parisaṃsthāpayituṃ.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Those beings will say to him: "You taught us many skills and knowledge — how is it that you cannot save yourself?" 2. He will say to them: "It is not possible now, dear friends, to save oneself."'

body.text: SaSū(C) 168
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 168

body.text: 1. tatra te satvās, tasya tad bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā, nānāprakāraṃ paridevayiṣyanti. 2. yathā tasyaikapudgalasyārthena bahavo jñātisaṃghā jīvitād vyavaropitā anaparādhinaḥ, svakarmapratyayena, evam eva te satvā maraṇakālasamaye, teṣāṃ paridevatāṃ narakatiryagyoniparāyaṇaṃ ātmānaṃ samanupaśyante 'kalyāṇamitrasaṃsargahetoḥ. 3. tad ahaṃ yuṣmākaṃ brāhmaṇānām anyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthānām evaṃ vadāmi: mā yūyaṃ pramattā bhavatha! 4. tadyathāpināmājātapakṣaḥ śakunir na śaknoty ākāśe prakramituṃ devalokagamanāya, evam eva yuṣmābhir ahaṃkāramamakārasthitair na śakyaṃ nirvāṇaṃ anuprāptuṃ; na yuṣmākaṃ tathā ṛddhiḥ saṃvidyate. 5. tat kasya hetoḥ? karmaprakaraṇena yūyaṃ kukkuṭayonyā ivotpannāḥ. 6. na cireṇāyaṃ kāyo bhedanadharmā maraṇaparyavasāno bhaviṣyati. 7. maraṇakālasamaye nirāsvādanatā, paritasyanatā ca bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Those beings, hearing his words, will lament in various ways. 2. Just as through the affair of that one person, many kinsmen were put to death though guiltless — by the force of their own <s>karma</s> — just so, those beings, at the time of death, see themselves destined for hell and animal realms on account of association with bad spiritual friends (<s>akalyāṇamitra</s>). 3. Therefore I say to you <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, non-Buddhist wanderers, mendicants, peripatetics, and <s>Nirgranthas</s>: Do not be heedless! 4. Just as an unfledged bird cannot fly through the sky to reach the world of gods, even so, you who are established in ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and possessiveness (<s>mamakāra</s>) cannot attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s>; such supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) does not exist in you. 5. Why is that? By the course of <s>karma</s>, you are born as if from a hen\'s egg. 6. Before long, this body will be subject to dissolution, ending in death. 7. At the time of death, there will be tastelessness and anguish.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 169
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 169

body.text: 1. kim ayam asmābhir ātmabhāvaḥ sandhārito ye vayaṃ na devasukhaṃ na pratyanubhaviṣyāma, nāpi nirvāṇapadasthā bhaviṣyāmaḥ? 2. nirarthakam asmābhiḥ śarīram udvūḍhaṃ! 3. kā gatir asmābhiḥ kiṃ parāyaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati? 4. kutropapattiḥ, kutra vā nirodho bhaviṣyatīti?
body.translated_text: 1. '"Was this self-existence maintained by us in vain — we who shall neither experience the happiness of the gods nor attain the state of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>? 2. Purposelessly has this body been carried by us! 3. What destiny will be ours, what final goal? 4. Where will be our rebirth, and where our cessation?"'

body.text: SaSū(C) 170
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 170

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhagavāṃ punar api tān anyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthabrāhmaṇān āmantrayati: 2. mā yūyaṃ mārṣā ratnamayāj jaṃbudvīpān nirāśā bhaviṣyadhve! 3. mā yūyaṃ dharmaratnāt paribāhyā bhaviṣyatheti! 4. pṛcchatha yūyaṃ mārṣās tathāgataṃ yad yad evākāṃkṣathāha; ahaṃ yuṣmākaṃ sarvābhiprāyān paripūrayiṣyāmi.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> again addressed those non-Buddhist wanderers, mendicants, peripatetics, <s>Nirgranthas</s>, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>: 2. 'Do not, dear friends, become hopeless regarding the jewel-filled <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! 3. Do not become excluded from the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s>!' 4. 'Ask, dear friends, the <s>Tathāgata</s> whatever you wish; I shall fulfill all your intentions.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 171
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 171

body.text: 1. atha khalu te sarve brāhmaṇānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthā utthāyāsanebhya, ekāṃsāni cīvarāṇi pravṛtya, aṃjalayaḥ pragṛhya, bhagavantaṃ paripṛcchanti sma: 2. bahūni bhagavaṃ satvāni rātrindivas tathāgataḥ saṃsārāt parimocayati, na ca satvadhātor ūnatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā prajñāyate. 3. ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ yat te satvā samānā utpādanirodhaṃ darśayanti?
body.translated_text: 1. Then all those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, non-Buddhist wanderers, mendicants, peripatetics, and <s>Nirgranthas</s>, rising from their seats, arranging their cloaks over one shoulder, with palms joined, questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 2. 'Day and night, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> liberates many beings from <s>saṃsāra</s>, yet neither decrease nor increase of the realm of beings (<s>satvadhātu</s>) is perceived. 3. What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause, what the condition, that those beings, being the same, manifest arising and cessation?'

body.text: SaSū(C) 172
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 172

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisatvaṃ mahāsatvam āmantrayati sma: 2. mahāsannāhaṃ sannahyanti tīrthyā mahākaukṛtyavinodanārthāya. mahādharmolkājvālanāyamahāpraśnanidānaṃ paripṛcchanti. 3. paścime tu kāle na bhaviṣyanti daharā satvā vṛddhā vā ye utpādanirodhaṃ kariṣyanti. santi bhaiṣajyasena vṛddhā satvā daharā iva na kiṃcij jānanti.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 2. 'The <s>tīrthyas</s> (non-Buddhist ascetics) gird themselves with great armor for the purpose of dispelling great remorse. They inquire into the cause of questions regarding the blazing of the great torch of <s>Dharma</s>. 3. But in the last age there will be neither young beings nor old who will demonstrate arising and cessation. There are, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, old beings who, like the young, know nothing.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 173
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 173

body.text: 1. tadyathāpināma bhaiṣajyasena kaścid eva puruṣaḥ śiraḥ śocayeta, navakāni ca vastrāṇi pravṛṇuyāt sa ca gṛhād bahir niṣkrameta; 2. tam enaṃ satvā āmantrayanti: suprāvṛtāni te navakāni vastrāṇīti. 3. atha kaścid evāparaḥ satvo bhavet; sa śiraḥ śocayeta, purāṇakāni ca vastrāṇi prāvṛṇuyāt; tāni ca śithilakāni bhavanti, na ca śobhante. 4. sa ca puruṣaḥ susnātaśirā bhavati, vastraṃ cāsya na śobhate. 5. evam eva bhaiṣajyasena saṃti vṛddhā satvā ye jaṃbudvīpaṃ na śobhayanti. 6. daharās tu satvā utpādanirodhaṃ darśayanti.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Just as, for example, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a certain man might wash his head and put on new garments and go out from his house; 2. beings would address him: "Your new garments are well-worn!" 3. Then suppose there were another being; he too might wash his head but put on old garments; and those garments would be loose-fitting and not look fine. 4. That man has a well-washed head, but his garment does not look fine. 5. Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, there are old beings who do not adorn <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. 6. But young beings demonstrate arising and cessation.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 174
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 174

body.text: 1. atha khalu te sarve 'nyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthabrāhmaṇā utthāyāsanād, bhagavantam etad avocan: ko bhagavann asmākaṃ vṛddho vā daharo vā? 2. bhagavān āha: vṛddhā yūyaṃ! punaḥ punar narakatiryakpreteṣu duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ dṛṣṭvā tad adyāpi yūyaṃ tṛptiṃ nādhigacchatha!
body.translated_text: 1. Then all those other-<s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, ascetics, mendicants, <s>Nirgranthas</s>, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> rose from their seats and said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Which of us, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is old and which is young?' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You are the old ones! Again and again having experienced painful feelings in the hells, animal realms, and hungry ghost realms, even now you do not attain satisfaction!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 175
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 175

body.text: 1. atha khalu te sarve brāhmaṇānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthāḥ, sarve ca nāgarājāno bhagavantam etad avocan: na bhūyo bhagavann utsahāma saṃsāre duḥkhāṃ vedanām anubhavituṃ! 2. te cānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthabrāhmaṇā evam āhuḥ: na santi daharā satvā ye śaknuyur dharmatāṃ sākṣātkartum.
body.translated_text: 1. Then all those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, other-<s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, ascetics, mendicants, <s>Nirgranthas</s>, and all the <s>Nāga</s> kings said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'We can no longer endure experiencing painful feelings in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth), O <s>Bhagavān</s>!' 2. Those other-<s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, ascetics, mendicants, <s>Nirgranth</s> and <s>brāhmaṇa</s> ascetics said: 'There are no young beings who are able to directly realize the true nature of <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 176
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 176

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: paśya bhadanta bhagavan kiyad duradhimocyā ime satvāḥ! 2. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena, sāṃprataṃ tathāgataḥ sarvalokapratyakṣaṃ karoti.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'See, Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, how hard to convert these beings are!' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> will now make it manifest before the whole world.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 177
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 177

body.text: 1. atha khalu caturnavati koṭīsahasrāṇi navakānāṃ satvānāṃ te tathāgatasya purataḥ sthitāḥ. na ca tathāgataṃ vandanti, nālapanti, na saṃlapanti. 2. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yad ete satvā bhagavantaṃ nālapanti, na saṃlapanti, na vandanti, na ca bhagavantaṃ paripṛcchanti? 3. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena, satvā evaṃ vadanti: na śakyaṃ navakaiḥ satvair dharmatā sākṣātkartum. 4. ta ete bhaiṣajyasena navakāḥ satvā yuṣmābhir draṣṭavyāḥ. 5. te ca satvā evaṃ āhur: vayaṃ bhagavan navakāḥ satvā, vayaṃ sugata navakāḥ satvā! 6. bhagavān āha: eṣāṃ bho satvānāṃ lokapratyakṣaṃ, sāṃprataṃ svaśarīrāl lokasya pramāṇaṃ darśayatha.
body.translated_text: 1. Then ninety-four thousand <s>koṭis</s> of young beings stood before the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And they did not bow to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, did not speak, did not converse. 2. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the reason and condition that these beings do not speak to, do not converse with, do not bow to, and do not question the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' 3. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, beings say thus: "It is not possible for young beings to directly realize the true nature of dharmas." 4. These young beings, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, should be seen by you. 5. And those beings spoke thus: "We are young beings, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! We are young beings, O <s>Sugata</s>!" 6. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "For the sake of making it manifest to these beings and to the world, now from your own bodies show proof to the world."'

body.text: SaSū(C) 178
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 178

body.text: 1. tena khalu punaḥ kālena tena samayena caturnavati koṭīsahasrāṇi navakānāṃ satvānāṃ, kāyasya bhedād antarīkṣe sthitvā, daśabhūmipratilabdhā abhūvan. 2. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: sulabdhālābhā bhagavann īdṛśāḥ satvāḥ ye saṃsāre parikṣayāya paryādānāya vīryam ārabhante. 3. adyaiva bhagavann ime satvā utpannāḥ, adyaiva bhagavann ime satvāḥ parimuktāḥ, adyaiva sarve daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā dṛṣṭāḥ.
body.translated_text: 1. Then at that time and occasion, ninety-four thousand <s>koṭis</s> of young beings, upon the dissolution of their bodies, standing in mid-air, attained the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages). 2. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Well-gained is the gain of these beings, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, who exert effort for the exhaustion and cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s>. 3. Today itself, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, these beings have arisen; today itself, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, these beings are liberated; today itself they are seen as established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 179
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 179

body.text: 1. atha khalu sarvabrāhmaṇānyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthā, nāgarājāno 'pi, mārāś ca pāpīmān saparivāra upasaṃkrānto vicakṣuṣkaraṇāya, sarve bhagavantam etad avocann: iha vayaṃ bhagavans tathāgatasyāntikam upasaṃkrāntā vicakṣuṣkaraṇāya. 2. te vayaṃ bhagavann, iman dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā, prasādapratilabdhā abhūma buddhe ca dharme ca. 3. tatrāsmākaṃ bhagavan sarveṣām evaṃ bhagavaty: evaṃrūpaṃ buddhasukhaṃ pratilabhemahe! 4. evaṃrūpāś ca tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loke bhavemaḥ.
body.translated_text: 1. Then all the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, other-<s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, ascetics, mendicants, <s>Nirgranthas</s>, and also the <s>Nāga</s> kings, and <s>Māra</s> the Evil One with his retinue, approached to gain the eye of wisdom, and all said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Here we have approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> to gain the eye of wisdom, O <s>Bhagavān</s>. 2. We, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, having heard this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma), have gained faith in the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s>. 3. May we all, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, attain such <s>Buddha</s>-happiness! 4. And may we become such <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones in the world!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 180
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 180

body.text: 1. bhagavān āha: evam etad bhadramukhā! yathā yūyaṃ tathāgatasyāntikam upasaṃkrāntāḥ, tairyuṣmābhir imaṃ saṃghāṭaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā, ānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ utpāditaṃ. 2. tena yūyaṃ bhadramukhāḥ kuśalamūlena na cireṇa kālenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbotsyadhve. abhisaṃbhotsyadhve.
body.translated_text: 1. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So it is, O fair-faced ones! Just as you have approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by you, having heard this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, the mind has been generated toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). 2. Therefore, O fair-faced ones, through that root of merit, before long you shall fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. You shall attain full awakening.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 181
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 181

body.text: 1. samanantarabhāṣitā ca tathāgateneyaṃ vāg, atha teṣāṃ sarveṣām anyatīrthikacarakaparibrājakanigranthabrāhmaṇānām anutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilābho 'bhūt, 2. sarve ca daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā bodhisatvāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ, 3. sarve ca te bodhisatvā, upary antarīkṣe sapta tālān vaihāyasam abhyudgamya, saptaratnamayāni kūṭāgārāṇi tathāgatasyopanāmayanti, 4. sarve ca nānāvikurvādhiṣṭhānardhyabhisaṃkārān abhisaṃskurvanti. 5. atha te, bhagavata upari mūrdhni sthitvā bhagavantaṃ nānāpuṣpair abhyavakiranti. 6. tathāgatāṃś ca manasikurvanti, svakāye ca buddhasaṃjñām utpādayanty. 7. anekāni ca devaputrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi divyapuṣpais tathāgatam abhyavakiranti sma.
body.translated_text: 1. No sooner had this word been spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> than all those other-<s>tīrthika</s> wanderers, ascetics, mendicants, <s>Nirgranthas</s>, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> attained the acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>), 2. and all became <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s>. 3. And all those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, rising up into the sky to the height of seven palm trees, offered pavilions made of the seven precious substances to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, 4. and all performed various miraculous displays of supernatural power. 5. Then, standing above the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s head, they showered the <s>Bhagavān</s> with various flowers. 6. And they contemplated the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and generated the perception of a <s>Buddha</s> in their own bodies. 7. And many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) showered the <s>Tathāgata</s> with celestial flowers.

body.text: SaSū(C) 182
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 182

body.text: evaṃ ca vācam abhāśanta: mahālābhaḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ! mahākṣetro, lokanāthaḥ; samādhibalādhānaprāptaḥ; vijño, vijñārthikaḥ, yaḥ īdṛśān satvān saṃsārād anupūrveṇopāyakauśalyena parimocayaty: ekena subhāṣitamātreṇa etāvanti satvāni saṃsārāt parimucyante!
body.translated_text: And they spoke these words: 'Great is the gain of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>! Great is his field, the Protector of the World; he who has attained the power of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); the wise one, seeker of wisdom, who liberates such beings from <s>saṃsāra</s> gradually through skillful means — by a single well-spoken utterance, so many beings are freed from <s>saṃsāra</s>!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 183
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 183

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatva utthāyāsanād, ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā, dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya, bhagavantam etad avocat: 2. ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yad ete devaputrā evaṃ vācaṃ niścārayanti, bahūni ca rdhyabhisaṃskārān kurvanti, bahūni ca tathāgatasya varṇān abhisaṃstuvanti sma? 3. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu kulaputra, na hi te māṃ stuvanti, svakāyam eva stunvanti; 4. svakāyam eva dharmarājāsane sthāpayiṣyanti; 5. svakāyam evāgradharmāsane pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyanti; 6. svakāyād eva dharmaraśmin niścārayiṣyanti; 7. sarvabuddhaparigṛhītāś ca bhaviṣyanty anuttarāsyāḥ samyaksaṃbodher abhisaṃbodhāya, abhisaṃbudhya ca dharman deśayiṣyanti.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 2. 'What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the reason and condition that these <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) utter such words, perform many miraculous displays, and praise the many virtues of the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' 3. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, son of good family, for they do not praise me — they praise their own bodies; 4. they will establish their own bodies on the throne of the <s>Dharma</s> king; 5. they will establish their own bodies on the foremost seat of the <s>Dharma</s>; 6. from their own bodies they will emit the rays of the <s>Dharma</s>; 7. and they shall be embraced by all <s>Buddhas</s> for the full awakening to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and having fully awakened, they shall teach the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 184
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 184

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: bahavo bhadanta bhagavan satvāḥ, bahavo bhadanta sugata satvā rātrindivaṃ parimucyante; tad adyāpi satvānāṃ kṣayo na bhavati. 2. bhagavān āha: sādhu sādhu bhaiṣajyasena yas tvaṃ tathāgatam etam arthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase. śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena! 3. tadyathāpināma bhaiṣajyasena kaścid eva puruṣo bhaved, āḍhyo, mahādhano, mahābhogaḥ, bahudhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgārasamanvāgataḥ, bahudāsadāsīkarmakarapauruṣeyāni cāsya syur, bahūni ca dhanaskandhāni, bahūni ca kṣetrārāmāṇi saṃvidyeran, bahūni ca dhanadhānyāni; 4. sa ca puruṣo vasantakāle sarvāṇi tāni dhanadhānyāni vāpayet. 5. atha yāvad apareṇa kālasamayena sarvāṇi tāni bījāni paripacyeran, sa paripakvānīti viditvā, tataḥ sa puruṣas tāni dhanadhānyāni gṛhasyābhyantare pṛthak pṛthak sthāpayati; sthāpayitvā paribhuṃkte. 6. yāvad vasantakāle punar eva bījāni vāpayati.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Many, Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, are the beings; many, Venerable <s>Sugata</s>, are the beings who are liberated day and night — yet even now the depletion of beings does not occur.' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, that you think this matter should be asked of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>! (3) Suppose, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, there were some man, wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, endowed with many storehouses of wealth, grain, and treasuries, and he had many male and female servants, workers, and attendants, and many heaps of wealth, and many fields and gardens were to be found, and many stores of grain. (4) And that man, in the spring season, would sow all those grains and seeds. (5) Then, at a later time and season, when all those seeds had ripened, knowing them to be ripened, that man would store those grains separately inside his house; and having stored them, he would consume them. (6) Until in the spring season he would again sow the seeds.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 185
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 185

body.text: 1. evam eva bhaiṣajyasena ime satvāḥ, pūrvaṃ śubhaṃ karma kṛtvā, paścāt teṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ parikṣayāt, punaḥ punar api puṇyakṣetram anveṣante, kuśalamūlāny avaropayanti. 2. kuśalamūlāny avaropayitvā tatra ca kuśaladharme pratipattyā saṃpādayanti. 3. pratipattisaṃpannā sarvadharmān vardhayanti. 4. sarvadharmān vardhayitvā prītiprāmodyam utpādayanti, 5. tena ca prītiprāmodyacittena bhaiṣajyasenānekāni kalpakoṭīsahasrāṇi na nāśyante. 6. evam eva bhaiṣajyasena prathamacittotpādiko bodhisatvo na kadācid vināśadharmā bhavati, saṃkṣiptena sarvadharmān prajānāti.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, these beings, having formerly done good <s>karma</s>, afterwards, upon the exhaustion of those <s>karmas</s>, again and again seek a field of merit (<s>puṇyakṣetra</s>) and plant roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). (2) Having planted roots of merit, they accomplish through practice in those wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. (3) Accomplished in practice, they increase all <s>dharmas</s>. (4) Having increased all <s>dharmas</s>, they generate joy and gladness (<s>prītiprāmodya</s>). (5) And with that mind of joy and gladness, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, for many thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> they are not destroyed. (6) Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has generated the first thought [of awakening] (<s>prathamacittotpādika</s>) is never subject to destruction; in brief, he comprehends all <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 186
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 186

body.text: āha: 1. kathaṃ bhagavan prathamacittotpādiko bodhisatvaḥ svapnaṃ paśyati? 2. bhagavān āha: bahūni bhaiṣajyasena prathamacittotpādiko bodhisatvaḥ svapnāntare bhayāni paśyati. 3. tat kasya hetor? yadā svapnāntare bhayāni paśyati, tadā sarvapāpakāni karmāṇi pariśodhayati. 4. na śakyaṃ bhaiṣajyasena pāpakarmaṇā satvena tīvraṃ duḥkham apanayitum, na ca pāpena svapnena dṛṣṭenāsya bhayaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: He said: (1) 'How, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has generated the first thought [of awakening] see dreams?' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Many, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, are the fears that a first-thought <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees within dreams. (3) For what reason? When he sees fears within dreams, then he purifies all evil <s>karmas</s>. (4) It is not possible, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, for a being with evil <s>karma</s> to remove intense suffering, nor does fear arise for him from seeing an evil dream.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 187
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 187

body.text: 1.bhaiṣajyasena āha: katamāni bhagavan prathamacittotpādiko bodhisatvaḥ svapnāntare bhayāni paśyati? 2. bhagavān āha: agniṃ bhaiṣajyasena prajvalitaṃ paśyati. tatas tena bodhisatvenaivaṃ veditavyaṃ: sarvakleśā me dagdhāḥ. 3. dvitīyaṃ bhaiṣajyasena udakaṃ paśyati, luḍitaṃ, saṃpraluḍitaṃ. tatra tena prathamacittotpādikena bodhisatvena na bhetavyaṃ. 4. tat kasya hetoḥ? evaṃ hi bhaiṣajyasena, sarvapāpakṣayaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati. 5. tṛtīyaṃ bhaiṣajyasena prathamacittotpādiko bodhisatvaḥ svapnaṃ paśyati mahābhayaṃ. 6. āha: katamaṃ bhagavan?
body.translated_text: (1) <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said: 'Which fears, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does a first-thought <s>Bodhisattva</s> see within dreams?' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'He sees a blazing fire, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>. Then that <s>Bodhisattva</s> should understand thus: "All my defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) are burnt." (3) Second, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, he sees water, rolling, surging. In that case, that first-thought <s>Bodhisattva</s> should not be afraid. (4) For what reason? Thus, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the exhaustion of all evil has been accomplished. (5) Third, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the first-thought <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees a great fear in a dream.' (6) He said: 'Which, O <s>Bhagavān</s>?'

body.text: SaSū(C) 188
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 188

body.text: 1. bhagavān āha: svaśarīre śīrṣaṃ muṇḍitaṃ paśyati. tatra tena bodhisatvena na bhetavyaṃ. 2. tenaivaṃ cittam utpādayitavyaṃ: rāgadveṣamohāni me muṇḍitāni bhavanti, 3. ṣaḍgatikaṃ ca me saṃsāraṃ parājitaṃ bhaviṣyati. 4. na hi tasya narakāvāso bhaviṣyati, na tiryakṣu, na preteṣu vā, nāsureṣu vā, na nāgeṣu, na deveṣu. 5. pariśuddheṣu bhaiṣajyasena buddhakṣetreṣu prathamacittotpādiko bodhisatva upapattiṃ pratigṛhṇāti.
body.translated_text: (1) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'He sees his own head shaved. In that case, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> should not be afraid. (2) He should generate this thought: "My passion (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) have been shaved off." (3) "And my six-destinied <s>saṃsāra</s> will be defeated." (4) For he will not have a dwelling in the hells, nor among animals, nor among <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), nor among <s>Asuras</s>, nor among <s>Nāgas</s>, nor among gods. (5) In purified <s>Buddha</s>-fields, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the first-thought <s>Bodhisattva</s> accepts rebirth.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 189
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 189

body.text: 1. bhaiṣajyasena, paścime kāle paścime samaye, yadi kaścit satvo bodhau cittaṃ pariṇamayiṣyati, tena mahatī paribhāṣaṇā draṣṭavyā, paribhūtavāsaś ca bhaviṣyati. 2. tatra tena bhaiṣajyasena na parikhedacittam utpādayitavyaṃ, na viṣīditavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: (1) '<s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, in the last time, in the last age, if some being will dedicate his mind to awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), he will see great ridicule, and will experience a dwelling of contempt. (2) In that case, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, he should not generate a mind of weariness, nor should he be dejected.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 190
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 190

body.text: 1. bahavo bhaiṣajyasena mayā dharmā deśitāḥ. 2. mayā ca bhaiṣajyasenānekāni kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi duṣkaracaryā cīrṇā. 3. na mayā bhaiṣajyasena rājyabhogārthāya vā, vṛttibhogārthāya vā, aiśvaryabhogārthāya vā duṣkaracaryā cīrṇā; svabhāvadharmāvabodhāya bhaiṣajyasena mayā duṣkaracaryā cīrṇā. 4. na ca me tāvad anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ prāptā yāvan na mayāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ śrutaḥ: 5. yasmiṃs tu bhaiṣajyasena kālasamaye mayāyaṃ saṃghāṭo dharmaparyāyaḥ śrutaḥ, tatraiva divase anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃbuddhā. 6. gaṃbhīro 'yaṃ bhaiṣajyasena dharmaparyāyaḥ. 7. durlabho 'sya dharmaparyāyasya śravaḥ. 8. paramadurlabho bhaiṣajyasena tathāgatānām utpādaḥ. paramadurlabho bhaiṣajyasenāsya dharmaparyāyasya dhārakaḥ.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Many <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, have been taught by me. (2) And by me, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, for many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, difficult practices (<s>duṣkaracaryā</s>) were undertaken. (3) Not for the sake of royal pleasures, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, nor for the sake of livelihood pleasures, nor for the sake of lordly pleasures did I undertake difficult practices; for the realization of the intrinsic nature of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, I undertook difficult practices. (4) And I did not attain supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) until I heard this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. (5) But when, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, at that time and season, I heard this <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, on that very day I fully awakened to supreme perfect awakening. (6) This <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, is profound. (7) The hearing of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> is rare. (8) Supremely rare, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, is the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Supremely rare, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, is a keeper of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 191
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 191

body.text: 1. ye te iman dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti, sarve te 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyante. 2. kalpasahasraṃ bhaiṣajyasena saṃsārāt paścānmukhaṃ kariṣyanti. 3. pariṣuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pratilapsyante, nirodhamārgaṃ ca prajñāsyanti. 4. bhavyāś ca te niśrayaṃ prajñātuṃ, bhavyāḥ kuśalasthānaṃ prajñatuṃ, bhavyā abhijñākuśalasthānaṃ prajñatum, bhavyāḥ kuśalasthānanirodhaṃ prajñātum.
body.translated_text: (1) 'All those who will hear this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> will fully awaken to supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). (2) For a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, they will turn away from <s>saṃsāra</s>. (3) They will obtain a purified <s>Buddha</s>-field, and they will comprehend the path of cessation (<s>nirodha-mārga</s>). (4) And they will be capable of comprehending the basis, capable of comprehending the place of what is wholesome (<s>kuśala-sthāna</s>), capable of comprehending the place of direct knowledge (<s>abhijñā-kuśala-sthāna</s>), and capable of comprehending the cessation of the place of what is wholesome.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 192
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 192

body.text: 1. nirodham eva bhaiṣajyasena kimartham ucyate? 2. āha: artha ucyate bhagavan dharmasthānam. 3. bhagavān āha: katamaṃ bhaiṣajyasena dharmasthānaṃ? 4. āha: dharma ucyate bhagavann ārabdhavīryatā, ārabdhaśīlatā; śīlasamanvāgamatā dharmanidhānam ity ucyate. idaṃ bhagavan dharmanidhānaṃ saṃbhavati. 5. bhagavān āha: sādhu sādhu bhaiṣajyasena yas tvaṃ tathāgatam etam arthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase.
body.translated_text: (1) '<s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, for what purpose exactly is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) spoken of?' (2) He said: 'What is spoken of, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the abode of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmasthāna</s>).' (3) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Which, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, is the abode of <s>Dharma</s>?' (4) He said: '<s>Dharma</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is said to be the state of exerted energy, the state of exerted morality; the endowment of morality is called the treasury of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharma-nidhāna</s>). This, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is where the treasury of <s>Dharma</s> arises.' (5) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, that you think this matter should be asked of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 193
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 193

body.text: 1. āha: kena kāreṇa na bhagavaṃs tathāgatā loka utpadyante? 2. bhagavān āha: ye bhaiṣajyasena bāhuśrutyasamanvāgamaṃ prajānanti, te tathāgatānām utpādaṃ prajānanti. 3. te tathāgatānām utpādaṃ jñātvā, idaṃ tathāgatānām utpāde sukhasthānaṃ prajānanti. 4. yadā ca tathāgatā loka utpadyante, tadā satvā sarvadharmān prajānanti. laukikalokottarān dharmān prajānanti. laukikalokottarāṇi jñānāni prajānanti.
body.translated_text: (1) He said: 'For what reason, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise in the world?' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Those, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, who comprehend the endowment of great learning, they comprehend the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. (3) Having known the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, they comprehend this place of happiness in the arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. (4) And when <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise in the world, then beings comprehend all <s>dharmas</s>. They comprehend worldly and supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. They comprehend worldly and supramundane knowledges.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 194
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 194

body.text: 1. āha: jñānam evaṃ jñātvā, katamaṃ nirvāṇaṃ prajānanti? 2. bhagavān āha: dharmam eva bhaiṣajyasena prajānanti. 3. dharmam eva jñātvā, evam eva bhaiṣajyasena dharmasaṃgrahaṃ prajānatāṃ prathamo lābha utpadyate. 4. yathāśrutaṃ gṛhya, dhārmika eva lābho bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: (1) He said: 'Having thus known knowledge, which <s>nirvāṇa</s> do they comprehend?' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'They comprehend the <s>Dharma</s> itself, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>. (3) Having known the <s>Dharma</s> itself, just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, for those who comprehend the collection of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmasaṃgraha</s>), the first gain arises. (4) Taking what has been heard, the gain will be in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dhārmika</s>).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 195

tadyathāpināma bhaiṣajyasena kaścid eva puruṣo vāṇijako bhavet. sa, lābhahetor gacchan, parakyasvakasya suvarṇasya puruṣabhārasahasraṃ gṛhītvā, gacchet. 2. tasya tau mātāpitarāv evam āhutuḥ: 3. śṛṇu putra, idaṃ suvarṇasya puruṣabhārasahasraṃ gṛhītvā parakyasvakasya ca, tat tvayedaṃ suvarṇaṃ sugṛhītaṃ kartavyaṃ, na ca kiṃcid ato vināśayitavyaṃ. mahālābhaṃ kṛtvā, suvarṇaṃ eva sugṛhītaṃ kuru, tad asmākaṃ mahālābho bhaviṣyati, sukhaṃ ca jīviṣyāmaḥ. 4. sa ca putras tau mātāpitarāv evaṃ vaded: evaṃ kariṣyāmi, ity uktvā, sa vāṇijakaḥ suvarṇaṃ gṛhītvā gacched. atha sa vāṇijakaḥ pramādād yāvan māsamātreṇa sarvaṃ suvarṇaṃ vināśayed vilayaṃ kuryāt.
body.translated_text: 1. Just as, for example, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, there might be a certain man, a merchant. He, going for the sake of profit, having taken a thousand man-loads of gold belonging to others and to himself, might depart. 2. His mother and father said to him thus: 3. 'Listen, son — having taken this thousand man-loads of gold, both others' and your own, you must keep this gold well-guarded, and nothing of it should be destroyed. Having made a great profit, keep the gold well-guarded; then there will be great profit for us, and we shall live happily.' 4. That son said to his mother and father thus: 'I shall do so.' Having said this, the merchant, taking the gold, departed. Then that merchant, through carelessness, within merely a month, destroyed and squandered all the gold.

body.text: SaSū(C) 196

1. atha sa puruṣaś cintāyāsam āpannaḥ, śokaśalyenāviddhahṛdayaḥ; sahrīr apatrāpyena ca svagṛhaṃ na paraviśeta. 2. tasya tau mātāpitarau śṛṇuyātāṃ: evaṃ yuvābhyāṃ putreṇa tat suvarṇaṃ sarvaṃ vināśitam. iti śrutvā nirāśībhūtau; śokaśalyenābhyāhatahṛdayau, vastrāṇi pāṭayataḥ, śocataḥ krandataḥ. 3. evaṃ ca paridevataḥ: duṣputro 'smākaṃ gṛhe putrarūpeṇotpannaḥ. sakalaṃ eva gṛhaṃ vināśītavān. asmākam anāthaṃ kṛtvā, dāsau karmakarau kṛtau. 4. tasya tau mātāpitarau, cintāparigatahṛdayau, nirāśau, kālagatau. 5. tatas tena putreṇa śrutaṃ: matāpitarau me, nirāśau kālagatau. so 'pi putro, nirāśa eva, kālagataḥ.
body.translated_text: 1. Then that man, fallen into anxiety and distress, his heart pierced by the arrow of grief, out of shame and embarrassment did not return to his own home. 2. His mother and father would hear: 'All that gold has been destroyed by your son.' Having heard, they became without hope; their hearts struck by the arrow of grief, they tore their clothes, wept, and lamented. 3. And they mourned thus: 'An evil son was born in our house in the form of a son. He has destroyed our entire household. Having made us destitute, he has made us slaves and laborers.' 4. Those mother and father, their hearts overcome by worry, without hope, passed away. 5. Then that son heard: 'My mother and father have passed away without hope.' That son too, without hope, passed away.

body.text: SaSū(C) 197

1. evam eva bhaiṣajyasena tathāgato 'py etam arthaṃ bhāṣate: 2. ye satvā mama śāsane na prasīdanti te nirāśībhūtā maraṇakālasamaye, śokaśalyābhyāhatahṛdayā, mahādharmaratnabahiṣkṛtāḥ kālaṃ kurvanti, 3. yathā tau mātāpitarau nirāśau śocataḥ, paridevataḥ, suvarṇahetoḥ śokaśalyābhyāhatahṛdayau, parakyasvakena suvarṇena śokaśalyaparigatau, cintām āpadya kālagatau.
[SaSū(C) 198] 1. evam eva bhaiṣajyasena, ye mama śasane na prasīdanti, paścān maraṇakālasamaye, paritapyamānāḥ paridevanto duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti, 2. pūrvakṛtāni ca puṇyāni paribhuktvā, na bhūyo 'nyāni puṇyāni kurvanti sukṣetragatāni. 3. teṣāṃ śokaśalyaparigatahṛdayānāṃ, tena kālena tena samayena, narakatiryagyoniyamalokopapattiṃ ghorāṃ dāruṇān dṛṣṭvā maraṇakālasamaye evaṃ bhavati: 4. ko me trātā bhaved? yad ahaṃ narakatiryakpretayamalokaṃ na paśyeyan, na ca tāṃ duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayeyaṃ!
body.translated_text: 1. Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> also speaks on this matter: 2. Those beings who do not have faith in my teaching, at the time of death they become without hope, their hearts struck by the arrow of grief, excluded from the great <s>Dharma</s>-treasure, they pass away; 3. just as those mother and father, without hope, weeping, lamenting, their hearts struck by the arrow of grief on account of the gold, overwhelmed by worry on account of the gold belonging to others and themselves, died after falling into anxiety. [198] 1. Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, those who do not have faith in my teaching, afterward at the time of death, burning with anguish, lamenting, they experience painful sensation; 2. and having exhausted the merit previously accumulated, they do not again produce other merit planted in fertile fields. 3. For them, their hearts overcome by the arrow of grief, at that time and on that occasion, upon seeing the terrible, dreadful prospect of rebirth in the hells, animal realms, <s>Yama</s>'s world, and among <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), at the time of death it occurs to them: 4. 'Who will be my savior, so that I may not see the hells, animal realms, <s>preta</s> realm, and <s>Yama</s>'s world, and may not experience that painful sensation!'

children.text: SaSū(C) 199
1. tasya mātāpitarāv evam āhatuḥ: kiṃ kariṣyāma putraka? gāthābhiś cāddhyābhāṣataḥ:
children.translated_text: 1. His mother and father said to him thus: 'What shall we do, dear son?' And they addressed him in verses:

children.text: (1) grahītuṃ śakyate naiva vyādhir duḥkhaṃ mahābhayaṃ /
children.translated_text: (1) 'Disease, suffering, and great fear cannot be seized;

children.text: nāsti te maraṇaṃ putra glānasya maraṇād bhayaṃ //
children.translated_text: there is no death for you, O son — for one who is ill, the fear comes from death.

body.text: mokṣo bhaviṣyate tubhyaṃ vyādhibhyo bhayabhairavāt /
body.translated_text: Liberation from diseases and from terrible fear will be yours.'

children.text: 2. putra āha:
children.translated_text: 2. The son said:

children.text: (2) niruddhyate me vijñānaṃ kāyo me pīḍyate bhṛśam /
children.translated_text: (2) 'My consciousness is being obstructed; my body is being tormented severely;

children.text: sarve aṅgāni duḥkhanti mṛtyuṃ paśyāmi ātmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: all my limbs are in pain — I see my own death.'

children.text: (3) na paśyataś cakṣuṣī me karṇau me na śṛṇonti ca /
children.translated_text: (3) 'My eyes do not see; my ears do not hear;

children.text: śrotraṃ punar na lapsyāmi na kāyaḥ saṃsahiṣyati //
children.translated_text: I shall not regain my hearing; my body will not endure.'

children.text: (4) aṅgamaṃgāni mucyaṃti kāṣṭhā iva acetanāḥ /
children.translated_text: (4) 'My limbs and members are falling apart, like logs, without consciousness;

children.text: visvādayasi me amba nāgataṃ maraṇaṃ tava //
children.translated_text: you try to console me, O mother, [but] death has not yet come to you!'

children.text: 3. mātā āha:
children.translated_text: 3. The mother said:

children.text: (5) vaktuṃ nārhasi putraivaṃ mā me trāsaparāṃ kuru /
children.translated_text: (5) 'You should not speak thus, O son! Do not cause me to be filled with terror;

children.text: kāyaṃ tava jvarākrāntaṃ viprakārāṇi paśyasi //
children.translated_text: your body is seized by fever — you see [mere] disturbances.'

children.text: 4. putra āha:
children.translated_text: 4. The son said:

children.text: (6) na paśyāmi jvaraṃ kāye na ca vyādhir na duḥkhati /
children.translated_text: (6) 'I do not see fever in my body, nor disease — it is not [merely] painful;

children.text: paśyāmi maranaṃ ghoraṃ hataṃ kāyaṃ ca me bhṛśam //
children.translated_text: I see terrible death — my body has been severely destroyed.'

children.text: (7) paśyāmi ātmanā sarvaṃ kāyaṃ duḥkhaprapīḍitaṃ /
children.translated_text: (7) 'I see with my own [eyes] my entire body tormented by suffering;

children.text: (8) gacchāmi kasya śaraṇaṃ ko me trātā bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: (8) to whose refuge shall I go? Who will be my savior?'

children.text: mātāpitā vadet putra devakrodhaṃ hi te bhavet /
children.translated_text: The mother and father said: 'O son, this must be the wrath of a deity;

children.text: (9) devebhyo yajanaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ svastir bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: (9) having performed a sacrifice to the deities, then well-being will come.'

children.text: putra āha:
children.translated_text: The son said:

children.text: kariṣyathā yūyam eva yena svastir bhaven mama /
children.translated_text: 'Do it yourselves — that by which my well-being may come;

children.text: (10) śīghraśīghraṃ ca gatvā vai pṛcchathā devapālakam //
children.translated_text: (10) go very quickly and ask the temple guardian!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 200

1. atha tasya tau mātāpitarau, devakulaṃ gatvā, devasya dhūpaṃ dāpayanti. 2. atha sa devapālako, devasya dhūpaṃ datvā, evaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate; 3. devas te kruddhaḥ; devasyopakāraḥ kartavyaḥ, yajanaṃ kartavyaṃ, tatra paśur ghātayitavyaḥ, puruṣaś ca ghātayitavyaḥ; tatas te putro vyādheḥ parimokṣyate. 4. atha tau mātāpitarau cintayataḥ: kathaṃ kariṣyāmo? daridrāś cāsma. 5. yadi devo na prasīdati, tad asmākaṃ putraḥ kālaṃ kariṣyati; 6. atha vā prasādaṃ kuryāt, tad vayaṃ paramadaridrāḥ. paśuṃ puruṣaṃ cānayāma.
body.translated_text: 1. Then his mother and father, having gone to the temple, had incense offered to the deity. 2. Then the temple guardian, having offered incense to the deity, spoke this word: 3. 'The deity is angered with you; service must be rendered to the deity, a sacrifice must be performed — therein an animal must be slaughtered and a person must be killed; then your son will be freed from the disease.' 4. Then those mother and father thought: 'What shall we do? We are poor.' 5. 'If the deity is not appeased, then our son will pass away;' 6. 'but if he were to be appeased, then we who are utterly destitute — let us bring an animal and a person.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 201

1. atha tau śīghraśīghraṃ svagṛhaṃ gatvā, yat kiṃcid gṛhe pariṣkāraṃ saṃvidyate, tat sarvaṃ vikrīya, paśukrayārthe gacchataḥ. 2. atha tāvad anyataraṃ puruṣam evaṃ vadeyuḥ: dehi bhoḥ puruṣa suvarṇam asmākaṃ yācitaṃ; 3. yadi śaknumo daśame divase punar api dātuṃ, tac chobhanam; 4. atha na śaknumo dātuṃ, tad vayaṃ tava dāsā bhaviṣyāmaḥ, karmakarāḥ. 5. tau ca taṃ suvarṇaṃ gṛhītvā gaccheyuḥ puruṣaṃ kretuṃ.
body.translated_text: 1. Then those two, going quickly to their own home, whatever furnishings were found in the house, selling all of that, went to purchase an animal. 2. Then they said to a certain man: 'Give us, good sir, gold on loan; 3. if we are able to repay it on the tenth day, that would be well; 4. but if we are unable to repay, then we shall become your slaves, your laborers.' 5. And having taken that gold, they went to purchase a person.

body.text: SaSū(C) 202

1. tābhyāṃ puruṣaḥ krītaḥ; 2. sa ca puruṣo na jānīyād yan: mām ete jīvitād vyavaropayiṣyanti. 3. atha tau mātāpitarau, saṃmoham āpannau, na bhūyaḥ svagṛhaṃ praviṣṭau; 4. tau devakulaṃ gatvā devapalakam āmantrayanti: śīghram idānīṃ yajanaṃ kuruṣva! 5. atha tau mātāpitarau svayam eva taṃ paśuṃ ghātayataḥ, taṃ ca puruṣaṃ jīvitād vyavaropayataḥ. 6. tataḥ sa devapālaka ārabdho yajñaṃ yajanāya medaṃ prajvālayati. 7. tataḥ sa devo 'vatīrya evaṃ kathayati: tava putro mayā parigṛhītā iti. 8. tatas tau mātāpitarau, prītiprāmodyena sphuṭāv, āhatuḥ: varaṃ putro jīvatu, vayaṃ dāsā bhaviṣyāmaḥ. 9. tatas tau mātāpitarau nivartya suyaṣṭaṃ devaṃ kṛtvā, yāvat svagṛhaṃ gatvā, tadā taṃ putraṃ kālagataṃ paśyanti. 10. tatas tau mātāpitarau, mahatā duḥkhadaurmanasyena śokaśalyenāviddhahṛdayau, nirāśībhūtau tatraiva kālagatau. 11. evam eva bhaiṣajyasenākalyāṇamitrasaṃsargatā draṣṭavyā.
body.translated_text: 1. A person was purchased by them. 2. And that person did not know that: 'These will deprive me of life.' 3. Then those mother and father, having fallen into delusion, no longer entered their own home. 4. Going to the temple, they addressed the temple guardian: 'Perform the sacrifice now quickly!' 5. Then those mother and father themselves slaughtered the animal and deprived the person of life. 6. Then the temple guardian began to ignite the fat for the sacrificial offering. 7. Then the deity, having descended, spoke thus: 'Your son has been accepted by me.' 8. Then those mother and father, bursting with joy and delight, said: 'May our son live — we shall be slaves!' 9. Then those mother and father, having turned back after completing the sacrifice to the deity, when they went to their own home, they saw that their son had already passed away. 10. Then those mother and father, struck by the arrow of grief with great suffering and mental anguish, their hearts pierced, becoming without hope, died right there. 11. Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, should the association with bad spiritual friends (<s>akalyāṇamitra</s>) be understood.

body.text: SaSū(C) 203

1. āha: pṛcchāmi tāvad bhagavan: kutas bhagavan teṣāṃ satvānām upapattiḥ? 2. bhagavān āha: alaṃ, ma me bhaiṣajyasena paripṛccha! 3. āha: pṛcchāmi bhagavan, pṛcchāmi sugata! 4. bhagavān āha: tatra bhaiṣajyasena mātā raurave mahānarake upapannā, pitā saṃghāte mahānarake upapannaḥ, putras tapane mahānarake upapannaḥ, devapālako mahāvīcau mahānarake upapannaḥ.
body.translated_text: 1. He said: 'I ask the <s>Bhagavān</s>: where, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, were those beings reborn?' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Enough — do not ask me, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>!' 3. He said: 'I ask, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! I ask, O <s>Sugata</s>!' 4. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'In that case, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: the mother was reborn in the <s>Raurava</s> great hell, the father was reborn in the <s>Saṃghāta</s> great hell, the son was reborn in the <s>Tapana</s> great hell, and the temple guardian was reborn in the great <s>Avīci</s> hell.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 204
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 204

body.text: 1. āha: anaparādhikasya bhagavan puruṣasya, kutropapattiḥ, ko 'syābhisaṃparāyaḥ? 2. bhagavān āha: iha bhaiṣajyasenānaparādhikasya puruṣasya trāyastriṃśānān devānām sahabhāvyatāyām upapattiḥ. 3. āha: ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yat sa puruṣas trāyastriṃśanāṃ devānāṃ sahabhāvyatāyām upapannaḥ? 4. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena sa puruṣo maraṇakālasamaye tathāgatasyopari cittaṃ prasādya, evaṃ vācam abhāṣata: namas tasya bhagavatas tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya, ity ekavārākṛtaṃ. 5. sa tena bhaiṣajyasena kuśalamūlena ṣaṣṭiḥ kalpān trāyastriṃśatāṃ devānāṃ sukham anubhaviṣyati; 6. aśīti kalpāṃ jātyā jātismaro bhaviṣyati; 7. jātau jātau ca sarvaśokavigato bhaviṣyati; 8. jātamātraś ca sarvaduḥkhāni nirvāpayiṣyati; na hi te sarvasatvā śakyaṃ parinirvāpayitum.
body.translated_text: 1. He said: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, where is the rebirth of a blameless person, what is his future destiny?' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Here, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the rebirth of a blameless person is in the company of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.' 3. He said: 'What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause, what is the condition, that this person is reborn in the company of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods?' 4. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>. That person, at the time of death, having placed his mind with faith upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>, spoke these words: "Homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One" — this done but once. 5. By that root of merit, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, he will experience happiness among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods for sixty <s>kalpas</s>; 6. for eighty <s>kalpas</s> he will remember his past births from life to life; 7. and in each and every birth he will be free from all sorrow; 8. and as soon as he is born he will extinguish all sufferings; yet it is not possible to bring all beings to final <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 205
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 205

body.text: 1. evam ukte bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: kathaṃ bhagavan na śakyaṃ sarvasatvāḥ parinirvāpayitum? 2. bhagavān āha: vīryaṃ bhaiṣajyasenārabdhavyam. 3. āha: katamo bhagavan vīryāraṃbhaḥ? 4. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena, vīryam ucyate phalānāṃ darśanaṃ. yad uta srotaāpattiphalaṃ nāma, vīryasthānaṃ; 6. sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ nāma, vīryasthānaṃ; 7. anāgāmiphalaṃ nāma, vīryasthānaṃ; 8. arhatvaphalam, arhannirodhaś ca nāma, vīryasthānaṃ; 9. pratyekabuddhaphalaṃ, pratyekabuddhaphalajñānaṃ nāma, vīryasthānaṃ; 10. bodhisatvabhūmiphalaṃ ca, bodhisthānaṃ, vīryasthānaṃ nāma. 11. ime bhaiṣajyasena vīryasthānānāṃ nāmāni.
body.translated_text: 1. When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'How is it, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that it is not possible to bring all beings to final <s>nirvāṇa</s>?' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Vīrya</s> (effort) must be exerted, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>.' 3. He said: 'What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the exertion of <s>vīrya</s>?' 4. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>. <s>Vīrya</s> is said to be the seeing of fruits. Namely, the fruit of <s>srotaāpatti</s> (stream-entry) is a stage of <s>vīrya</s>; 6. the fruit of <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner) is a stage of <s>vīrya</s>; 7. the fruit of <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner) is a stage of <s>vīrya</s>; 8. the fruit of <s>arhat</s>-ship and the cessation of the <s>arhat</s> is a stage of <s>vīrya</s>; 9. the fruit of <s>pratyekabuddha</s> and the knowledge of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> fruit is a stage of <s>vīrya</s>; 10. the fruit of the <s>bodhisattva</s> stages and the stage of awakening is called a stage of <s>vīrya</s>. 11. These, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, are the names of the stages of <s>vīrya</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 206
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 206

body.text: 1. āha: kathaṃ bhagavan srotaāpanno darśayitavyaḥ, srotaāpattiphalañ ca? 2. bhagavān āha: tadyathāpināma kaścid eva bhaiṣajyasena puruṣa vṛkṣaṃ vāpayeta; 3. vāpitasya vṛkṣasya tatraiva divase aṅkuraṃ viruhyeta; 4. yatraiva divase aṅkurāṇi viruhyeraṃs, tatraiva divase tad aṃkuraṃ yojanam adhastād gacchete. 5. dvitīyaś ca puruṣa evam eva vṛkṣaṃ vāpayeta; 6. tatraiva divase vātakṣobhena tasya vṛkṣasya nāṅkurāṇi viruhyeran; atha sa puruṣas tasmāt sthānāt taṃ vṛkṣaṃ uddharet. 7. athānyataraś ca puruṣaḥ kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādaṃ kuryāt: kimarthaṃ me bhūmiṃ khanasīti?
body.translated_text: 1. He said: 'How, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, should a <s>srotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer) be demonstrated, and the fruit of <s>srotaāpatti</s>?' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Suppose, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a certain person were to plant a tree; 3. and on the very same day the planted tree would sprout; 4. and on the very same day the sprouts appeared, those sprouts would go down one <s>yojana</s> (league) below. 5. And a second person would likewise plant a tree; 6. but on that same day, due to the disturbance of wind, sprouts would not appear on his tree; then that person would uproot the tree from that spot. 7. And another person would start a quarrel, dispute, conflict, and argument, saying: "Why are you digging my land?"'

body.text: SaSū(C) 207
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 207

body.text: 1. tena ca rājā aśrauṣīd evaṃ: dvau puruṣauparasparakalahabhaṇḍanavigrahajātau, vivadataḥ. 2. tena ca rājñā tayor dūtaḥ preṣitaḥ: gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa, tau dvau puruṣāv ānaya! 3. evaṃ deveti, sa puruṣas tvaramāṇarūpaḥ pradhāvitvā, tau puruṣāv etad avocat: rājā yuvayor āmantrayati. 4. atha tāvad eva tatraikapuruṣo bhītas, trasto; dvitīyaś ca puruṣo bhīto, 'nutrastaḥ. 5. yena rājā tenopanītāv upanīya, rājñaḥ purataḥ sthāpitāv, atha rājā tayor evam āha: 6. kimiti bho yuvayoḥ kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādo jātaḥ?
body.translated_text: 1. Then the king heard thus: 'Two men have engaged in quarrel, dispute, and conflict, and are arguing.' 2. The king sent a messenger to those two: 'Go, good man, and bring those two men!' 3. 'Yes, Your Majesty!' That man, running with haste, said to those two men: 'The king summons you both.' 4. Then at that very moment, one of those men became frightened and terrified; and the second man too became frightened and trembling. 5. They were brought before the king and made to stand in his presence; then the king said to them thus: 6. 'Why, sirs, has this quarrel, dispute, conflict, and argument arisen between you?'

body.text: SaSū(C) 208
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 208

body.text: 1. atha khalu tau dvau puruṣāv utthāya rājānam etad avocatāṃ: 2. śṛṇu mahārāja, asmākaṃ na kiṃcit pṛthivīpradeśaḥ saṃvidyate. 3. yācitake pṛthivīpradeśe vṛkṣo vāpitaḥ. 4. yatraiva divase vāpitas, tatraiva divase 'ṅkuraṃ, patrāṇi, puṣpāṇi, phalāni ca prādurbhūtāni, āmārdhaṃ pakvārdhaṃ ca. 5. etena ca dvitīyena puruṣeṇa tatraiva divase tasmin pṛthivīpradeśe vṛkṣo vāpitaḥ, 6. tasya ca vṛkṣasya nāṃkurāṇi rohanti; 7. vātena kṣubhitena na patrāṇi, na puṣpāṇi, na phalāni prādurbhūtāni, 8. na ca mahārāja yojanam adhastād asya mūlaṃ gacchati. 9. sa eṣa puruṣo mayā sārdhaṃ vivadati: tavāparādha iti. 10. api tu ca deva svayam eva parīkṣya jānīyān: nātra mama kiṃcid aparādhaḥ saṃvidyate.
body.translated_text: 1. Then those two men rose up and said to the king: 2. 'Listen, O great king! We have no plot of land of our own. 3. On a borrowed plot of land, a tree was planted. 4. On the very day it was planted, on that same day sprouts, leaves, flowers, and fruits appeared — half unripe and half ripe. 5. And this second person planted a tree on that same plot of land on that very day, 6. but sprouts did not grow on his tree; 7. due to the disturbed wind, neither leaves, nor flowers, nor fruits appeared, 8. nor do its roots go one <s>yojana</s> below, O great king. 9. This man quarrels with me, saying: "It is your fault." 10. But, O Lord, examine it yourself and know: no fault of mine whatsoever exists here.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 209
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 209
