body.text: 1. atha khalu sa rājā triṃśat koṭyo 'mātyānām āhūyaikadhye sannipātyaivam āha: kathayatha yūyaṃ. 2. amātyā āhuḥ: kiṃ kathayāma mahārāja? 3. rājāha: kvacid yuṣmābhir dṛṣṭaṃ vā śrutaṃ vā, yatraiva divase vṛkṣo vāpitas, tatraiva divase 'ṅkuraṃ viruhyate, 4. patrāṇi, puṣpāṇi, phalāni ca jāyante, pakvārdhamāmārdhāni? 5. niścayam idaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kartavyaṃ. 6. atha khalu te amātya utthāyāsanāt, taṃ rājānam evam āhuḥ: asmākaṃ mahārāja niścayam idaṃ na śobhate kartuṃ, na ca śakṣyāmo 'sya niścayaṃ vaktuṃ. 7. vismayam idaṃ mahārāja! 8. eṣa eva puruṣas tāvat praṣṭavyaḥ. 9. vada bhoḥ puruṣa, kiṃ satyam etam arthaṃ yad vadasi? 10. āha: satyaṃ mahārājaitam arthaṃ! 11. rājāha:
body.translated_text: 1. Then the king summoned thirty <s>koṭis</s> of ministers, assembled them together, and said thus: 'Speak, all of you!' 2. The ministers said: 'What shall we say, O great king?' 3. The king said: 'Has it ever been seen or heard by you that on the very day a tree is planted, on that same day sprouts appear, 4. and leaves, flowers, and fruits arise — half ripe and half unripe? 5. A determination must be made by you regarding this.' 6. Then those ministers rose from their seats and said to the king: 'For us, O great king, it is not fitting to make a determination on this, nor are we able to pronounce a judgment. 7. This is a marvel, O great king! 8. This very person should be questioned. 9. Speak, good man! Is this matter you say true?' 10. He said: 'True is this matter, O great king!' 11. The king said:

children.text: (1) na śrutaṃ naiva paṣyāma duḥśrāddheyaṃ vacas tava /
children.translated_text: 'We have not heard nor do we see — hard to believe is your word;

children.text: vṛkṣo yatra dine vuptas tatraivāṅkurito dine //
children.translated_text: that a tree on the day it was planted, on that very day sprouted!

children.text: (2) patrāḥ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ dattaṃ dine tatraiva bhāṣase /
children.translated_text: Leaves, flowers, and fruit appeared on that same day, you say.'

children.text: kṛtāṃjāliḥ sa puruṣas taṃ rājānam athābravīt //
children.translated_text: That man, with palms joined, then spoke to the king:

body.text: (3) gaccha svayaṃ vāpaya taruṃ paśya ruhyati aṅkuram //
body.translated_text: 'Go yourself, plant the tree, and see the sprout grow!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 210
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 210

body.text: 1. atha khalu sa rājā tṛṃśatkoṭibhir amātyaiḥ sārdhaṃ bahir niṣkrāmati, 2. tau ca dvau puruṣau cārakāvarodhaṃ kārayati. 3. tataḥ sa rājā svayam eva vṛkṣaṃ vāpayati, na ca sa vṛkṣo 'ṅkurāṇi dadāti, na patrāṇi, na puṣpāṇi, na phalāni. 4. atha sa rājā ruṣṭa evam āha: gacchantu bhavantaḥ, śīghram ānayantu dārupāṭakāni kuṭhārāṇi. 5. yāvad ānayitvā, yas tena puruṣeṇa vāpito vṛkṣaḥ sapatrapuṣpaphalaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, taṃ vṛkṣaṃ roṣāc chedayati.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the king went out together with thirty <s>koṭis</s> of ministers, 2. and had those two men placed under guard. 3. Then the king himself planted a tree, but that tree did not produce sprouts, nor leaves, nor flowers, nor fruits. 4. Then the king, angered, said thus: 'Go, sirs! Quickly bring axes and wood-cutting tools!' 5. When they brought them, the tree that had been planted by that person, which had appeared with leaves, flowers, and fruits — that tree he ordered to be cut down in anger.

body.text: SaSū(C) 211
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 211

body.text: 1. taṃ caikaṃ vṛkṣaṃ chinnaṃ, dvādaśa vṛkṣāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ; 2. dvādaśa vṛkṣāś chinnāś, caturviṃśati vṛkṣāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ, saptaratnamayāḥ, samūlāḥ, sapatrāḥ, sapahalāḥ, sāṃkurāḥ. 3. atha tebhyaś caturviṃśati vṛkṣebhyaś caturviṃśati pakṣiṇaḥ kukkuṭāḥ prādurbhūtāni, suvarṇacūḍāni, suvarṇatuṇḍāni, saptaratnamayāni pakṣmāṇi. 4. atha khalu sa rājā roṣābhibhūtaḥ svahastena kaṭhāraṃ gṛhya taṃ vṛkṣaṃ parāhanati; tataś ca vṛkṣāt parāhatād amṛtodakaṃ pravahati.
body.translated_text: 1. When that one tree was cut, twelve trees appeared; 2. when the twelve trees were cut, twenty-four trees appeared — made of the seven precious substances, with roots, with leaves, with fruits, and with sprouts. 3. Then from those twenty-four trees, twenty-four birds, roosters, appeared — with golden crests, golden beaks, and feathers made of the seven precious substances. 4. Then the king, overcome with anger, seizing an axe with his own hand, struck that tree; and from the struck tree, a stream of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) water began to flow.

body.text: SaSū(C) 212
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 212

body.text: 1. atha khalu sa rājā saṃvignamanā ājñāpayati: gacchata, tau puruṣau tataś cārakābandhanān mocayadhvam. 2. evaṃ deveti tatkṣanam eva pradhāvitvā, tau puruṣau tataś cārakabandhanān mokṣayitvā, yena taṃ vṛkṣaṃ tenopanīyataḥ. 3. atha sa rājā papraccha: kim ayaṃ vṛkṣas tvadvāpitaḥ, eko bhūtvā, cchidyamāno dviguṇavṛddhyābhivardhamānaḥ, yāvac caturviṃśatidhā gataḥ? madvāpitas tu vṛkṣo nāṃkurāṇi, na patrāṇi, na puṣpāṇi, na phalāni dattavān? 4. tataḥ sa puruṣa evam āha: yādṛśāni mahārāja mama puṇyāṇi, na tava tādṛśāni puṇyāni saṃvidyante.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the king, his mind filled with awe, commanded: 'Go! Release those two men from their prison bonds!' 2. 'Yes, Your Majesty!' Immediately running forth, they released those two men from their prison bonds and brought them to that tree. 3. Then the king asked: 'How is it that this tree you planted, being one, when cut multiplied twofold, until it became twenty-four? Yet the tree I planted produced neither sprouts, nor leaves, nor flowers, nor fruits?' 4. Then that man said thus: 'Such are my merits, O great king; you do not possess such merits.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 213
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 213

body.text: 1. atha khalu te triṃśad amātyakoṭyas, tasya puruṣasyobhau jānumaṇḍalau pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya, evam āhuḥ: tvayā rājyaṃ kārayitavyaṃ, nāyaṃ pūrvimako rājā śobhate. 2. atha khalu sa puruṣas tān amātyān gāthābhiḥ pratyabhāṣata:
body.translated_text: 1. Then those thirty <s>koṭis</s> of ministers, placing both their knees on the ground before that man, said thus: 'You should rule the kingdom; this former king is not fitting.' 2. Then that man addressed those ministers in verses:

body.text: (1) rājyabhogaiś ca me nārtho na dhānyena dhanena vā //
body.translated_text: 'I have no need for royal pleasures, nor for grain, nor for wealth.'

children.text: (2) prasādo mama buddhebhyo bhaveyaṃ dvipadottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: (2) 'Through my faith in the <s>Buddhas</s>, may I become the best of two-footed beings,

children.text: vrajen nirvāṇadhātau hi śānte yatra tathāgataḥ //
children.translated_text: and may I go to the peaceful realm of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> where the <s>Tathāgata</s> abides.'

children.text: (3) deśeyaṃ dharmaṃ yuṣmākaṃ nirvāṇapuragāminaṃ /
children.translated_text: (3) 'I would teach you the <s>Dharma</s> leading to the city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.'

children.text: paryaṃkaṃ sa bandhitvā pratijñām akarot tataḥ //
children.translated_text: Having sat cross-legged, he then made this vow:

children.text: (4) pūrvaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ rājño bandhanam āgataḥ /
children.translated_text: (4) 'Previously I committed sin and came to be imprisoned by the king;

children.text: idan tu kṛtvā praṇidhiṃ mama pāpakṣayo bhavet //
children.translated_text: but by making this aspiration, may my sins be exhausted.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 214
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 214

body.text: 1. atha khalu te caturviṃśati pakṣiṇakukkuṭakoṭyo vajratuṇḍena tūryāṇi parāhanati sma. 2. atha khalu tena kālena tena samayena dvātriṃśati kūṭāgārasahasrāṇi prādurbhūtāni, 3. ekaikaṃ ca kūṭāgāraṃ paṃcaviṃśatiyojanapramāṇaṃ prādurabhavat 4. ekaikasmiṃś ca kūṭāgāre paṃcaviṃśati koṭyo pakṣiṇānāṃ prādurbhūtāni, suvarṇacūḍāni, suvarṇatuṇḍāni, suvarṇamukhāni; 5. te mānuṣyakaṃ vācaṃ niścārayanti:
body.translated_text: 1. Then those twenty-four <s>koṭis</s> of roosters among the birds struck musical instruments with their diamond beaks. 2. Then at that time and occasion, thirty-two thousand pavilions appeared, 3. and each pavilion measured twenty-five <s>yojanas</s> in extent. 4. And in each pavilion, twenty-five <s>koṭis</s> of birds appeared, with golden crests, golden beaks, and golden faces; 5. they uttered human speech:

children.text: (1) asādhus te mahārāja yad vṛkṣaś cheditas tvayā /
children.translated_text: (1) 'You have done wrong, O great king, in that you cut down the tree;

children.text: koṭīśatāni vṛkṣāṇāṃ caturviṃśat sthitāḥ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: twenty-four hundred <s>koṭis</s> of trees stand again.

children.text: (2) pāpena karmaṇānena aniṣṭhaṃ bhokṣyase phalam /
children.translated_text: (2) By this sinful action you shall experience unpleasant fruit;

children.text: na jānīṣe kīdṛśaḥ satvo yenāyaṃ vāpito drumaḥ //
children.translated_text: you do not know what kind of being it was by whom this tree was planted.'

body.text:
6. rājāha:
(3) na jānāmi imam arthaṃ vyākurudhavaṃ mahātapā /
body.translated_text: 6. The king said: (3) 'I do not know this matter — explain it, O great ascetics!'

body.text:
7. pakṣiṇa āhuḥ:
(4) eṣo hi lokapradyoto utpatsyati vināyakaḥ /
body.translated_text: 7. The birds said: (4) 'This one is the Light of the World; he shall arise as a Guide.',

body.text:
8. rājāha:
(5) katamo dvitīyaḥ puroṣo yasya vṛkṣaṃ na rūhati /
body.translated_text: 8. The king said: (5) 'Who is the second person for whom the tree does not grow?'

children.text: 9. pakṣiṇa āhuḥ:
children.translated_text: 9. The birds said:

children.text: (6) devadatto hi mūḍho 'sau yasya vṛkṣaṃ na rūhati /
children.translated_text: (6) 'That fool is <s>Devadatta</s>, for whom the tree does not grow;

children.text: na kṛtaṃ kuśalaṃ kiṃcid ruhyate 'sya kathaṃ druma //
children.translated_text: he has done no wholesome deed — how then could a tree grow for him?'

body.text: SaSū(C) 214
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 214

body.text: 10. atha khalu tena kālena tena samayena tṛṃśat koṭya 'mātyānām, iman dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā, sarve daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā, abhijñāpratilabdhāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ, sa ca rājā daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitaḥ, kuśaladharmābhisamayam anuprāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: 10. Then at that time and occasion, thirty <s>koṭis</s> of ministers, having heard this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma), all became established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) and attained the <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges), and the king too became established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> and attained the realization of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: SaSū(C) 215
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 215

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yat triṃśat koṭyo janānāṃ daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā, abhijñāpratilabdhā saṃvṛttāḥ? 2. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena, vyākariṣyāmi. 3. atha khalu bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāṃ smitaṃ prāduṣcakāra. 4. atha tasmin samaye bhagavato mukhadvārāc caturaśīti raśmisahasrāṇi naścaranti smā, anekavarṇāni, nānāvarṇāny, anekaśatasahasravarṇāni, tadyathā nīlapītalohitāvadātamaṃjiṣṭhāsphaṭikarajatavarṇāni. 5. tā anantāparyantā lokadhātūn avabhāsya, punar eva pratyudāvṛtyā, bhagavantaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya, bhagavato mūrdhany antardhīyanta.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the reason and condition that thirty <s>koṭis</s> of people became established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> and attained the <s>abhijñās</s>?' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, I shall explain.' 3. Then at that moment the <s>Bhagavān</s> displayed a smile. 4. At that time, from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s mouth, eighty-four thousand rays of light issued forth, of many colors, of various hues, of many hundreds of thousands of colors — namely, blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, crystal, and silver colors. 5. Those rays, having illuminated boundless and infinite world-realms, returned and, after circumambulating the <s>Bhagavān</s>, disappeared into the crown of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s head.

body.text: SaSū(C) 216
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 216

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ utthāyāsanād, ekāṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ prāvṛtya, dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamaya, bhagavantam etad avocat: 2. ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya prāduṣkaraṇāya? nāhetukaṃ nāpratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāduṣkurvanti. 3. bhagavān āha: paśyasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena caturdiśaṃ lokadhātau samantāj janakāyam āgacchantaṃ mamāntike? 4. āha: nohīdaṃ bhagavan na paśyāmi. 5. bhagavān āha: tena hi bhaiṣajyasena vyavalokaya, paśya janakāyaṃ!
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> rose from his seat, draped his robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 2. 'What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the reason and condition for the display of this smile? For <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones do not display a smile without cause and condition.' 3. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do you see, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a multitude of people coming from the four directions of the world-realm to my presence?' 4. He said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>, I do not see them.' 5. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Then, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, look and see the multitude of people!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 217
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 217

body.text:
1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo vyavalokyādrākṣīt. 2. pūrvasyān diśy eko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ; tatraikānte paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni; te ca na bhāṣante, na jalpanti, nālapanti, na bhuṃjanti, nottiṣṭhanti; nottiṣṭhanti; tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayanti. 3. dakṣiṇasyān diśy eko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ; tatra paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni; te na jalpanti, nālapanti, na bhāṣante, nottiṣṭhanti, na caṃkramanti; tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsyanti. 4. paścimāyāṃ diśy eko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ; tatra paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni; te na jalpanti, nālapanti, na bhāṣanti, nottiṣṭhanti, na caṃkramanti; tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayanti. 5. uttarasyān diśy eko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ; tatra paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni; te na jalpanti, nālapanti, na bhāṣaṃte, na bhāṣaṃte, nottiṣṭhanti, na caṃkramanti; tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayanti. 6. ūrdhvāyān diśy eko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ; tatra paṃcaviṃśati koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni; te na jalpanti, na bhāṣanti, nottiṣṭhanti, na caṃkramanti; tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsyanti. 7. adhastāddiśy eko vṛkṣaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, saptayojanasahasrapramāṇaḥ; tatra ca paṃcaviṃśati
koṭīsahasrāṇi janakāyasya sannipatitāni; te na jalpanti, nālapanti, na bhāṣanti, nottiṣṭhanti, na caṃkramanti; tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayanti.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> looked and saw: 2. In the eastern direction a single tree appeared, seven thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent; on one side, twenty-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of people had assembled; and they did not speak, did not converse, did not talk, did not eat, did not stand up; they remained in silence. 3. In the southern direction a single tree appeared, seven thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent; there, twenty-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of people had assembled; they did not converse, did not talk, did not speak, did not stand up, did not walk about; they remained in silence. 4. In the western direction a single tree appeared, seven thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent; there, twenty-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of people had assembled; they did not converse, did not talk, did not speak, did not stand up, did not walk about; they remained in silence. 5. In the northern direction a single tree appeared, seven thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent; there, twenty-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of people had assembled; they did not converse, did not talk, did not speak, did not stand up, did not walk about; they remained in silence. 6. In the upward direction a single tree appeared, seven thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent; there, twenty-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of people had assembled; they did not converse, did not speak, did not stand up, did not walk about; they remained in silence. 7. In the downward direction a single tree appeared, seven thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent; there, twenty-five thousand <s>koṭis</s> of people had assembled; they did not converse, did not talk, did not speak, did not stand up, did not walk about; they remained in silence.

body.text: SaSū(C) 218
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 218

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: pṛccheyam ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kaṃcid eva pradeśaṃ, sacen me bhagavān avakāśaṃ kuryāt pṛṣṭapraśnavyākaraṇāya. 2. evam ukte bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisatvaṃ mahāsatvam etad avocat: pṛccha tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena yad yad evākāṃkṣasy; ahan te tasya tasyaiva praśnasya paripṛṣṭasya vyākaraṇena cittam ārādhayiṣye.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I would ask the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, about a certain matter, if the <s>Bhagavān</s> would grant me the opportunity to have my question answered.' 2. When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'Ask, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, whatever you wish; I shall satisfy your mind with the answer to each and every question.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 219
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 219

body.text: 1. evam ukte bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: kiṃ bhagavaṃś caturdiśe lokadhātuṣu janakāya āgatyāvasthito? yāvad adhastādūrdhvāyāṃ diśi paṃcāśat koṭyo janakāyam āgatyāvasthitaḥ. 2. te ca bhagavantaṃ nālapanti, na saṃlapanti, na jalpanti, na vadanti, na bhāṣanti, nottiṣṭhanti, na caṃkramanti; tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayanti. ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ? 3. bhagavān āha: gaccha tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena, svayam eva tāṃs tathāgatān paripṛccha yato lokadhātāv ete janakāyā āgatāḥ. 4. āha: kasya ṛddhibalādhānena gacchāmi? 5. bhagavān āha: svakena bhaiṣajyasena ṛddhibalādhānena gaccha.
body.translated_text: 1. When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Are there, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, multitudes of people who have come and stand in the world-realms of the four directions? And below and above, fifty <s>koṭis</s> of people have come and stand. 2. And they do not speak to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, do not converse, do not talk, do not say anything, do not speak, do not stand up, do not walk about; they remain in silence. What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the reason and condition for this?' 3. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Go yourself, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, and ask those <s>Tathāgatas</s> from which world-realms these multitudes of people have come.' 4. He said: 'By whose power of supernatural attainment shall I go?' 5. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Go by your own power of supernatural attainment, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 220
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 220

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo, bhagavantaṃ tṛguptaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya, tatraivāntardhitaḥ. 2. ṣaṇnavati lokadhātukoṭīr atikramya, candrapradīpā nāma lokadhātuḥ. 3. tatra candrāvatikṣetro nāma tathāgato, 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, aśītikoṭībodhisatvamahāsatvaparivṛtaḥ, puraskṛto dharman deśayati sma. 4. tāṃ lokadhātuṃ bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo 'nuprāptaḥ.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, disappeared right there. 2. Having traversed ninety-seven <s>koṭis</s> of world-realms, there was a world-realm named <s>Candrapradīpā</s>. 3. There, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Candrāvatikṣetra</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, surrounded by eighty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, honored by them, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. 4. The <s>bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> arrived at that world-realm.

body.text: SaSū(C) 221
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 221

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvas tasya bhagavataś candrāvatikṣetrasya tathāgatasya purata sthito, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya, bhagavantam etad avocat: 2. āgato 'smi bhagavan ṣaṇnavati lokadhātukoṭīsahasrāṇy atikramya, nāhaṃ bhagavaṃs tāvanti satvāni kvacit paśyāmi yāvanti tatra dṛṣṭāni.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> stood before that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata Candrāvatikṣetra</s>, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 2. 'I have come, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, having traversed ninety-seven thousand <s>koṭis</s> of world-realms, and I have not seen anywhere as many beings as I have seen there.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 222
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 222

body.text: 1. sa bhagavān āha: tatraiva bhaiṣajyasena saṃcaranti, saṃtiṣṭhanti. 2. āha: yathā kathaṃ punar bhagavan? 3. bhagavān āha: acetanavṛkṣasaṃbhūtāni satvāni. 4. āha: kena bhagavan dṛṣṭaṃ kena śrutaṃ yad acetane vṛkṣe manuṣyā jāyante? 5. sa bhagavān āha: na bhaiṣajyasena tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ vā na śrutaṃ vā yad acetane vṛkṣe manuṣyā jāyaṃte? 6. āha: na me bhagavan dṛṣṭaṃ na śrutaṃ yad acetane vṛkṣe manuṣyā jāyante. 7. sa bhagavān āha: icchasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena draṣṭuṃ? tad ahaṃ sāṃprataṃ darśayiṣyāmi. 8. āha: icchāmi bhagavann, icchāmi sugata!
body.translated_text: (1) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Right there, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, they move about and abide.' (2) He said: 'How so, O <s>Bhagavān</s>?' (3) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'They are beings born from insentient trees.' (4) He said: 'By whom, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, has it been seen or heard that humans are born in an insentient tree?' (5) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Have you not, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, seen or heard that humans are born in an insentient tree?' (6) He said: 'I have not, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, seen or heard that humans are born in an insentient tree.' (7) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do you wish, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, to see? I shall now show you.' (8) He said: 'I wish it, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! I wish it, O <s>Sugata</s>!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 223
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 223

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhagavāṃś candrāvatikṣetras tathāgatas tasyāṃ velāyāṃ śatapuṇyavicitritaṃ svaṃ bāhuṃ prasārayati sma, 2. tataś ca bāhutaḥ koṭīśatasahasraṃ janakāyānāṃ prādurabhavat, 3. ekaikaś ca janakāyo bāhuśataṃ prasārya, nānāgandhavilepanais tathāgatam abhyavakiranti. 4. atha sa bhagavāṃś candrāvatikṣetras tathāgato bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisatvaṃ mahāsatvam āmantrayati: paśyasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyasena? eṣa janakāyas tathāgataṃ nānāgandhamālyavilepanair abhyavakiranti. 5. āha: paśyāmi bhagavan, paśyāmi sugata. 6. sa bhagavān āha: ete acetanā janakāyāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ! ete acetanā manuṣyāḥ! ayonijā ete satvāḥ. 7. atha khalu teṣāṃ koṭīśatasahasrāṇām ekaikasya yad bāhuśataṃ te sarve vikīryante.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> of the <s>Candrāvati</s> (Moon-Radiance) field, at that moment extended his own arm adorned with a hundred merits. (2) From that arm there appeared a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of groups of people. (3) Each group of people, extending a hundred arms, showered the <s>Tathāgata</s> with various fragrances and ointments. (4) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> of the <s>Candrāvati</s> field, addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'Do you see, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>? These groups of people are showering the <s>Tathāgata</s> with various fragrances, garlands, and ointments.' (5) He said: 'I see, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! I see, O <s>Sugata</s>!' (6) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'These groups of people have appeared as insentient beings! These are insentient humans! These beings are non-womb-born (<s>ayonija</s>).' (7) Then the hundred arms of each of those hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> [of beings] all disintegrated.

body.text: SaSū(C) 224
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 224

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvas taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavantam etad avocat: kimidaṃ bhagavan, kimidaṃ sugata yan manuṣyāṇāṃ muhūrtamātreṇa bāhuśataṃ vikīrṇam? 2. yadi bhagavaṃ cchatabāhavo na mucyante, kaḥ punar vādo dvibāhukā manuṣyā mokṣyante! 3. bhagavān āha: evam eva bhaiṣajyasenācetanāḥ satvā jāyante, acetanā niruddhyante. 4. asmākam api bhaiṣajyasena śarīram acetanabhūtaṃ manyitavyaṃ. 5. āha: katame bhagavan satvā ye daharāḥ, katame vṛddhāḥ? 6. bhagavān āha: santi bhaiṣajyasena daharāḥ satvā, santi vṛddhāḥ. 7. āha: katame bhagavan daharāḥ, katame vṛddhāḥ? 8. āha: ye te vṛkṣebhyo nirjātās, te daharāḥ. 9. āha: icchāmi bhagavan daharāṇi satvāni draṣṭum.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, having seen that, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What is this, O <s>Bhagavān</s>? What is this, O <s>Sugata</s>, that the hundred arms of humans disintegrated in a mere moment?' (2) 'If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, those with a hundred arms are not liberated, what then need be said of two-armed humans being liberated!' (3) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, insentient beings are born, and insentient beings cease.' (4) 'Even our body, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, should be considered as insentient.' (5) He said: 'Which beings, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are young, and which are old?' (6) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'There are, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, young beings, and there are old ones.' (7) He said: 'Which, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are young, and which are old?' (8) He said: 'Those born from trees — they are young.' (9) He said: 'I wish, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, to see the young beings.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 225
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 225

body.text: 1. atha khalu sa bhagavāṃś candrāvatikṣetras tathāgato dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇitalaṃ prasārayati. 2. atha daśabhyo digbhyaḥ koṭīśatasahasraṃ janakāyānām āgacchanti; 3. adhastādūrdhvāyān diśi paṃcāśat koṭī janakāyasyāgacchanti; 4. āgatvā ca te janakāyā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya, na ca tathāgatam ālapanti, na saṃlapanti; tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayanti sma.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> of the <s>Candrāvati</s> field, extended his right palm. (2) From the ten directions, a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of groups of people came. (3) From the downward and upward directions, fifty <s>koṭis</s> of groups of people came. (4) Having come, those groups of people bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, but they did not speak to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor converse with him; they acquiesced in silence.

body.text: SaSū(C) 226
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 226

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: kim ete bhagavan satvās tathāgataṃ nālapanti, na saṃlapanti, tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayanti? 2. bhagavān āha: na jānāsi bhaiṣajyasena? acetanaḥ pṛthivīpradeśe nālapanti, na saṃlapanti, na dharmaskandhaṃ prajānāti. 3. tat kasya hetoḥ? ihaikatyā bhaiṣajyasena daharā satvāḥ notpādaṃ jānanti, na nirodhaṃ jānanti, dṛṣṭvā ca na jarāṃ, na vyādhiṃ, na śokaṃ, na paridevaṃ, na priyaviprayogaṃ, nāpriyasaṃprayogaṃ, na priyād vinābhāvaṃ, na maraṇaṃ, nākālamṛtyum. 4. nāpi tāni sarvakaṭukāni duḥkhāṇi dṛṣṭvā udvegam āpadyante. kutas te jñāsyanti? 5. punaḥ punas te bhaiṣajyasena śikṣayitavyāḥ.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Why, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, do these beings not speak to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor converse with him, but acquiesce in silence?' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do you not know, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>? On the insentient ground they do not speak, nor converse, nor comprehend the aggregates of <s>Dharma</s>. (3) For what reason? Here, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, some young beings do not know arising, do not know cessation, and having seen [the world] do not know old age, nor disease, nor grief, nor lamentation, nor separation from the beloved, nor union with the unloved, nor absence from what is dear, nor death, nor untimely death. (4) Even having seen all those bitter sufferings, they do not develop a sense of urgency. How then will they know? (5) Again and again, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, they must be trained.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 227
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 227

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: kuto bhagavan daharā satvā āgacchanti? kutaś cyavanti? kutropapadyante ye dharmaṃ na jānanti? 2. bhagavān āha: śṛṇu bhaiṣajyasena, yan mānuṣyakam ātmabhāvaṃ pratigṛhṇanti, tan na rupyakāreṇa kṛtaṃ, 3. na cīmarakāreṇa kṛtaṃ, 4. na kāṣṭhakāreṇa kṛtaṃ, 5. na kuṃbhakāreṇa kṛtaṃ. 6. na rājabhayenotpadyante. 7. strīpuruṣasaṃyogāt pāpena karmaṇā saṃyuktāḥ saṃbhavanti. 8. punaḥ punaś ca teṣāṃ satvānāṃ śilpāni śikṣāpayanti. 9. anantaṃ ca kaṭukaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃbhavati. 10. kaṭukā vedanāḥ tatra, teṣāṃ pūrvakṛtānāṃ pāpakānāṃ karmaṇāṃ vipākam, anubhavanti. 11. ihaiva te bhaiṣajyasena daharāḥ satvā āgatā ya ete nālapanti, na saṃlapanti, nottiṣṭhanti. te īdṛśān duḥkhāṃ vedanām anubhavanti! 12. anena kāraṇena bhaiṣajyasena nālapanti, na saṃlapanti. 13. evaṃ te bhaiṣajyasena daharāḥ satvāḥ, kuśalam ajānānāḥ, notpādaṃ jānanti, na nirodhaṃ jānanti, na ca te mānuṣyakam ātmabhāvaṃ pratilapsyante. 14. ime ucyante bhaiṣajyasena daharāḥ satvāḥ.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'From where, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, do the young beings come? From where do they fall? Where are they reborn — those who do not know the <s>Dharma</s>?' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>. That they take on a human embodiment — that is not made by a silversmith, (3) nor made by a weaver, (4) nor made by a carpenter, (5) nor made by a potter. (6) They do not arise from fear of a king. (7) From the union of man and woman, conjoined with unwholesome <s>karma</s>, they come into being. (8) Again and again their crafts and skills are taught to those beings. (9) And boundless bitter suffering arises. (10) Painful feelings there — they experience the ripening of those previously performed evil <s>karmas</s>. (11) It is here, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, that the young beings have come, those who do not speak, do not converse, do not rise up. They experience such painful feelings! (12) For this reason, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, they do not speak, they do not converse. (13) Thus, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, those young beings, not knowing what is wholesome, do not know arising, do not know cessation, and they will not obtain a human embodiment. (14) These, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, are called the young beings.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 228
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 228

body.text: 1. āha: kathaṃ bhagavan daharāḥ satvā utpadyante, kathaṃ nirudhyante? 2. bhagavān āha: tadyathāpināma bhaiṣajyasena kaścid eva puruṣo 'gniṃ kāṣṭhena parimārjayeta, tasyānupūrveṇa taṃ kāṣṭham agninā pradīpyeta; 3. evam eva bhaiṣajyasena mānuṣyātmabhāvaṃ prathamaṃ saṃjāyate, jātaṃ ca sad vedanāṃ vedayati. 4. āha: ko 'trābhijāto jātaḥ, kaḥ parinirvṛtaḥ? 5. bhagavān āha: buddha eva bhaiṣajyasenābhijāto jātaḥ, tathāgata eva parinirvṛtaḥ!
body.translated_text: (1) He said: 'How, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are young beings born, and how do they cease?' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Just as, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a certain man might rub fire with a piece of wood, and gradually that wood would be kindled by the fire; (3) just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a human embodiment first comes into being, and having been born, one experiences feelings.' (4) He said: 'Who here was born fully awakened, and who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>?' (5) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Only the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, was born fully awakened; only the <s>Tathāgata</s> has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>!'

body.text: SaSū(C) 229
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 229

body.text: 1. tadyathāpināma bhaiṣajyasena kasmiṃścid andhakāragṛhe timirāgāre rājñā puruṣo bandhanāvarodhaḥ kṛtaḥ syāt. 2. tatra sa puruṣo, 'ndhakāragṛhe praviṣṭaḥ, antargṛhe timiraṃ timirāgāraṃ paśyet. 3. athānyaḥ kaścit puruṣaḥ, pūrvaduḥkhavedanābhir dṛṣṭaś, cintayen: naṣṭa eṣa puruṣo, 'nabhyasitaduḥkho jīvitanāśaṃ yāsyati. 4. sa tatrāgnim ānayitvā tatrābhyantargṛhe sūkṣmam agniṃ chorayet. 5. sa ca puruṣaś cārakāvaruddhas tam agniraśmiṃ paśyed, dṛṣṭvā cāśvasto bhaved, utsāhaṃ ca vardhayet. 6. sa cāgniḥ kenacid eva hetunā prajvaleta, tena cāgninā prajvālena tad gṛhaṃ samantataḥ prajvalet; sa ca puruṣas tatraiva dahyeta.7. taṃ ca dagdhaṃ rājā śrutvā cintāyāsam āpadyeta; tasyaivaṃ bhaven: na bhūyo 'haṃ svaviṣaye kaṃcit satvaṃ cārakāvarodhaṃ kariṣyāmi. 8. atha sa rājā teṣāṃ svaviṣayanivāsināṃ satvānām evaṃ samāśvāsayet: mā yūyaṃ bhavantaḥ satvā bhāyatha! mā uttrasatha! abhayaṃ yuṣmākaṃ bhavatu! 9. na mama viṣaye bhūyo daṇḍopacāraṃ vā, bandhanāvarodhaṃ vā bhaviṣyati, na ca kasyacit satvasya jīvitavināśaṃ kariṣyāmi. 10. nirbhayā bhavantaḥ satvā yūyaṃ bhavatha!
body.translated_text: (1) 'Just as, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, a man might be confined by a king in a dark house, a chamber of darkness. (2) That man, having entered the dark house, would see darkness within the inner chamber, a house of darkness. (3) Then another man, having witnessed his former painful experiences, would think: "This man is lost; unaccustomed to suffering, he will go to the destruction of his life." (4) He would bring fire there and secretly place a small fire inside the inner chamber. (5) That imprisoned man would see the firelight, and having seen it would become reassured and increase his courage. (6) That fire, by some cause, would blaze up, and by that blazing fire the house would be ablaze on all sides; and that man would be burned right there. (7) The king, having heard that he was burned, would become distressed with worry; and this thought would occur to him: "Never again will I imprison any being in my realm." (8) Then that king would reassure the beings dwelling in his realm thus: "Do not, good beings, be afraid! Do not be terrified! May there be fearlessness for you! (9) In my realm there shall no longer be punishment, nor imprisonment, nor shall I bring about the destruction of any being's life. (10) Be fearless, good beings!"'

body.text: SaSū(C) 230
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 230

body.text: 1. evam eva bhaiṣajyasena tathāgataḥ sarvakleśadagdhaḥ, sarvavyādhipraśāntaḥ. 2. yathā sa puruṣo gṛhadāhāt svakāyaṃ dahati, satvānām arthāya hitāya sukhāya ca pratipanno bhavati satvān vadhabandhanāvarodheṣu parimocayituṃ, 3. evam eva tathāgato, rāgadveṣamohamalaprahīṇaḥ, sarvasatvānān dīpa iva loka utpannaḥ, satvān mocayati; 4. narakatiryakpretāsurakāyebhyaḥ daharāṃś ca satvān, vṛddhāṃś ca satvān mocayati.
body.translated_text: (1) 'Just so, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has burned away all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and pacified all diseases. (2) Just as that man, through the burning of the house, burns his own body, [the <s>Tathāgata</s>] is one who has set forth for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of beings, to liberate beings from killing, bondage, and imprisonment. (3) Just so the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having abandoned the stains of desire, hatred, and delusion, has arisen in the world like a lamp for all beings, and liberates beings — (4) from the realms of hell, animals, hungry ghosts, and <s>Asuras</s> he liberates both young beings and old beings.'

children.text: SaSū(C) 231
children.translated_text: SaSū(C) 231

children.text: 1. atha tāvad evopary antarīkṣād imā gāthā niścacārā:
children.translated_text: (1) Then at that very moment, these verses issued forth from the sky above:

children.text: (1) aho kṣetraṃ jinakṣetraṃ sukṣetram abhisaṃskṛtaṃ /
children.translated_text: (1) 'Ah, the field! The field of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror)! A good field, well-prepared,

children.text: vuptāni yatra bījāni na vināśaṃ vrajanti hi //
children.translated_text: where seeds that are sown never go to destruction!'

children.text: (2) buddhakṣetraṃ jinakṣetraṃ praśastaṃ jinaśāsanaṃ /
children.translated_text: (2) 'The <s>Buddha</s>-field, the <s>Jina</s>-field — glorious is the teaching of the <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: śāstā karoty upāyaṃ hi sarvasatvaparigrahe //
children.translated_text: the Teacher indeed employs skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) in embracing all beings.'

children.text: (3) sthito nirvāṇadhātau sandṛśyate dharaṇītale /
children.translated_text: (3) 'Abiding in the realm of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, he is seen upon the surface of the earth;

children.text: śāntaṃ kṛtvā sarvalokaṃ buddhaḥ śodheti dakṣiṇāṃ //
children.translated_text: having pacified the entire world, the <s>Buddha</s> purifies the offering.'

children.text: (4) moceti navakān satvān moceti ca purāṇakān /
children.translated_text: (4) 'He liberates new beings; he liberates old beings;

children.text: mocayitvānupūrveṇa sarvasatvāṃs tridhātukāt //
children.translated_text: having liberated gradually all beings from the triple realm (<s>tridhātuka</s>).'

children.text: (5) baddhā hi narakadvāras tiryakpretā vimocitāḥ /
children.translated_text: (5) 'The doors of the hells are bound shut; animals and <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) are liberated;

children.text: śāntiḥ kṛtā hi lokesmin paraloke sukhaṃ kṛtaṃ //
children.translated_text: peace has been made in this world; happiness has been made in the next world.'

children.text: SaSū(C) 232
children.translated_text: SaSū(C) 232

children.text: 1. atha khalu bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāṃ smitaṃ prāduṣcakāra, āha ca:
children.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that moment, displayed a smile, and spoke:

children.text: (1) sādhu darśanu sādhūnāṃ buddhānāṃ sādhu darśanaṃ /
children.translated_text: (1) 'Excellent is the sight of the virtuous; excellent is the sight of <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: sādhu dharmaguṇaḥ kṣetraṃ saṃghasāmagridarśanam //
children.translated_text: excellent is the <s>Dharma</s>-virtue-field; excellent is the sight of the harmony of the <s>Saṅgha</s>.'

children.text: (2) sādhu saṃghātanirdeśaṃ sarvapāpavināśanaṃ /
children.translated_text: (2) 'Excellent is the <s>Saṃghāṭa</s> teaching, the destroyer of all evil;

children.text: ye śroṣyanti idaṃ sūtraṃ padaṃ prāpsyanty anuttaram //
children.translated_text: those who will hear this sūtra will attain the unsurpassed station.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 233
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 233

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇāmya, bhagavantam etad avocat: 2. ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ, smitasya prāduṣkaraṇāya? 3. bhagavān āha: paśyasi tvaṃ kulaputraitāni daharāṇi satvāni? 4. āha: paśyāmi bhagavan, paśyāmi sugata. 5. bhagavān āha: sarva ete bhaiṣajyasenādyaiva daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitā bodhisatvā bhaviṣyanti.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, extending his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> and bowing, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: (2) 'What is the cause, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, what is the condition for the display of this smile?' (3) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do you see, O son of good family, these young beings?' (4) He said: 'I see them, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I see them, O <s>Sugata</s>.' (5) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'All of these, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, on this very day will become <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages).'

body.text: SaSū(C) 234
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 234

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo 'śītir yojanasahasrāṇy ūrdhavam upary antarīkṣe 'sthād. 2. athāśītir devaputrakoṭīsahasrāṇi bhagavata upari puṣpavarṣaṃ pravarṣanti. 3. te ca daharāḥ satvā dṛṣṭvā sarve 'ñjalayaḥ kṛtvā namaskurvanti.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s> stood in the sky above, eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s> high. (2) Then eighty thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of divine sons rained a shower of flowers upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. (3) And those young beings, seeing this, all made <s>añjali</s> (palms joined) and paid homage.

body.text: SaSū(C) 235
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 235

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo antarīkṣastha evaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate yena trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ śabdenāpūrayati. 2. dvātriṃśan mahānarakopapannāḥ satvās taṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇvanti, 3. dvātriṃśac ca devanikāyās taṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇvanti; 4. trisāhasramahāsāhasraś ca lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitaḥ; 5. caturaśītiś ca nāgarājasahasrāṇi mahāsamudre saṃkṣubdhāni; 6. triṃśat koṭīsahasrāṇi rākṣasānām imaṃ jaṃbudvīpam āgatāni, 7. paṃcaviṃśat koṭīsahasrāṇi pretānāṃ yakṣānāṃ rākṣasānām aḍakavatyāṃ rājadhānyām āgatāni. 8. bhagavataḥ purato mahāsannipātaḥ saṃsthitaḥ.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, standing in the sky, spoke these words by which he filled the <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> (billion-fold) world-system with sound. (2) The beings reborn in the thirty-two great hells heard that sound; (3) and the thirty-two classes of gods heard that sound. (4) And the <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> world-system trembled with six kinds of earthquakes. (5) And eighty-four thousand <s>Nāga</s> kings were stirred up in the great ocean. (6) Thirty thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Rākṣasas</s> came to this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. (7) Twenty-five thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>pretas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s> came to the royal city of <s>Aḍakavatī</s>. (8) A great assembly was established before the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: SaSū(C) 236
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 236

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhagavāṃs teṣān daharāṇāṃ satvānān dharman deśayati. 2. daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu koṭīsahasrāṇi bodhisatvānāṃ mahāsatvānāṃ svakasvakābhir ṛddhibhir āgatāni. 3. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamaya, bhagavantam etad avocat: bahavo bhagavan, bahavo sugata bodhisatvāḥ sannipatitāḥ sanniṣaṇṇāḥ, 4. bahūni ca bhagavan devanāgāni sannipatitāni sanniṣaṇṇāni, 5. punaś cānekāni rākṣasapretāny, aḍakavatyāṃ rājadhānyām āgatya, sannipatitāni sanniṣaṇṇāny abhūvan dharmaśravaṇāya.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> to those young beings. (2) From the world-systems in the ten directions, thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> came, each by their own supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>). (3) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, extending his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> and bowing, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Many, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, many, O <s>Sugata</s>, are the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have gathered and are seated. (4) And many, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are the divine <s>Nāgas</s> who have gathered and are seated. (5) And furthermore, many <s>Rākṣasas</s> and <s>pretas</s>, having come to the royal city of <s>Aḍakavatī</s>, have gathered and are seated for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 237
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 237

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisatvaṃ mahāsatvaṃ āmantrayati: āgaccha kulaputra! 2. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatva, ṛddhibalenordhvād avatīrya, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamaya, bhagavantam etad avocat: 3. dharmaskandho bhagavan, dharmaskandha ity ucyate? kiyatā bhagavan dharmaskandha iti? 4. bhagavān āha: dharmaskandha iti kulaputrocyate yo brahmacaryaṃ paryeṣate, brahmacaryaṃ paryeṣya sarvapāpād viramati. 5. paśyasi tvaṃ kulaputrāmī daharā satvā abrahmacaryād viramanti? 6. āha: paśyāmi bhagavan, paśyāmi sugata! 7. āha: te nūnan dhāraṇīpratilabdhā bhaviṣyanti, sarvadharmasamanvāgatāś ca bhaviṣyanti. 8. āha: kenopāyena bhagavan bahūni satvāni sannipatitāni dharmaskandhaṃ śrotum?
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'Come, O son of good family!' (2) Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, descending from above by supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), extending his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> and bowing, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: (3) 'The aggregate of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmaskandha</s>), O <s>Bhagavān</s> — it is called the aggregate of <s>Dharma</s>? What constitutes, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the aggregate of <s>Dharma</s>?' (4) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The aggregate of <s>Dharma</s>, O son of good family, is said to be one who seeks the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>); having sought the holy life, one abstains from all evil. (5) Do you see, O son of good family, these young beings who are abstaining from non-celibacy?' (6) He said: 'I see them, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I see them, O <s>Sugata</s>!' (7) He said: 'They will surely obtain <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention), and will become endowed with all <s>dharmas</s>.' (8) He said: 'By what means, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, have so many beings gathered to hear the aggregate of <s>Dharma</s>?'

body.text: SaSū(C) 238
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 238

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhagavāṃ bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisatvaṃ mahāsatvam āmantrayati: 2. bahavo bhaiṣajyasena satvāḥ santi ye jātir eva duḥkhaṃ na śṛṇvanti, jarā eva duḥkhaṃ na śṛṇvanti, vyādhir eva duḥkhaṃ na śṛṇvanti, śokaduḥkhaṃ, paridevaduḥkhaṃ, priyaviprayogaduḥkham, apriyasaṃprayogaduḥkhaṃ. 3. maraṇaṃ tu sarvaduḥkhaṃ harati. 4. kāyajīvitam idam ucyate bhaiṣajyasena sarvaduḥkham.
body.translated_text: (1) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: (2) 'Many, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, are the beings who do not hear that birth itself is suffering, that old age itself is suffering, that disease itself is suffering — the suffering of grief, the suffering of lamentation, the suffering of separation from the beloved, the suffering of encounter with the unloved. (3) But death takes away all suffering. (4) This body-life, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, is called all-suffering.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 239
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 239

body.text: 1. atha khalu te daharāḥ satvā, iman nirdeśaṃ śrutvā, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjalayaḥ praṇamaya, bhagavantam etad avocan: asmākam api bhagavan martavyam? 2. bhagavān āha: yuṣmābhir api kulaputrāḥ, sarvasatvaiś ca martavyam iti. 3. ta āhuḥ: kathaṃ bhagavan maraṇakālam ākramati? 4. bhagavān āha: maraṇakāle kulaputrāś carimavijñāne vijñānanirodho nāma vātaḥ, vijñānavibhramo nāma vātaḥ, vijñānasaṃkṣobhasaṃyukto nāma vātaḥ; 5. ime trayaḥ kulaputrā vātā maraṇakālasamaye carimavijñāne saṃluḍanti, saṃkṣubhanti, saṃkṣobham utpādayanti. 6. ta āhuḥ: katamāni bhagavaṃs trīṇi maraṇakālasamaye vijñānanirodhe vartamāne śarīraṃ nirghātayanti? 7. bhagavān āha: śastrakaś ca nāma mārṣāḥ, sūcakaś ca nāma mārṣāḥ, ṣṭhīlakaś ca nāma ye śarīraṃ nirghātayaṃti. 8. āhuḥ: kim etad bhagavaṃ ccharīraṇ nāma? 9. bhagavān āha: ādīptakaś ca nāma mārṣā, 10. dahanavāsakaś ca nāma, 11. meḍikaś ca nāma, 12. śṛṃgārikaś ca nāma, 13. śmaśānikaś ca nāma, 14. durbuddhikaś ca nāma, 15. bhāragurukaś ca nāma, 16. jātiparipīḍitaś ca nāma, 17. jātisaṃkṣubhitaś ca nāma, 18. jīvitaparibhāvikaś ca nāma, 19. maraṇapriyaviprayogakaś ca nāma; 20. ime mārṣā ucyante śarīranāmānaḥ.
body.translated_text: (1) Then those young beings, having heard this teaching, extending their palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> and bowing, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Must we too die, O <s>Bhagavān</s>?' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You too, O sons of good family, and all beings must die.' (3) They said: 'How, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does the time of death approach?' (4) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'At the time of death, O sons of good family, in the final consciousness, there is a wind called "consciousness-cessation" (<s>vijñāna-nirodha</s>), a wind called "consciousness-confusion" (<s>vijñāna-vibhrama</s>), and a wind called "consciousness-agitation" (<s>vijñāna-saṃkṣobha</s>). (5) These three winds, O sons of good family, at the time of death, in the final consciousness, churn and agitate, and produce disturbance. (6) They said: 'Which three, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, strike the body when the cessation of consciousness occurs at the time of death?' (7) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The one called "the cutter" (<s>śastraka</s>), venerables; the one called "the piercer" (<s>sūcaka</s>), venerables; and the one called "the crusher" (<s>ṣṭhīlaka</s>) — these strike the body. (8) They said: 'What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is this thing called body?' (9) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It is called "the blazing" (<s>ādīptaka</s>), venerables; (10) "the burning dwelling" (<s>dahanavāsaka</s>); (11) "the filthy" (<s>meḍika</s>); (12) "the adorned" (<s>śṛṃgārika</s>); (13) "the charnel ground" (<s>śmaśānika</s>); (14) "the evil-minded" (<s>durbuddhika</s>); (15) "the heavy burden" (<s>bhāraguruka</s>); (16) "the one afflicted by birth" (<s>jātiparipīḍita</s>); (17) "the one disturbed by birth" (<s>jātisaṃkṣubhita</s>); (18) "the one despising life" (<s>jīvitaparibhāvika</s>); (19) "the one [causing] separation from the beloved through death" (<s>maraṇapriyaviprayogaka</s>). (20) These, venerables, are called the names of the body.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 240
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 240

body.text: 1. ta āhuḥ: kathaṃ bhagavan mṛyate, kathaṃ jīvati? 2. bhagavān āha: vijñānaṃ nāmāyuṣmanto mriyate, puṇyaṃ nāmāyuṣmanto jīvati! 3. śarīraṃ nāma mārṣā mṛyate, snāyukoṭībhir baddham, 4. caturaśītibhiḥ sirākūrcasahasrai romakūpair baddham, 5. dvādaśabhiḥ sahasrair aṃgānāṃ baddhaṃ, 6. ṣaṣṭyuttarais tribhiḥ śatair asthīnāṃ baddham. 7. caturaśītiḥ kṛmikulaśatāny abhyantare vasanti; 8. teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇakānāṃ maraṇaṃ saṃvidyate, maraṇanirodhaṃ ca saṃvidyate; 9. tatra sarve te prāṇakā nirāśā bhavanti. 10. yadā sa puruṣo mṛyate, tadā sarvaprāṇakānāṃ vātasaṃkṣobhaḥ saṃluḍati anyonyaparibhākṣanārthāya, 11. tadā te duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti. 12. anye punaḥ putraśokaṃ kurvanti, anye duhitṛśokaṃ, jñātiśokaṃ; sarve eva te śokaśalyaviddhāḥ anyonyabhakṣaṇam ārabhante; 13. sarve te anupūrveṇa parasparaṃ bhakṣayanta. 14. dvau prāṇakāv avatiṣṭhante. tau saptāham abhiyudhyataḥ. yāvat saptāhe 'tikrānte tata ekaḥ prāṇako nirmathyate, eko mucyate. 15. tat katama āyuṣmanta ucyate dharmaḥ? 16. tat kiṃ manyadhve? yathā sarvaprāṇakānām anyonyavirodhena maraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: (1) They said: 'How, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does one die, and how does one live?' (2) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) dies, O long-lived ones; merit (<s>puṇya</s>) lives, O long-lived ones!' (3) 'The body, venerables, dies — bound by millions of sinews, (4) bound by eighty-four thousand bundles of veins and hair-pores, (5) bound by twelve thousand limbs, (6) bound by three hundred and sixty bones. (7) Eighty-four hundred families of worms dwell within it. (8) For all those living creatures, death exists, and cessation of death exists. (9) There, all those creatures become despairing. (10) When that person dies, then the agitation of wind among all the creatures churns for the purpose of devouring one another. (11) Then they feel painful sensations. (12) Some grieve for sons, some grieve for daughters, grieve for relatives; all of them, pierced by the thorn of grief, begin to devour one another. (13) All of them gradually devour one another in succession. (14) Two creatures remain. Those two fight for seven days. After the seven days have passed, one creature is destroyed, and one is freed. (15) Which, O long-lived ones, is called <s>Dharma</s>? (16) What do you think? Thus is the death of all creatures through mutual conflict.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 241
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 241

body.text: 1. evam eva bālapṛthagjanā satvā anyonyavirodham āpadyante: 2. te jātyā na bibhyanti, vyādhibhyo na bibhyanti, maraṇān na bibhyanti. 3. yathā tau dvau prāṇakau yudhyataḥ, evam eva bālapṛthagjanāḥ parasparaṃ yudhyante. 4. atha maraṇakālasamaye ucyate sādhupuruṣaiḥ; 5. kiṃ tvaṃ bho puruṣa viśvāsam āpadyase? kiṃ tvayā manuṣyaloke na kiṃcid ādīnavaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ? na jātyā ādīnavo dṛṣṭaḥ, na jarāyā, na vyādher ādīnavo dṛṣṭaḥ, na maraṇād ādīnavo dṛṣṭaḥ? 6. āha: dṛṣṭo me āyuṣmanto jātyā ādīnavo, jarāyā, vyādher ādīnavo dṛṣṭaḥ, sarvapaścān maraṇād ādīnavo dṛṣṭaḥ. 7. āha: kathaṃ na kṛtāni yat karaṇīyāni kuśalamūlāni? 8. tat kathaṃ tvayā bhoḥ puruṣa na kṛtam ubhayor lokayor hitasaṃvartakāni dharmaskandhakuśalamūlāni? 9. dvitīyaṃ mārṣāḥ pṛcchāmi: kathaṃ tvayā na kṛtaḥ kuśalamūlasaṃbhāraḥ yena tvaṃ parimuktaḥ syā jātyā maraṇāt? 10. tat kathaṃ te na kṛtaṃ yoniśomanasikārapratyavekṣaṇam? 11. kiṃ tvayā bhoḥ puruṣa śrutaṃ pṛthivyāṃ gaṇḍyākoṭanaśabdaṃ? 12. na ca dṛṣṭā jāṃbudvīpakā manuṣyā dānāni dadantaḥ, puṇyāni ca kurvantaḥ upavāsam upavasantaḥ, tathāgatakṣetre kuśalamūlabījāny avaropayantaḥ? 13. gandhaṃ vā, mālyaṃ vā, dīpaṃ va, na tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ vā dīyamānam? 14. na ca te dṛṣṭās tathāgatasya catasraḥ parṣadaḥ santarpyamānāḥ? 15. bhikṣur vā, bhikṣuṇī vā, upāsako vā, upāsikā vā, imāś catasraḥ parṣadaḥ śāsane 'bhinivustāḥ, evaṃ tasya hitāni vadanty, ālapanti ca. 16. na hi devakṛtaṃ kiṃcit, asādhu tvayā bhoḥ puruṣa kṛtam imaṃ jaṃbudvīpam āgatya.
body.translated_text: 1. 'Just so, foolish ordinary beings fall into mutual conflict: 2. they do not fear birth, they do not fear diseases, they do not fear death. 3. Just as those two creatures fight, so too foolish ordinary beings fight with one another. 4. Then, at the time of death, virtuous persons say to him: 5. "Why do you, O man, place your trust? Have you not seen any danger in the human world? Have you not seen the danger of birth, of old age, the danger of disease, the danger of death?" 6. He says: "I have seen, O venerable ones, the danger of birth, of old age; the danger of disease I have seen; and finally, the danger of death I have seen." 7. They say: "Why then were the wholesome roots that should have been cultivated not cultivated?" 8. "Why then, O man, have you not cultivated the roots of wholesome merit that bring about benefit in both worlds?" 9. "A second time, sirs, we ask: why have you not accumulated a store of wholesome roots by which you might be freed from birth and death?" 10. "Why then have you not practiced wise attention and investigation?" 11. "Have you, O man, heard the sound of the <s>gaṇḍī</s> (gong) being struck upon the earth?" 12. "Have you not seen the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> giving gifts, performing merit, observing fasting days, and planting seeds of wholesome roots in the field of the <s>Tathāgata</s>?" 13. "Have you not seen perfume, or garlands, or lamps being offered, or food and drink being given?" 14. "Have you not seen the four assemblies of the <s>Tathāgata</s> being satisfied?" 15. "Whether <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun), <s>upāsaka</s> (layman), or <s>upāsikā</s> (laywoman) — these four assemblies, devoted to the teaching, speak thus for his benefit and address him." 16. "Nothing is done by the gods — it is you, O man, who have done wrong, having come to this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>."'

children.text: SaSū(C) 242
children.translated_text: SaSū(C) 242

children.text: 1. tasya mṛtasya dharmarājā, tasmin kāle taṃ puruṣam anuśāsan, tā gāthā bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: 1. 'To that dead man, <s>Dharmarāja</s> (the King of Dharma), at that time instructing that person, spoke these verses:'

children.text: (1) dṛṣṭvā tathāgatotpādaṃ śrutvā gaṇḍīparāhatām /
children.translated_text: (1) 'Having seen the arising of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, having heard the <s>gaṇḍī</s> (gong) being struck,

children.text: śrutvā dharman deśayamānaṃ śantaṃ nirvāṇagāminaṃ //
children.translated_text: having heard the peaceful <s>Dharma</s> being taught, leading to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> —

children.text: (2) kasmāt te na kṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ paralokasukhāvaham /
children.translated_text: (2) why did you not perform merit that brings happiness in the next world?

children.text: bhokṣyase narake duḥkham aniṣṭakarmaṇaḥ phalam //
children.translated_text: You shall experience suffering in hell, the fruit of unwholesome <s>karma</s>.'

children.text: SaSū(C) 243
children.translated_text: SaSū(C) 243

children.text: 1. atha sa puruṣas taṃ dharmarājānaṃ gāthābhir pratyabhāṣata:
children.translated_text: 1. 'Then that man replied to <s>Dharmarāja</s> in verses:'

children.text: (1) bālabuddhir aham āsaṃ pāpamitravaśānugaḥ /
children.translated_text: (1) 'I was of foolish understanding, following evil companions;

children.text: kṛtaṃ me pāpakaṃ karma kāmabhrāntena cetasā //
children.translated_text: I committed sinful <s>karma</s> with a mind deluded by desires.

children.text: (2) kāmaś ca me citas tasya āgataṃ dāruṇaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: (2) Those desires of mine — their terrible fruit has now arrived;

children.text: kṛtā me prāṇināṃ hiṃsā sāṃghikaṃ ca vināśitaṃ //
children.translated_text: I caused harm to living beings and destroyed what belonged to the <s>Saṅgha</s>.

children.text: (3) kṛtaṃ me stūpabhedaṃ ca praduṣṭena ca cetasā /
children.translated_text: (3) I committed the breaking of <s>stūpas</s>, with a corrupt mind;

children.text: dauṣṭhulyaṃ bhāṣitaṃ vākyaṃ mātā me paritāpitā //
children.translated_text: I spoke wicked words and tormented my mother.

children.text: (4) aparādhaṃ vijānāmi svaśarīreṇa yat kṛtaṃ /
children.translated_text: (4) I recognize the offenses committed by my own body;

children.text: raurave narake paśyāmy upapattiṃ sudāruṇe //
children.translated_text: I see my rebirth in the terrible <s>Raurava</s> hell.

children.text: (5) saṃghāte vedanāṃ vetsye tathaiva ca pratāpane /
children.translated_text: (5) In <s>Saṃghāta</s> hell I shall experience suffering, and likewise in <s>Pratāpana</s>;

children.text: mahāvīcau ca kaṭukām anubhaviṣyāmi vedanāṃ //
children.translated_text: and in <s>Mahāvīci</s> (Avīci) I shall undergo bitter agony.

children.text: (6) mahāpadme ca narake krandayiṣyāmi suduḥkhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: (6) In the <s>Mahāpadma</s> hell I shall cry out in great suffering;

children.text: vārā śataṃ kālasūtre utpatsyāmi mahābhaye //
children.translated_text: a hundred times I shall be reborn in the terrifying <s>Kālasūtra</s> hell.

children.text: (7) hatāś ca nārakā satvāḥ punaḥ paśyanti te bhayam /
children.translated_text: (7) The slain hell-beings, again they see that terror;

children.text: yojanānāṃ śataṃ bhūyaḥ prapadyanti mahābhayam //
children.translated_text: for hundreds of <s>yojanas</s> further they enter into great fear.

children.text: (8) dvāran te na labhiṣyanti punaḥ kuṃbhe prapāpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: (8) They shall find no door of escape, cast again into the cauldron;

children.text: kṣūraṃ tu nāma narakaṃ sahasraṃ kṣūrasaṃbhavam //
children.translated_text: the hell called <s>Kṣūra</s> (Razor) — a thousand razors arise therein.

children.text: (9) śatam sahasraṃ koṭīnāṃ kṣūrāṇāṃ jāyate 'grataḥ /
children.translated_text: (9) Hundreds, thousands, and <s>koṭis</s> of razors arise before him;

children.text: tais tasya bhidyate gātraṃ karmabhi duṣkṛtaiḥ svakaiḥ //
children.translated_text: by them his limbs are cut to pieces through his own evil deeds.

children.text: (10) vātakṣobhā mahāghorā sarvaṃ chindanti tāṃ tanum /
children.translated_text: (10) Terrible wind-storms cut apart his entire body;

children.text: anubhāvyā mayā duḥkhā īdṛśā narake dhruvam //
children.translated_text: such sufferings must assuredly be endured by me in hell.

children.text: (11) drakṣyante sarvasatvā me kāyaṃ duḥkhaprapīḍitaṃ /
children.translated_text: (11) All beings shall see my body afflicted with suffering;

children.text: arthā parakyā ādattā mayā veśmasya kāraṇāt //
children.translated_text: I took the wealth of others for the sake of building a house.

children.text: (12) putrā duhitaro mahyaṃ bhrātā ca bhaginī tathā /
children.translated_text: (12) My sons and daughters, my brothers and sisters,

children.text: mātā pitā caiva mama mitrajñātigaṇo 'pi ca //
children.translated_text: my mother and father, and my circle of friends and relatives —

children.text: (13) dāsakarmakarāś caiva gāvo bhṛtyaḥ paśuṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: (13) my servants and workers, cows, dependents, and livestock too —

children.text: bhrānto 'smy ahaṃ kukāryeṣu rupyasauvarṇabhājanaiḥ //
children.translated_text: I was deluded in evil deeds by vessels of silver and gold.

children.text: (14) vastrais tathā susūkṣmaiś ca bhrāntaḥ kārāpane gṛhe /
children.translated_text: (14) And by very fine garments, deluded in having a house built;

children.text: suvicitraṃ gṛhaṃ kṛtvā naranārīsamākulaṃ //
children.translated_text: having made a splendid house filled with men and women,

children.text: (15) vīṇās tūryāḥ parāhatya rataṃ me durdamaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: (15) having <s>vīṇās</s> and musical instruments played — my mind delighted, hard to tame;

children.text: gātraṃ gandhodakair liptaṃ kṛtajño 'dyāpi naiva saḥ //
children.translated_text: my body anointed with perfumed waters — yet even now he is not grateful.

children.text: (16) acetanaśarīras tvaṃ bhrānto 'smi tava kāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: (16) You are a senseless body — I was deluded for your sake;

children.text: na vidyate mama trātā kaścit satvaḥ punar bhavet //
children.translated_text: there is no savior for me — what being could there be again?

children.text: (17) vātakṣobhe mahāghore śarīraparitāpane /
children.translated_text: (17) In the terrible wind-storm, tormenting the body,

children.text: bhuktā rasā svāduvanto jihvayā vividhās tathā //
children.translated_text: various delicious flavors were enjoyed by the tongue.

children.text: (18) śīrṣe mālāś ca bahavo baddhā śvitrāḥ suśobhanāḥ /
children.translated_text: (18) Many garlands were bound upon the head, beautiful and white;

children.text: rūpeṇa bhrāmitaś cakṣuś cakṣutrāṇaṃ na vidyate //
children.translated_text: the eye was deluded by beautiful form — there is no protection for the eye.

children.text: (19) pāpānāṃ cakṣuṣī hetur mayā dṛṣṭvā tu yat kṛtam /
children.translated_text: (19) The eyes are the cause of sins — because of what I saw, I acted thus;

children.text: śrotrau hetuś ca me bhūyaḥ bāhū vajraparāhatau //
children.translated_text: the ears too are a further cause — my arms were struck as if by a thunderbolt.

children.text: (20) hastebhyaḥ kaṭakā baddhā aṅgulīyebhi yaṃtrikā /
children.translated_text: (20) Bracelets were bound upon my hands, rings upon my fingers,

children.text: grīvāyāṃ muktihārāṇi pādau cāpi svalaṃkṛtau //
children.translated_text: pearl necklaces upon my neck, and my feet too were well adorned.

children.text: (21) jālāni kṛtvā tatraiva sauvaraṇaṃ saṃsthitaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: (21) Having made nets of gold arrayed right there,

children.text: gātrai ca vividhā ratnā sauvarṇakaṭakās tathā //
children.translated_text: upon the limbs were various jewels and golden bracelets.

children.text: (22) udārai ramito bhogair manasaṃbṛhaṇair api /
children.translated_text: (22) Delighted by excellent pleasures, by things that nourish the mind,

children.text: sparśaṃ ca sukumāraṃ me tṛṣṇagrastena sevitaṃ //
children.translated_text: soft touch was enjoyed by me, seized by craving.

children.text: (23) nānāstaraṇaśayyābhiḥ kāyaḥ krīḍāpito mayā /
children.translated_text: (23) Upon various beds and couches my body was made to sport;

children.text: snāto gandhodakair viśadair gandhaiś cāpi pralepitaḥ //
children.translated_text: bathed with clear perfumed waters and anointed with fragrances,

children.text: (24) karpūracandanair divyair dhūpanaiś cāpi dhūpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: (24) perfumed with divine camphor and sandalwood incense,

children.text: kastūrikāsamāyukto vāso varṇakaraḥ kṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: combined with musk, garments were made to enhance beauty.

children.text: (25) gandhavārṣikatailena sumanācaṃpakādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: (25) With fragrant seasonal oils, jasmine, champaka, and the like,

children.text: mrakṣitaḥ pāṇḍuraṃ vastraṃ prāvṛtaṃ sūkṣmakāśikam //
children.translated_text: I was anointed; a white garment of fine <s>Kāśika</s> cloth was worn.

children.text: (26) avatīrya hastipṛṣṭhād aśvapṛṣṭhe 'bhiruhya ca /
children.translated_text: (26) Descending from an elephant's back and mounting a horse's back,

children.text: rājāham iti manyāmi jano me dhāvate grataḥ //
children.translated_text: I thought "I am a king" — people ran before me.

children.text: (27) antaḥpuraṃ vijānāmi gīte nṛtye suśīkṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: (27) I know the inner palace; I was well-trained in song and dance;

children.text: nirāparādhā mṛgayā hatāḥ kāṇḍaiś ca me mṛgāḥ //
children.translated_text: innocent deer on the hunt were killed by my arrows.

children.text: (28) īdṛśaṃ me kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ paralokam ajānatā /
children.translated_text: (28) Such sin was committed by me, not knowing the next world;

children.text: paramāṃsā mayā bhuktās tato duḥkham idaṃ mama //
children.translated_text: I ate the choicest meats — hence this suffering of mine.

children.text: (29) maraṇaṃ me na vijñātam āgamiṣyati dāruṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: (29) I did not realize that terrible death would come;

children.text: bālabuddhir aham āsaṃ śarīraṃ poṣitaṃ mayā //
children.translated_text: I was of foolish understanding — my body was nourished by me.

children.text: (30) āgataṃ maraṇaṃ me 'dya kaścit trātā na vidyate /
children.translated_text: (30) Death has come to me today — no savior is to be found;

children.text: yūyaṃ hi jñātayaḥ sarve mukhaṃ me kiṃ nirīkṣatha //
children.translated_text: you who are all my relatives — why do you merely gaze at my face?

children.text: (31) kasmād vastraṃ pāṭayadhvaṃ pralāpaiś cāpi kiṃkṛte /
children.translated_text: (31) Why do you tear your garments? What is the use of lamentations?

children.text: keśān kasmād vikiratha raktaṃ kiṃ vā kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: Why do you scatter your hair? What will blood accomplish?

children.text: (32) pāṃsuṃ ca śīrṣe kṣipatha urastāḍaṃ karotha kim /
children.translated_text: (32) Why do you throw dust upon your heads? What is the use of beating your chests?

children.text: jīvaṃ nāhaṃ vāritavyaḥ pāpāt kiṃ ruditena vaḥ //
children.translated_text: While I am still alive I should not be held back from sin — what use is your weeping?

children.text: (33) śarīraṃ me vṛkabhojyaṃ kukkurāṇāṃ ca vāyasām /
children.translated_text: (33) My body shall become food for wolves, dogs, and crows;

children.text: bhaviṣyate pakṣiṇāṃ ca vṛthāpuṣṭo mayā tanuḥ //
children.translated_text: it shall become food for birds — in vain was this body nourished by me.

children.text: (34) maraṇoragasaṃspṛṣṭo jāyate 'pi sudāruṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: (34) Touched by the serpent of death, one is born in terrible states;

children.text: tathopayojyaṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ yathāsmān mucyate bhayāt //
children.translated_text: the medicine must be applied by which one is freed from this fear.

children.text: (35) yan me vaidyāḥ pradāsyanti bhaiṣajyaṃ na tad iṣyate /
children.translated_text: (35) The medicine that physicians will give me — that is not what is needed;

children.text: sāṃprataṃ dharmabhaiṣajyaṃ kleśoragavimocakam //
children.translated_text: now give me the medicine of <s>Dharma</s>, which liberates from the serpent of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).

children.text: (36) mṛyato mama dātavyaṃ māmemaṃ saṃprayacchatha /
children.translated_text: (36) As I am dying, it should be given to me — grant me this!

children.text: puṣyamāṇaśarīro 'yam avaśyaṃ nāśam eṣyati //
children.translated_text: This body that was nourished will inevitably come to destruction.

children.text: (37) pāpaskandhaṃ kim ākṣipya yat paścā duḥkhadāyakam /
children.translated_text: (37) Why take up this mass of sin that afterward brings suffering?

children.text: poṣito me pṛyaṃ kāyaḥ kṛtaghnatvaṃ kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: This beloved body that was nourished by me will act with ingratitude.

children.text: (38) putrā duhitaraṃ kiṃ me cakṣuṣā sannirīkṣatha /
children.translated_text: (38) Why, O my sons and daughters, do you gaze at me with your eyes?

children.text: trāyadhvam asmād rogān me rudadhvaṃ kin nirarthakam //
children.translated_text: Save me from this disease! What is the point of weeping uselessly?

children.text: (39) yūyaṃ hi putra duhitaḥ kṛtaghnā mama sāmpratam /
children.translated_text: (39) You, my sons and daughters, are now ungrateful to me;

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ poṣaṇārthāya parakīyaṃ mayā hṛtaṃ //
children.translated_text: for the sake of nourishing you, I took what belonged to others.

children.text: (40) sāṃprataṃ maraṇaṃ prāptaṃ nirāśaṃ māṃ karotha kim /
children.translated_text: (40) Now death has arrived — why do you make me hopeless?

children.text: jātidurgatisaṃtrasto maraṇena ca pīḍitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Terrified by the evil destinies of rebirth and afflicted by death,

children.text: (41) vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ sparśaṃ paramavedanāḥ /
children.translated_text: (41) feelings, perceptions, mental formations, contact, and supreme sensations —

children.text: tṛṣṇāyā bhrāmyate bālaḥ prāpnoti kaṭukaṃ phalaṃ //
children.translated_text: by craving the fool wanders and reaps bitter fruit.

children.text: (42) śokabandhanaṃ mahyaṃ tu jātasya viṣame kule /
children.translated_text: (42) The bondage of grief is mine, born in a wretched family;

children.text: alpapuṇyaṃ tu māṃ jñātvā śociṣyanty apare janāḥ //
children.translated_text: Other people, knowing me to be of little merit, will grieve for me.

children.text: (43) dānaśīlaparibhraṣṭo dharmāc cāpi parāṅmukhaḥ /
children.translated_text: (43) Fallen from generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and morality (<s>śīla</s>), and turned away from the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: punarbhavaṃ na jānīte kleśoragaviṣārditaḥ //
children.translated_text: afflicted by the poison of the serpent of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>), he does not know rebirth.

children.text: (44) bhrāmyate 'vidyayā bālo yatra mokṣaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: (44) The fool wanders through ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) where liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) does not exist;

children.text: mokṣārthaṃ na vijānāti bhrāntaḥ pāpaṃ karoti ca //
children.translated_text: he does not understand the purpose of liberation, and, deluded, commits sin.

children.text: (45) kleśaiś ca bhrāmyate bālo nityaṃ vyākṣiptamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: (45) The fool is made to wander by defilements (<s>kleśa</s>), his mind constantly distracted;

children.text: dahyate hy agninā dīptaḥ kāyo vividhabandhanaḥ //
children.translated_text: blazing, the body is burned by fire, bound by manifold bonds.

children.text: (46) vibhrānto bhramate kāyo yatra saukhyaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: (46) Bewildered, the body wanders where happiness does not exist;

children.text: tac ca saukhyaṃ na jānāti yad abhyantasukhāvaham //
children.translated_text: and he does not know that happiness which brings inner bliss.

children.text: (47) buddhānāṃ sukhadaṃ kṣetraṃ dharmacakraṃ mahāgadam /
children.translated_text: (47) The happiness-giving field of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Dharma) — the great remedy,

children.text: śīlaṃ ca satyaṃ śīlanāṃ brahmaghoṣās tathāgatā //
children.translated_text: morality (<s>śīla</s>) and truth of the virtuous, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of divine voice —

children.text: SaSū(C) 244
children.translated_text: SaSū(C) 244

children.text: 1. atha khalu bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisatvaṃ mahāsatvam āmantreyad avocat: evaṃ ca bhaiṣajyasena satvā maraṇakāle paridevanti; na na hi teṣāṃ kaścit trātā bhaviṣyaty anyatra sukṛtānāṃ karmāṇāṃ phalavipākaṃ. gāthāś cemā bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> and said: 'Thus, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, beings lament at the time of death; for indeed no one will be their savior except the fruit-ripening of well-performed <s>karmas</s>.' And he spoke these verses:

children.text: (1) kṛtvā tu pāpakaṃ karma narakeṣu patanti hi /
children.translated_text: (1) Having committed sinful <s>karma</s>, they fall into the hells;

children.text: bhuṃjante cīmaraṃ taptaṃ pīvante lohapānakam //
children.translated_text: they eat burning chaff and drink molten iron.

children.text: (2) kāyebhyo varṣate 'ṅgāraṃ dagdhāḥ krandanti dāruṇam /
children.translated_text: (2) From their bodies rain down glowing coals; burned, they cry out terribly;

children.text: dahyaty eṣāṃ tac charīraṃ narakesmin mahābhaye //
children.translated_text: their bodies burn in this hell of great fear.

children.text: (3) na vijānanti saukhyāni dharmaṃ ca na vijānate /
children.translated_text: (3) They do not know happiness, nor do they understand the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: bālo bhramaty adharmeṇa saukhyaṃ nāpnoti kiṃcana //
children.translated_text: the fool wanders through unrighteousness (<s>adharma</s>) and obtains no happiness whatsoever.

children.text: (4) śraddhāśīlena saṃpannaḥ prajñāyukto mahātapāḥ /
children.translated_text: (4) Endowed with faith and morality (<s>śīla</s>), joined with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), of great austerity,

children.text: mitraṃ bhajati kalyāṇaṃ śīghraṃ bhoti tathāgataḥ //
children.translated_text: he resorts to a good spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) and swiftly becomes a <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: (5) vīryam ārabhate śreyaṃ buddhalokopapattaye /
children.translated_text: (5) He undertakes effort (<s>vīrya</s>) for the good, for rebirth in a <s>Buddha</s>-world;

children.text: deśetha kuśalaṃ dharmaṃ sarvasatvaparigrahaṃ //
children.translated_text: he would teach the wholesome <s>Dharma</s> that embraces all beings.

children.text: (6) maitraṃ cittaṃ samāpanno brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: (6) Having attained a mind of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), devoted to the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>),

children.text: śrutvaivaṃ bhaiṣajyasena pratipattiparo bhavet //
children.translated_text: having heard thus, O <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, one should be devoted to practice.

children.text: (7) vimuktidarśanaṃ buddhaṃ ghuṣṭaśabdaṃ vināyakaṃ /
children.translated_text: (7) The <s>Buddha</s> — the vision of liberation (<s>vimukti</s>), whose fame resounds, the Guide (<s>Vināyaka</s>),

children.text: lokasya mātāpitaraṃ bodhicittaṃ tad ucyate //
children.translated_text: the mother and father of the world — that is called the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>).

children.text: (8) kalyāṇamitrāṃ paramaṃ suduṣkaraṃ yo deśayet /
children.translated_text: (8) The supreme good spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), most difficult to find, who would teach

children.text: dharmaṃ loke śṛṇvanti ye gauravād buddhaśāsanaṃ /
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharma</s> — those in the world who hear the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching with reverence,

children.text: te bhonti buddhāḥ sugatā narottamāḥ //
children.translated_text: they become <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Sugatas</s>, the best of men.

children.text: (9) lokanāthā bhavanty ete sarvasatvapramocakāḥ /
children.translated_text: (9) They become Protectors of the World, liberators of all beings;

children.text: śāntebhyo buddhakṣetrebhyo ye bhavanti sagauravāḥ //
children.translated_text: those who are reverent toward the peaceful <s>Buddha</s>-fields.

body.text: SaSū(C) 245
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 245

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: kimidaṃ bhagavan? pṛthivī kaṃpati saṃprakaṃpati! 2. evam ukte bhagavān bhaiṣajyasenaṃ bodhisatvaṃ mahāsatvam etad avocat: vyavalokaya bhaiṣajyasena! kiṃ paśyasi? 3. vyavalokitaṃ bhaiṣajyasenena bodhisatvena mahāsatvena. 4. atha tāvad eva caturbhyo digbhyaḥ paśyati: pṛthivī vivaraṃ dadāti. pṛthivyāṃ vivṛtāyāṃ, paśyati: 5. pṛthivīvivarebhyo viṃśati koṭyo manuṣyāṇāṃ jāyante; 6. adhastāddiśi viṃśati koṭyo manuṣyāṇāṃ jāyante; 7. ūrdhvāyāṃ diśāyāṃ paṃcaviṃśati koṭyo manuṣyānāṃ jāyante.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What is this, O <s>Bhagavān</s>? The earth trembles and quakes!' 2. When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>: 'Look, <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>! What do you see?' 3. The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s> looked. 4. Then at once he saw from the four directions: the earth opened up. When the earth had opened, he saw: 5. from the crevasses of the earth, twenty <s>koṭis</s> of humans were born; 6. in the downward direction, twenty <s>koṭis</s> of humans were born; 7. in the upward direction, twenty-five <s>koṭis</s> of humans were born.

body.text: SaSū(C) 246
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 246

body.text: atha te daharāḥ satvā vyavalokya bhagavantam etad avocan: katame bhagavann iha jātāḥ? 2. bhagavān āha: paśyatha yūyam? ime janakāyāḥ! 3. ta āhuḥ: paśyāmo bhagavan. 3. bhagavān āha: ime janakāyā yuṣmākaṃ sakhāyā jātāḥ. 5. ta āhuḥ: eteṣām api bhagavan satvānāṃ maraṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? 6. bhagavān āha: evam etan mārṣāḥ, sarvasatvānām api maraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: 1. Then those young beings, looking at the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said: 'Who, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, has been born here?' 2. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do you see? These multitudes of people!' 3. They said: 'We see, O <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 4. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'These multitudes of people are born as your companions.' 5. They said: 'Will death come to these beings too, O <s>Bhagavān</s>?' 6. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Even so, dear friends — death will come to all beings.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 247
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 247

body.text: 1. atha te pūrvimakā satvā daharāḥ, ye prathamam utpannās, te, yena bhagavāṃs tenāṃjaliṃ praṇamayya, bhagavantam etad avocan: 2. notsahāmo vayaṃ punar bhagavaṃ jātiṃ, maraṇaṃ ca draṣṭum! 3. bhagavān āha: tat kiṃ yūyam utsahatha vīryabalālabdham? 4. ta āhuḥ: tathāgataṃ saṃmukhaṃ paśyema! 5. tasya ca sakāśād dharmaśravaṇaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ manāpaṃ śṛṇuyāma! 6. tathāgataśrāvakasaṃghaṃ ca niṣaṇṇaṃ paśyema! 7. bodhisatvān mahardhikān mahānubhāvān paśyema! 8. īdṛśaṃ ca bhagavan notsahāmo: jātiṃ maraṇaṃ ca draṣṭum.
body.translated_text: 1. Then those earlier beings, the young ones who were born first, joining their palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 2. 'We cannot bear, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, to see birth and death again!' 3. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Then what is it that you can bear through the strength of effort (<s>vīryabala</s>)?' 4. They said: 'May we see the <s>Tathāgata</s> face to face! 5. And may we hear from him the sweet and agreeable hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>! 6. And may we see the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples) seated! 7. May we see the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of great supernatural power and great majesty! 8. But this, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, we cannot bear: to see birth and death.'

body.text: SaSū(C) 248
body.translated_text: SaSū(C) 248

body.text: 1. atha khalu bhaiṣajyaseno bodhisatvo mahāsatva, ṛddhibalenotthāyāsanāt, sārdhaṃ taiḥ paṃcabhir bodhisatvaśataiḥ, te sarve ṛddhyā utthāya, upary antarīkṣe caṃkramanti. 2. paryaṃkañ ca baddhvā dhyāyanti. 3. teṣāṃ sarvakāyebhyaḥ siṃhā niṣkrāmanti, 4. vyāghrā niṣkrāmanti, 5. vyāḍā niṣkrāmanti, 6. hastino niṣkrāmanti. 7. mahāṛddhivikurvitāni darśayanti. 8. parvateṣu ca paryaṃkaṃ baddhvā niṣīdanti. 9. viṃśatir yojanasahasrāṇy ūrdhvam āruhanti. 10. daśa koṭīsahasrāṇi candramasūryāṇimavataranti.
body.translated_text: 1. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasena</s>, rising from his seat by the power of supernatural attainment (<s>ṛddhibala</s>), together with those five hundred <s>bodhisattvas</s> — they all rose up by supernatural power and walked in the sky above. 2. And seated cross-legged, they meditated. 3. From all their bodies, lions emerged, 4. tigers emerged, 5. serpents (<s>vyāḍa</s>) emerged, 6. elephants emerged. 7.
